## 8. The definitional rules (classification 5.6)

Statement pass 7 (§6.2) runs after every verifying rule. It first computes each posted credit's payer facts (channel family, payer region, payer name, payer key, entry fields, and the hold predicates of §8.1). Then it runs Q7's credit-union arm (§8.7), the asset-sale reading (Q11 (2026-10-02) (b), §8.1) and the Q5 and Q6 verifications (§8.5, §8.6), which refuse any row a hold of §8.1 names or the asset-sale reading reads. Last, it gives every remaining `unverified_deposit` its tier and reason, in the order of §8.10.

### 8.1 Holds that apply to any channel

Every hold below skips a row that the registry, a payout entity or a factoring payee claimed (§8.9), except `insurer_payer`, `possible_return` and the pay and benefit holds, which read wording no platform prints on its own payouts. Audit round 3, R3-B14 (R3-06, §20; Q8 of 2026-10-02, "Their consumer-side credits (refunds, loans to the holder) stay as today", and the MCA principle): a payout entity or a lease-to-own or patient financier never claims a credit whose row, read without the receiver field's value and without the holder's names (the I47 strip's), prints a non-sale or financing word (`_payout_non_sale`: `ADVANCE(S)`, `ADVNC`, `ADVN`, `ADVC`, `CASH ADV…`, `CAPITAL`, `CAPTL`, `INTEREST`, `DIVIDEND(S)`, `REBATE(S)`; never `FUNDING`, `FUNDED`, `PAYOUT`, `PAYMENT`, `LEASE FUND`, `PROCEEDS` or a bare `ADV`, a payment advice), so a holder named `… CAPITAL …` never vetoes (in a labelled receiver field or printed with no label; the classifier's Cherry veto, §6.3's OQ2 note, reads the same text since R3-B14 review round 1, finding 1, §20): the holds read such a row as the same row from any other payer (an advance, a cash advance or capital held `financing_named_payer`; interest, a dividend or a rebate held `non_sale_purpose`, or `financing_named_payer` where the financier's own name prints a root, `SNAP FINANCE`, `TERRACE FINANCE`). A classifier descriptor that verified such a row keeps its verification, as before Q8. Q5 and Q6 never verify such a row and never count it toward a repeat (`_payout_claim_vetoed`, read by `_never_q5_or_q6`), so where no hold reads its word (an abbreviated advance, `ADVNC`, `ADVN`, `ADVC`) a payout entity's credit is counted as `payout_credit_entity`, as before the batch, and a financier's as a named payer, never Verified on its company form. A financier's such credit that the rules count is still read by §8.9's lump-sum test as that financier's payout (`_vetoed_financier`, the financier read without the veto; R3-B14 review round 1, finding 2, §20), so a large one-off abbreviated advance stays held as `customer_financing_lump_sum`, as before the batch. The **posting labels** removed before a hold reads a row are §7.5's credit posting labels, plus `INSTANT CREDIT`, `REAL TIME CREDIT`, `COUNTER CREDIT`, `POS CREDIT`, `ATM CREDIT`, `TELLER CREDIT`, `BRANCH CREDIT`, `CARD CREDIT`, `BATCH CREDIT`, `MERCHANT CREDIT` and `CREDIT FROM`, and the channel phrases `FUNDS TRANSFER`, `FUNDS AVAILABLE` and `INSTANT FUNDS`.

- **`insurer_payer`:** a row whose revenue method is `insurer_customer_payment` (§6.1 step 5, T14). The customer-payment wording, read on a credit from a listed insurer, is `\b(?:DRP|VENDOR ?(?:PMT|PAY|PAYMENT)|COMM?ISS?IONS?|AGT ?COMM|AGENT COMP|AGTEFT|REPAIR)\b`. Since the underwriter's Q2 (2026-10-02, R2-OW08) only a customer-payment row the for-work release refuses reaches it (premium- or refund-coded, under $1, a direction conflict, claimed); the rest pay for the business's work (below).
- **`insurer_named_payer`** (new): the payer region prints `\bINSUR\w*`, `\bASSURANCE\b`, `\bMUTUAL\b`, `\bCASUALTY\b`, `\bINDEMNITY\b` or `\bUNDERWRIT\w*`, or `\bCLAIMS?\b` on a row that is neither an `HCCLAIMPMT` entry nor from a healthcare payer. It closes Q6's "insurers never count" for carriers no registry lists (`FABRIKAM MUTUAL INSURANCE COMPANY DES:CLAIM PAYMT`). Measured on the memo's rows: $1.06M, 527 rows, 61 statements.
  Audit I26 (by Q6 of 2026-09-28, "insurers never count", and the last sentence of the underwriter's Q2 (2026-10-02) option the owner picked, "a one-off claim paid to a business on its own policy stays out"; the Q2 question did not ask it; §19.1, §20, R2-OW07): the reading (`insurer_payer_reading`) covers every insurer spelling, read on the payer region without the holder's own names (each of the holder's names by its runs, then R2-B04's other business names of the holder and the statement's receiver-field holder names, whole), so the holder's own `INSURANCE` word never makes its payer an insurer. Beside the spelled-out words above it reads the `INS` abbreviation; the cut forms `ASSUR`, `MUTUA`, `CASUALT…` and `INDEMN…`; `ASSURANCES`, `ASSURANT` and `ASSUREUR(S)`; `P AND C` (or `P & C`) at a name's end or before `INS…`, `CO`, `COMPANY` or `CORP`; `LOSS PMT`, `LOSS PAYMENT`, `LOSS PYMT` and `LOSS DRAFT`; `SUBRO…` (`SUBRO` and its cut forms `SUBROG…`, never the given name `SUBROTO`; R2-OW07 review round 1); `COUNTY MUT`, a Texas county mutual's 16-character cut (`PROG COUNTY MUT`; audit round 3, R3-B13: R3-11, §20) (`_INSURER_SPELLINGS`); and the registry's `INSURER_CREDIT_BRANDS`, carriers that print no insurer word, each bounded as a whole name (Farmers, never `FARMERS IN BLOOM` or `FARMERS EXCHANGE BANK`; American Family, never `AMERICAN FAMILY CARE` or a dental practice; Safeco; Hiscox; Aflac; Gainsco; AmTrust, never its bank, title or realty namesakes; National General, never `NATIONAL GENERAL CONTRACTORS`; Travelers' indemnity, casualty, property and commercial lines and its agents' `PI COMM`, never `TRAVELERS CASH`; American Income Life, `AM INCOME LIFE` or `AMERICAN INCOME LIFE`, never `AMERICAN INCOME FUND` or `AM INCOME LIFESTYLE`: American Income Life Insurance Company, ailife.com, a Globe Life subsidiary selling life and supplemental health insurance through its own agency force, whose agents' commission credits print that originator and no insurer word, the entry's `AIL INS` never read as the brand; audit round 3, R3-B16: R3-03, §20), credit-only: no classifier rule, debit, flag or lender reading reads the table, and no record carries it. R2-OW07 review round 1: a brand's and `P AND C`'s `INS` is the insurer word or its cut (`INS`, `INSU`, `INSUR…`), never another word's first letters (`FARMERS INSTITUTE`, `FARMERS INSTANT`, `NATIONAL GENERAL INSTRUMENTS`, `<NAME> P & C INSTALLATIONS`), and Travelers' property line reads only before an insurer word (`CAS`, `CASUALT…`, `INS`, `INSUR…`) or at the name's end, never a property manager (`TRAVELERS PROPERTY MANAGEMENT`). `ASSURED`, `ASSURE`, `P AND C FOODS`, `CLM`, `CLMS` and `CLMEFT` are never read, and `_INSURER_NAME` is unchanged. On a person-to-person rail only the spelled-out words and `CLAIM` read, as before I26 (R2-OW07 review round 1): a sender's surname or given name (`INTERAC E-TRANSFER FROM <NAME> MUTUA`, `VENMO … SUBROTO <NAME>`) or the rail's own word (`APPLE CASH INS`, instant) is no cut insurer, and a brand never reads a person's transfer. (Narrowed by audit round 3, R3-B13: R3-57, §20: a consumer rail only, Zelle, Interac and its e-Transfer and `VIREMENT` forms, Venmo, Cash App, Square Cash, Apple Cash and Popmoney (`_p2p_rail`). A push or instant rail (`RTP`, `FEDNOW`, `REAL TIME PAYMENT`, `INSTANT PAYMENT`, `VISA DIRECT`, `PMNT RCVD` …), a named transfer (`ONLINE TRANSFER FROM <NAME> INS CO`) and an ACH entry worded `TRANSFER` (`<NAME> INS CO DES:TRANSFER`, Chase's `CO ENTRY DESCR:TRANSFER`), which sit on the person-to-person channel too, read every spelling and the brands, so a one-off insurer credit there is held like one spelled `INSURANCE` (§17.1's I26 default; the standard's F1: the payer, not the rail, decides an insurer's credit); the cut `MUTUA` reads there only beside a company form on the payer region without the holder's names (`classifier.company_form`: `REAL TIME PAYMENT FROM <GIVEN NAME> MUTUA` is a surname). A push row that prints no payer region (`RTP CREDIT <NAME> INS CO`, `VISA DIRECT <brand>`) gets no reading of any spelling: §17.1's I26 item records it.) Accepted over-holds, held and reviewable (R2-OW07 review round 1; the patterns cannot tell them from an insurer): an ACH payer whose name ends in `MUTUA` (a 16-letter field's cut of `<NAME> MUTUAL` prints the same), National General's bare name (the same field cuts `NATIONAL GENERAL CONTRACTORS` to it), `P AND C` at a name's end or before `CO` or `CORP` (a company named by its initials) and the `INS` token before another word (`<NAME> HOME INS INSPECTIONS`). The first arm that reads wins: an `HCCLAIMPMT` entry is no insurer; a listed insurer's credit is read next (audit round 3, R3-B13: R3-11, §20: before the government arm, so a row the classifier's insurance rule read as a listed carrier is that carrier whatever government-shaped name it prints, `ALLSTATE COUNTY`, `STATE FARM COUNTY MUTUAL INS CO` on a wire; its arm is restated below); a government payer (§7.6) is an insurer only by the spelled-out words above or `CLAIM` (never on a healthcare payer), read without the holder's names and never for work, the reading the hold made before I26 (R2-OW07 review round 1: a government insurance programme's credit, employment, parental, disability or family-leave insurance or a public insurer's, `GOVERNMENT OF CANADA EMPLOYMENT INSURANCE`, `STATE OF <NAME> DISABILITY INSURANCE`, `DEPT OF INSURANCE`, stays held and never counts as the business's work, a personal government benefit being never revenue under the MCA principle; the widened spellings and the brands never read a government payer); a listed insurer's credit (§6.1 step 5's `insurance_provider_credit_exclusion` or T14's `insurer_customer_payment`) is the registry's entity, never this hold (a premium financier none; read before the government payer since audit round 3, R3-B13, above); a title firm is a title insurer when an insurer word or spelling prints (held here, as before; never for work); a premium-finance wording is premium financing, no insurer; a healthcare payer is an insurer only by the spelled-out words (Q6c unchanged: `AETNA LIFE INS … PREM` keeps its refusal); a §15 deferred payer (§7.7) only by those words or `CLAIM`; then a brand, keyed by its entity (a carrier `INSURANCE_PROVIDER_ALIASES` also names keeps that entity's name, `Travelers`, so one carrier is one key however it prints); then a spelled word, a spelling or `CLAIM`, keyed by the payer key. `CLAIM` is still read, never on an `HCCLAIMPMT` entry or a healthcare payer. A credit so read is held as `insurer_named_payer` exactly as the same credit spelled `INSURANCE` was, before the pay hold (`FARMERS INS DES:PAYROLL` is held here, not as `payroll_or_salary`), and a Q5 or Q6 repeat it now holds is the census's declared `q5_q6_held_insurer` (§14.2, §20). R2-OW07 review round 1: R2-OW06's precedence, an insurer-name hold other than IAA's keeping an asset sale held, reads this whole reading, so a payer the widened spellings or a brand read printing a truck, vehicle or equipment sale (`<NAME> INS CO DES:TRUCK SALE`, `SAFECO DES:VEHICLE SALE`) is held `insurer_named_payer`, not `non_revenue` `asset_sale_proceeds`, as the spelled-out insurer's already was (an insurer buying a vehicle reads as a total-loss settlement; held is reviewable) (qualified by audit round 3, R3-B13: R3-64, §20: an insurer-name hold keeps an insurer's printed asset sale held; a row the underwriter's Q2 release re-states takes no insurer-name hold and is read by Q11 (b), `non_revenue` / `asset_sale_proceeds` at a non-dealer (an agency, a clinic, a pharmacy, a repair shop whose name is no dealer evidence, or on the three-in-31-days ground), and where the holder's trade name is dealer evidence (§17.1's asset-sale follow-up (1): `AUTO…`, `COLLISION`, `BODY SHOP`) it keeps its release); and a row whose only insurer reading was the holder's own name, read away by the holder strip, is counted where no later hold of §8.10 names it (Truist's `CREF <payer> <holder's cut name> CUSTOMER ID`, the holder test not reading the holder's name in the middle of the region: a payer printing no insurer word, T21, or a glued one, `<NAME>INSURANCE`; held before I26), while a later hold that names it holds it (`holder_name` where the holder test reads the name at the region's end).
  A reading the underwriter's Q2 release counts as paid for the business's work (below) is no longer this hold's.
- **Insurers paid for the business's work (Q2 (2026-10-02); `insurer_paid_for_services`, R2-OW08).** The underwriter answered Q2, "True revenue" (option 2): an insurer's credit is counted in True, flagged, never Verified and never toward a Q5 or Q6 repeat, when it pays the business for its work. Before the payer facts (as audit fix batch B3's processor release does), pass 7 re-states such a credit (`_insurer_for_work`) as an unverified deposit of method `insurer_paid_for_services` (rule `insurer_paid_for_services`, confidence 0.60, its reason naming the ground in words, never the payer's), unclaimed: the method never joins `_REGISTRY_METHODS` or any claimed set, so the insurer-name hold passes over it and every later hold of §8.10 (4 to 11) still reads it, and where none names it the tier is `counted_flagged` / `insurer_paid_for_services`.
  - **Eligible.** The insurer reading above (`insurer_payer_reading`, on the payer region the facts read) is for work (never a title insurer's or a government payer's); no registry, payout entity, factoring payee or financier claimed the row (the insurer-name hold's convention); it is $1 or more, its direction agrees, and it is an unverified deposit or the insurance rule's `non_revenue` (`insurance_provider_credit_exclusion`), never a row a classifier rule verified (a descriptor, a remittance). A premium, refund, return, dividend, cancellation, unearned, overpayment, member or subscriber word, or a personal benefit's (`DISAB…`, `INVALIDIT…`, `ANNUIT…`, `PENSION…`; the MCA principle), on the payer (read without the holder's names) or the purpose refuses every ground, unless a commission form prints in the same words (`PREM COMM`). Medical claim payments to providers keep counting as today."; the MCA principle): the personal-benefit words read are those four stems and `_INSURER_PERSONAL_BENEFIT`, a disability benefit under another name (`STD` before a benefit, claim or payment word; a `WEEKLY` or `INCOME` benefit) and life-policy money (`DEATH…`, `SURVIVOR…`, `SURRENDER…`, `SURR`, `CASH VALUE`, `MATURITY`, `MATURED`, `BENEFICIAR…`), each refusing every ground; `LTD` before a benefit, claim or payment word, read on the purpose alone (`_INSURER_LTD_BENEFIT`: on the payer `LTD` is a carrier's legal form, so `<NAME> INSURANCE CO LTD DES:CLAIM PMT` still counts at a repair shop); and workers' compensation (`WC`, `WORKERS COMP…`, `WORK COMP`) or a plain `BENEFIT(S)` or `BNFT` wording (`_INSURER_NON_PROVIDER_BENEFIT`, read by `_non_provider_benefit` on the purpose and the payer; R3-B13 review round 1, finding 2, §20: on the payer a plain `BENEFIT(S)` or `BNFT` followed by an insurer word or spelling or a legal form is the carrier's name, never the payment, so `MUTUAL BENEFIT INS CO DES:DRP PAYMENT` still counts at a repair shop, while one printed after the name, `<NAME> MUTUAL INS BENEFIT PMT` on a layout with no entry field, and workers' compensation anywhere are read), refusing every ground only where the holder is no provider (`_holder_provider`: the holder's trade, the first `_holder_service_trade` reads with its strict and its loose words, is no clinic or pharmacy; a workers' compensation carrier paying a clinic, a therapy practice or a pharmacy pays for treatment; elsewhere it is a wage or an owner's benefit). (Amended by R3-B13 review round 1, finding 1, §20 below: the provider is the holder's first trade, the brief's reading, so a name whose first trade is a repair shop or an insurance agency is no provider whatever clinic or pharmacy word it also prints: `<NAME> HEALTH INSURANCE AGENCY LLC`, `<NAME> COLLISION DOCTORS LLC`.) A bare `LIFE` (group health and dental claims print it) and a bare `COMP` (an `INS COMP` commission) are never read. The commission override holds for each, and a refused credit is no eligible credit, so it never counts toward its key's frequency or the loose-trade count. The purpose is a wire's purpose fields (`_title_purpose_text`: OBI, RMR, PMT DET, RFB, URI; never its `REF`, which on the Fedwire layout is the sending bank: `REF COMM BANK NYC`) or the entry fields, read with R2-B12's layout entry (`_layout_entry`).

(3) `same_insurer_3_in_31_days`: one insurer key pays three or more eligible credits within an inclusive 31-day span (date[i+2] - date[i] ≤ 30 days; the span slides, so it reaches across a calendar month's edge: 03-01 to 03-31 holds, 03-01 to 04-01 does not; an undated credit counts as inside). The key is the registry's or the brand's entity, so one carrier is one key however it prints (`TRAVELERS INSURANCE` and `TRAVELERS INDEMN` pool), otherwise the payer key. (4) `insurer_service_statement`, only with the owner's switch `INSURER_FOR_WORK_STATEMENT_ARM` on (off: the literal reading, §17.1): another insurer's eligible credit on a statement where some key is frequent. A credit with no ground stays out as before: a listed insurer's stays `non_revenue`, any other is held (`insurer_payer` or `insurer_named_payer`): "a one-off claim paid to a business on its own policy stays out".
  - **What the release reads around it.** The insurer's `CLAIM` on a released row is no non-sale word (the release read it as a claim paid for the work: a body shop's, an agency's or a provider's claim payments); every other non-sale word still holds it. A released row is no insurer to B4's bill clause (`CounterCredit.insurer` False, applied on R2-B02's `CounterCredit`), so a debit naming its carrier that is no circular money does not hold it unless the debit is for its own amount or recurs at one amount without a premium or retry word (`PREM`, `PREMS`, `PREMIUM`, `PREMIUMS`, `RETRY`, read with Chase's glued SEC code split off); a premium never holds it, recurring or not (`payer_also_debited`; amended by audit round 3, R3-B16: R3-03, §20: the R2-OW08 reading, "a one-off premium bill to the same carrier at another amount does not hold it, while a debit for its own amount or a recurring one still does", reached only debits that print a bill word, so an agency's own premium to the carrier that pays its commissions held every commission). Its later holds, Q11's asset-sale reading (an IAA seller payout three times a month at a non-dealer is `non_revenue` / `asset_sale_proceeds`) and Q3's Zelle step (a Zelle credit from an insurer is `zelle_excluded`, its release kept as `zelle_prior_reading`) run as before; Q10's premium-trust hold, when it lands, holds it too. HCCLAIMPMT keeps verifying, a healthcare payer keeps Q6c, a §15 deferred payer is read only by the spelled-out words or `CLAIM` (§7.7), and the census declares the release (§6.3 narrowing 13; the demotion `insurer_paid_for_services`). A glued `FINUSA` is not a root (B6 review round 1, §20): with no left boundary it read any run-together payer name ending in `FIN` + `USA` (a muffin or griffin brand, `<NAME>FINUSA LLC`), held even as a Q6 repeat; Forward Financing's run-together `FORWARDFINUSA` is its ledger alias, read with a reference glued on (§6.1 step 6).

  **The Q9 release (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q9, "Keep them as true revenue", option 2; audit I16, I36(d); R2-OW09).** T4's root arm is lifted for three kinds of row, each counted and flagged, never Verified and never toward a Q5 or Q6 repeat (`finance_named_release`, read in the payer facts on an unverified credit nothing claimed; `CreditFacts.q9`):
  - **Read by place.** Only the root arm (`financing_named`) is lifted, read place by place (`_financing_root_places`, financing_named's own reading: the payer reading, the entry reading, or a payer-less row's reading, each where a root fires; a special payer arm, the whole-word or formed `CREDIT`, a glued `…CRED` name or a wire's wrap-split root, is marked and no longer ends the reading, so an entry root beside it is seen). Every other financing arm still holds, in its order: the registry's financing, an unadmitted listed auto lender, a dealer-funding word, a lone credit union's `VHCL PURCH`, a bank-originated wire and a lending bank. A released row takes every later hold (`payer_debited_as_lender`, `holder_name`, `payroll_or_salary`, `personal_income`, `non_sale_purpose`, `payer_also_debited`, the payroll-tax hold, the $1 floor), and the insurer and possible-return holds come before it.
  - **Never released:** a line whose row before its receiver fields (the holder's names removed) prints `PROCEEDS` or a disbursement (`DISBURS…`).
  - **(a) `finance_named_customer` and (c) `lender_paid_for_services`:** the root fires on the payer's name alone (no entry or row place) and the line prints §7.5's accounts-payable, vendor-payment or invoice wording (`_accounts_payable_wording`, the holder's names removed) or `COMMISSION(S)` (the orchestrator's extension under the underwriter's Q10, "commissions that reach the agency's operating account"; not Q9's own words). Never a payer region that names only a bank (R2-B03's `_bank_only_payer`). The payer's name reading as a lender's (`_LENDER_NAME_WORD`: a funding, lending, loan, capital, cash-advance, advance, MCA, acceptance, servicing, finance, mortgage, credit, leasing or portfolio word, `FINANCIAL` and `ADVANCED` left out; or a listed auto lender originating the row, `DEALER_FUNDING_PAYERS`) labels the row (c), `lender_paid_for_services`; every other payer is (a). The label is a label only: a customer whose name starts with a whole-word `ADVANCE`, `CAP`, `ADV` or `CREDIT` (`ADVANCE AUTO PARTS`) is labelled (c), its tier the same.
  - **A layout with no entry label** (empty entry fields: Wells Fargo, Citizens, TD and others print the entry words inside the payer region): a payer reading with two or more roots, or a root at or after the end of its first company form (`LLC`, `INC`, `CORP`, `CO`, `LTD` …), stays held (`_labelless_root_refusal`: `<NAME> CAPITAL ADVANCE VENDOR PMT`, `<NAME> LLC FUNDING PAYABLES`). A single root such a layout prints cannot tell a name from a purpose and is read as the name (the owner's (a)): `<NAME> FUNDING PAYABLES` is released whether `FUNDING` is the payer's name or the purpose's.
  - **A payer-less row** (a check, cash or deposit row with no payer region, or a transfer read on the whole row): its root is read on the whole row, so (a) and (c) never release it; a finance-named customer's check with an invoice memo stays held.
  - **(b) `lessor_rent`:** the statement's business is in leasing or property (`_lessor_business`), no special payer arm fired, and every place that fired is the rent sense of `LEASE` alone (`_RENT_LEASE`: never before `FUND…`, `FINANC…`, `LOAN`, `ADVANCE`, `PROCEEDS`, `BUYOUT`, `PURCH…` or `TO OWN`; the `LEASING` root is no rent), no other root left once it is blanked. A payer place is a rent memo only after the payer's first company form, with no root before the form's end (`<NAME> LLC LEASE PMT`, a memo the region swallowed): a payer named `LEASE …` before its form (`LEASE HOLDINGS LLC`) is no memo. A lease-to-own fund (`LEASE FUND`) and a leasing company stay with Q8 and T4.
  - **The lessor** (`_lessor_business`, read once per statement in pass 7 beside the business shape and the disbursers): one of the holder's names (the first credit's holder names, its account name and its holder name) prints a leasing or property trade word (`_PROPERTY_TRADE`: `REALTY`, `REAL ESTATE`, `PROPERTY`, `PROPERTIES`, `PROPS`, `LEASING`, `RENTAL(S)`, `LANDLORD`, `APARTMENT(S)`, `APTS`, `LOFTS`, `TOWNHOMES`, `STORAGE`, `PARKING`, `PLAZA`, `MALL`, `ESTATES`, `PROP MGMT`); or a property-management platform's credit posts (§7.10, `property_management_payments`); or two or more distinct payers pay rent: non-duplicate posted credits that no non-revenue rule took, no card credit and no Zelle deposit (Q3 (2026-10-02) excludes it later in the pass; the skip is kept in both readings of the owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3, so the Zelle setting moves Zelle rows only, R2-OW17), printing `RENT`, `RENTS`, `RENTAL(S)` (never `RENT A CAR`) or a rent `LEASE` on the row before its receiver fields, the holder's names removed; a row with a payer region counts under its payer key unless the region names the holder; a payer-less row counts as its own payer only on a check, cash, branch or ATM deposit; a payer-less transfer, person-to-person or wire row is never a rent payer. Audit round 3, R3-B14 (R3-60, §20; Q9 (b), "LEASE PAYMENT / rent received counts when the business is in leasing or property"): in the third arm a row whose payer region gives an empty payer key (an account designation: `ONLINE BANKING TRANSFER FROM CHK|SAV <n> CONFIRMATION <n> RENT`) is no rent payer, and the rent words are read on the row with the payer's own name removed (`_rent_payer_name`: on a row that prints a payer-name field, `_prints_payer_name_field`, its name proper, `_payer_name_proper`; on a row that prints none, the region up to the end of its first company form, the `_rent_memo_payer` convention; narrowed by R3-B14 review round 1, finding 3, §20, from "or the whole region when it prints no form", since such a region holds the entry description too: the region's leading rent words are the entry description a label-less layout prints first, Truist's `RENT <tenant> LLC … CUSTOMER ID`, never the name, and with no company form the name is the region up to a rental trade noun, `RENTALS` after a name word or `RENTAL` ending the region, `_rent_trade_noun_name`, or none, so a tenant's memo after a name with no form, `<tenant> RENT 540301 …`, `ACH DEPOSIT <tenant> RENT`, `<tenant> RENTAL PAYMENT`, `RENTAL INCOME <tenant>`, still reads), so a payer named `… RENTALS` (`<NAME> PARTY RENTALS INC DES:VENDOR PMT`, Truist's `PAYMENT <NAME> RENTALS … EQUIPMENT AND CUSTOMER ID`, Wells Fargo's `<NAME> AUTO RENTALS INC ACH PAYMNT`) is no rent payer, while a DES entry, a memo after the payer's company form (`<NAME> LLC LEASE PMT`) and a wire's or a book transfer's memo (`REF … RENTALS`) still read.
  - **The hidden-loan guard, last:** a payer the statement debits stays held as `financing_named_payer` (`_payer_collects`, R2-OW05's: any lender or other posted debit naming the payer by the B4 forms, 5.6's first word or a cut or glued spelling, or (audit round 3, R3-B17: R3-15, §20) a numbered company's number; only the bank's receiving fee and a card purchase are ignored; audit round 3, R3-B17 (R3-74, R3-77, §20): both sides read as §5.2's counter-debit readings, so a funder collecting under RBC's or Scotiabank's `INVESTMENT` form, CIBC's `PRE-AUTH DEBIT` or Scotiabank's `ACHDEBIT` is read by its name, never by the label). This is a documented over-hold of the owner's "collecting loan payments": a bill or a fee the business pays the same payer holds it too.
  - **Recorded limits:** a registered lender's credit that prints invoice or vendor wording (`GM FINANCIAL DES:VENDOR PMT`) is D1's financing proceeds before this pass (non-revenue first) and is never released (an open owner question, §17.1); a funder's first advance printed with vendor wording and no collection debit yet is released, flagged and reviewable; the wording is read per line, so one payer's worded rows count while its unworded rows stay held.
  - **The relabel** (§8.10): last in `_tier_reason`, after R2-B07's unread branch, a released row the tiers count takes the release's reason, unless its counted reason is one it keeps (`_Q9_KEEPS`: `payer_text_not_read`, `numbered_company_payer`, `factoring_payout`, `payout_credit_entity`, `platform_unconfirmed`, `customer_financing_payout`, `construction_progress_draw`, `insurer_paid_for_services`, `lender_paid_for_services`); a held reason is never overridden. A released Zelle row is still excluded by the Zelle step (`zelle_excluded`, its reading the release's).

- **`payer_debited_as_lender`:** the payer's first distinctive word (§7.5), or a numbered company's number (audit round 3, R3-B17: R3-15, §20), is also the first distinctive word (or the number) of a posted debit in the same statement whose state is `confirmed_lender`, `potential_lender` or a financing group. This is the unregistered funder that funds and then collects.   - the payer: an equipment auction or a car buyer (the registry's `ASSET_SALE_PAYERS`: Ritchie Bros. and RB Global, IronPlanet, Purple Wave, BigIron, GovDeals, Copart, IAA, Carvana, CarMax's stores, Peddle, Vroom; never Proxibid, never CarMax Auto Finance or CarMax Business Services) read as the whole payer name, as a factor's is (company forms, entry words, references, a DBA tail or a B/O field's address after the alias, and a seller's words `PAYOUT`, `SELLER`, `PROCEEDS`, `CONSIGNOR`, `CONSIGNMENT`; a longer name is another payer and a glued `<alias>LLC` is not read), with a seller's word on the row (`SELLER(S)`, `CONSIGN…`, `PAYOUT(S)`, `PROCEEDS`), or, for every platform but Copart and IAA (which also pay their towing and transport vendors), with no service word on the purpose (`TRANSPORT…`, `HAUL…`, `TOW`, `TOWING`, `DELIVER…`, `FREIGHT`, `SHIPPING`, `LOGISTIC…`, `LABOR`, `REPAIR…`, `RECON…`, `DETAIL…`, `INSPECT…`, `COMMISSION(S)`, `FEE(S)`, `REIMB…`, `REBATE(S)`, `SERVICE(S)`, `STORAGE`, `MARKETING`, `ADVERTIS…`, `RENT…`, `LEASE`) and a holder whose trade does not serve the platforms (a transporter, trucker, hauler, logistics firm, carrier, freight, delivery, expediting or courier firm, a detailer, a reconditioner, an inspector, a glass, tire, repair or mechanic shop, a driver or staffing firm, a towing or wrecker service); a platform's vendor payment (§7.5's accounts-payable wording, a vendor, invoice or payables word) is never read;
  - the purpose: `<asset> SALE` (never `SALES`), `SALE OF <asset>` and `SOLD <asset>` with at most two filler words between that are no connector or goods word (`TO`, `FOR`, `ON`, `AT`, `BY`, `FROM`, `OF`, `AND`, `OR`, `WITH`, `PER`, `IN`, `PART(S)`, `TIRE(S)`, `SERVICE(S)`, `REPAIR(S)`, `LABOR`, `ACCESSOR…`, `SUPPL…`, `GOODS`, `LOAD(S)`, `CARGO`, `FUEL`, `WARRANT…`, `INSURANCE`), and `<asset> SOLD`, read outside the payer's own name proper and never inside a name a company form ends within three more words with no connector (`<NAME> TRUCK SALE AND SERVICE INC`); the assets are the vehicle and heavy-equipment nouns (`TRUCK(S)`, `TRAILER(S)`, `VEHICLE(S)`, `VEH`, `CAR(S)`, `AUTO(S)`, `TRACTOR(S)`, `BOAT(S)`, `RV(S)`, `CAMPER(S)`, `MOTORCYCLE(S)`, `EXCAVATOR(S)`, `LOADER(S)`, `SKID STEER(S)`, `FORKLIFT(S)`, `BACKHOE(S)`, `BULLDOZER(S)`, `DOZER(S)`, `CRANE(S)`, `SEMI(S)`; R2-OW06 review round 1: `FLEET` alone is none, so a fleet card's `FLEET SALE` settlement wording is a fuel merchant's revenue, while `SALE OF FLEET VEHICLES` and `FLEET TRUCK SALE` read through their noun) and the generic `EQUIPMENT`, `EQUIP`, `MACHINERY`. A commission or a fee next to the sale (R2-OW06 review round 1: `COMMISSION(S)`, `COMM(S)` or `FEE(S)` right after it, `COMMISSION(S)` or `FEE(S)` right before it with at most `ON`, `FOR`, `FROM` or `OF` between: `CAR SALE COMMISSION`, `COMMISSION ON TRUCK SALE`, `TRUCK SALE FEE`) is a broker's or an agent's earned revenue and is never read; a fee printed apart (`TRUCK SALE NET OF FEES`) leaves the sale, and so (audit round 3, R3-B15: R3-59, §20; Q11 (b), standard G6, §4.2: deposits arrive net of fees) does a commission or a fee a netting word stands beside (`WITHHELD`, `DEDUCTED`, `DEDUCT…` or `NETTED` after it; `NET OF`, `LESS`, `AFTER` or `MINUS` before it, and a bare `NET` before `FEES` only, R3-B15 review round 1, finding 1, §20: `_asset_sale_commission`), what the proceeds are net of: `TRUCK SALE FEES WITHHELD`, `TRUCK SALE COMM WITHHELD`, `LESS FEES TRUCK SALE`, `NET FEES TRUCK SALE` and `NET OF COMMISSION TRUCK SALE` are the sale, while `TRUCK SALE COMMISSION`, `COMMISSION ON TRUCK SALE`, `TRUCK SALE FEE` and `FEE FOR TRUCK SALE` stay a broker's revenue, and so do a broker's or an agent's `NET COMMISSION ON TRUCK SALE` (its own earned commission after splits) and `NET FEE FOR TRUCK SALE`. R3-B15 review round 2 (finding 1, §20; R2-OW06 review round 1's broker carve-out, standard A11): a seller's proceeds never lead with or come out of a commission, so a commission word printed directly before the netting phrase (`COMMISSION LESS FEES ON TRUCK SALE`, `NET COMMISSION LESS FEES TRUCK SALE`, `AGENT COMMISSION AFTER FEES FOR TRUCK SALE`) or fees a netting word takes from or off a commission (`TRUCK SALE FEES WITHHELD FROM COMMISSION`) stays a broker's revenue, as its mirror `TRUCK SALE COMMISSION LESS FEES` does, while a commission a netting word itself stands before (`NET OF COMMISSION LESS FEES TRUCK SALE`) is still the sale. A vehicle's or heavy equipment's sale reads through an invoice reference (`INV`, `INVOICE`, `INV #<n>`; the owner made no invoice carve-out), so only accounts-payable, vendor or payables wording spares it; a generic equipment or machinery sale, which many trades invoice (HVAC, solar, restaurant and medical supply), is never read when it cites an invoice or vendor wording, when a single-row rule verified it, or when the holder is a supplier (`SUPPLY`, `SUPPLIES`, `SUPPLIER(S)`).

  Never read: a claimed row; a Zelle row in the No reading (Q3 (2026-10-02); in the counted reading of the owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3 a Zelle truck or equipment sale is asset-sale proceeds, as a Venmo one is, R2-OW17); a possible return or a refund; a row an insurer-name hold reads, unless the payer is IAA (its `INSURANCE` is the auction's name) and no later hold of §8.10's order would name the row (R2-OW06 review round 1: `CreditFacts.hold_past_insurer_name`, so an IAA seller payout beside an IAA purchase debit stays held `insurer_named_payer`, reviewable, as Copart's stays held `payer_also_debited`). The tier loop applies the reading where the tier would count the row, where IAA's insurer-name hold alone reads it, or where an invoice or customer-payment descriptor's verification stands (after the factoring, self-own, financier and payables demotions, §8.10); every other hold wins and keeps the row held. **Dealer evidence** (read once per statement, before the tiers): R2-OW05's dealer activity (a Q7 credit that is not payables-only, a credit union's `VHCL PURCH`, a floor-plan financier's row or a `FLOOR PLAN` form, a posted debit naming Manheim, ACV Auctions or OPENLANE, a dealer-only auction purchase), a §7.8 auction's payout credit, or a vehicle or equipment trade name on the holder's names (`AUTO(S)`, `AUTOMOTIVE`, `AUTOMOBILE(S)`, `CARS`, `MOTORS`, `MOTORCARS`, `TRAILERS`, `EQUIPMENT`, `EQUIP`, `MACHINERY`, `TRACTOR(S)`, `IMPLEMENT(S)`, `MARINE`, `MARINA(S)`, `BOATS`, `BOATYARD(S)`, `YACHT(S)`, `RV(S)`, `POWERSPORTS`, `MOTORSPORTS`, `CYCLES`, `DEALER(S)`, `DEALERSHIP`, `SALVAGE`, `WRECKING`, `AUCTION…`, `COLLISION`, `BODY SHOP`, `LEASING`, or an asset noun or `FLEET` before `SALES`, `RENTAL(S)`, `LEASING`, `SUPPLY`, `SUPPLIES` or `RECYCL…`; never a bare `SALES`, `SUPPLY`, `SUPPLIES`, `FLEET`, `RENTAL(S)`, `RECYCLING` or `TOWING`; `MOTOR`, `TRUCKING` and `TRUCKS` stay out) that prints no recovery, repossession, towing or collateral word (R2-OW05's veto). The trade-name arm goes beyond the owner's words (§17.1).
- **`payer_also_debited`:** the payer's first distinctive word (§7.5's definition), or a numbered company's number (audit round 3, R3-B17: R3-15, §20), is also the first distinctive word (or the number) of a posted debit in the same statement that is not a lender debit. The payer may be the owner's other account, an affiliate, or a funder whose daily debits no rule names; the accounts-payable verifier's R2 required review. It covers the §7.5 counter-debit rows (`payer_remittance_with_counter_debit`, 19 rows, $242K) and the Q5 and Q6 counter-debit guards (§8.5, §8.6). A payer debited as a lender is `payer_debited_as_lender` instead. Audit fix batch B4 (§20: I02, I38, I56) narrows it to the debits that can be circular money, as its purpose states: the bank's own receiving fee for an incoming wire or funds transfer never holds the payer; a processor's own fee, discount, chargeback, adjustment or returns debit never holds a credit that prints settlement, payout, `MID` or merchant-services wording; a bill the holder pays (bill pay, EBPP, autopay, a utility, telecom, cable or subscription) never holds a payer that does not read as an insurer; except that a fee or bill debit for the credit's own amount, or a bill debit that is one of two or more at one amount, still holds (a processor's fixed fee recurs at one amount by nature). The debit's kind is read without its receiver fields' values, the holder's own name. A transfer, wire, person-to-person or own-account debit matches at any size. Generic words and banks' channel names never make the first word (`MERCHANT`, `EXPRESS`, `UTILITIES` …), a name glued on one side matches it spaced on the other, and a three-letter payroll provider (`ADP`) is a word. Audit round 2, R2-B02 (§20; standard A1, A2, A6, §4.2), in this order: (R18) a platform's payout and the platform's own pull, each printing a payout id (`holder_name` above: the merchant's descriptor on both, Stripe's refund and negative-balance pulls), never hold unless the pull is for the payout's own amount; then the holds above in their order; then (R01) a processor's or a platform's payout, read by its settlement wording or a payout form before the receiver fields (`MRCHNTSVCS`, `MRCH SVCS`, `COMB DEP`, Payment Brands' `PAYMNTBRAND` and `PYMNTBRDMIN`, `INTUIT CANADA PAYMENTS` and its cut `INTUIT CANADA P`, `DEPOSIT <bank> MERCHANT`, a twelve-character payout id of letters and digits after `ST`) or by a merchant-ID field anywhere on the row (`MID <six digits or more>`, which Chase and Truist print after the receiver), is never held by the processor's card charge or by a one-off debit of its own that reads no other kind (a subscription, a `CARD PMT`, a debit that prints only the processor's name and digits): only a circular or lender debit, a debit for the payout's own amount, or a non-card debit recurring at one amount still holds it. A card purchase printed in a form the card-form prefix misses (`DEBIT CARD PURCHASE`, `DBCRD PUR`, `POS DB`, `POS DEBIT`, `POS PURCHASE`, `POINT OF SALE`, a glued `PURCHASE<digits>`, a charge ending `<state or province> USA` or `CAN`, or a debit the classifier classes `pos`) is a card charge where it reads a fee, a bill or another debit, never a circular debit or the receiving fee; it keeps that kind and still counts for recurrence (R2-B02 review round 1: the card form only lifts a payout's hold; beside a credit with no payout form it holds as its kind does, so a bill or subscription printed in a card form reads the bill rule above). (R02) An ATM, ABM or cash withdrawal that is no circular money never holds a payer (it names a place, never a payer; review round 1: a company whose name leads with `ATM` or `ABM`, a legal form within its next two words, none of them a cash or posting word (audit round 3, R3-B16: R3-34, §20: `WITHDRAWAL`, `WITHDRAW`, `WITHDRWL`, `WTHDRWL`, `WDL`, `WD`, `DEBIT`, `CASH`, `FEE`, `PURCHASE`, `TRANSACTION`, `TXN`, so `ATM WITHDRAWAL <name> INC` stays a cash withdrawal), or an ACH entry printing one, is a payee, never a withdrawal), and the readings and the whole-name match of `payer_debited_as_lender` above apply. (R48 part 1) The bank's receiving fee reads its outgoing words on its label and the words before the sender it reprints after `TT` or `FROM`, never inside that sender's name, so `FUNDS TRANSFER FEE TT CONTOSO TO G` is the fee for a wire from `CONTOSO TO GO INC`, never an outgoing-wire fee; a bare `WIRE TRANSFER FEE <name>` reads as before. Review round 1: `FROM` before the holder's own account (an account word or a masked account number) or before `TO` starts no sender, so `WIRE TRANSFER FEE FROM CHECKING TO <payee>` is the fee for the holder's own wire; `OUTGOING`, `BNF` and `BENEFICIARY`, which no sender's name prints, are read after the sender too. Audit round 3, R3-B16 (R3-33, §20): the holder's own account is also an account product's name (up to two of `BUSINESS`, `BUS`, `OPERATING`, `PAYROLL`, `PRIMARY`, `COMMERCIAL`, `ANALYZED`, `ANALYSIS`, `PERSONAL` before an account word), `MONEY MARKET`, `OPERATING` alone or a digit run of three or more (the number a bank prints after `*` or `...`), so `WIRE TRANSFER FEE FROM BUSINESS CHECKING TO <payee>` is circular; any other word after `FROM` still starts a sender (a product name outside the list and the holder's own name, `FROM <holder> TO <payee>`, are recorded residuals). (R3-35, §20) The processor's fee and the bill are read with Chase's glued SEC code split off the entry (`CO ENTRY DESCR:FEESSEC CCD`, `MTHLY DISCSEC`, `CHARGEBACKSEC`, `BILL PAYMTSEC`, `PLANT UTILSEC`, `VZ BILLPAYSEC`), and a fee word glued after another word at the entry's end is the processor's fee (`MONTHLYFEESEC`, `PAYCORFEESSEC`, `SERVICEFEESEC`, never `COFFEESEC`), so an unclaimed processor's fixed glued fee no longer re-holds its settlements; the receiving fee and circular money read the row as printed (a glued `TRANSFERSEC` keeps its kind). (R3-03, §20; owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q2; the MCA principle) A credit the Q2 release counted as an insurer paying for the business's work is held by a debit naming its carrier only when that debit is circular money, is for the credit's own amount, or recurs at one amount printing no premium or retry word (`PREM`, `PREMS`, `PREMIUM(S)`, `PREMSEC`, `RETRY`, read with the SEC code split off): an agency's or a provider's premium to the carrier that pays it is an ordinary expense, never money going round, and recurs at one amount by nature, as a processor's fixed fee does; an insurer the release does not count keeps B4's hold beside its premium or bill. (R3-77, §20; the underwriter's Q2; standard A9, B6) RBC's posting-type label `INSURANCE` (and its other labels, §5.2's counter-debit readings) names no party, so a clinic's `INSURANCE <insurer>` credits are compared with its debits by the insurer's own name: a debit to another insurer, `INSURANCE <another insurer>`, at the credit's own amount or recurring, never holds them, while a premium to the same insurer still names it. (R3-15, §20) A numbered affiliate's or own account's round trip (`MISC PAYMENT <n> ONTARIO` beside `ONLINE BANKING TRANSFER TO <n> ONTARIO INC`, an e-Transfer from and to `<n> ALBERTA LTD`, BMO's `DIRECT DEPOSIT <n> ONTA AP CC` beside `ONLINE BILL PAYMENT <n> ONTARIO INC`) is held by its number, as its word-named twin is, and BMO's cut `ONTA` is no key (a debit printing `ONTA` with another number never holds it).
- **`non_sale_purpose` after the counter-debit holds** (audit fix batch B4, §20: I56): a payroll provider's tax-service credit (`ADP`, `PAYCHEX`, `GUSTO` or `INTUIT` with `TAX` or `TAXES`, the tax word read on the payer region and the entry fields, never on the holder's name a label-less layout prints in the row) that no debit holds is the holder's own tax impound coming back.

### 8.2 Q2: cash, branch, ATM and bare deposits; transfer wording

The patterns follow the memo's `categorize.py`, which agrees with 94% of 315 hand-sorted payer groups; every pattern that file holds is inlined below. The cash, branch and ATM patterns apply only to a row that prints no electronic-payment form and no person-to-person rail, so an ACH payer named like a branch (`BRANCH MESSENGER`) is never read as a teller deposit.
- **Cash:** `\bCASH DEP(?:OSIT)?\b`, `\bATM CASH\b`, `\bCPS DEVICE\b`, `\bCURRENCY PROCESSING\b`, `\bSMART ?SAFE\b`, `\bCOIN\b`, `\bCASH IN\b`.
- **Branch and teller:** `\bCOUNTER (?:CREDIT|DEPOSIT)\b`, `\bTELLER\b`, `\bIN BRANCH\b`, `\bBRANCH\b`, `\bBRCH\b`, `\bDEPOSIT AT BR\b`, `\bDEPOSIT THANK YOU\b`, `\bMAIN OFFICE\b`, `\bPRE ?ENCODED\b`, `\bNIGHT (?:DEP|DROP)\b`, `\bBANKING CENTRE\b`, `^GC\b.*\bDEPOSIT\b`, `\bG DEPOT\b`, `\bDEPOT\b`, `\bDEPOSIT IBB\b`, `\bVAULT DEP\w*`, `\bSTORE DEPOSIT\b`, `\bDEPOSIT MADE IN\b`.
- **ATM:** `\bATM\b.*\bDEP(?:OSIT)?\b`, `\bDEP(?:OSIT)?\b.*\bATM\b`, `\bABM\b`.
- These three are `counted_flagged` / `no_payer_printed`, never Verified (§6.1 step 9b).
- **Two cash shapes the reader missed** (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q7: "make cash injections like ATM count as true revenue"; R2-OW14, §20), each the cash form's own last alternative, so they join the three above (`counted_flagged` / `no_payer_printed`, never Verified; G10 covers them):
  - **Arm R, a retail cash load:** `(?<![A-Z])US ?(?:WALGREENS|CVS|7 ?ELEVEN|WAL ?MART|DOLLAR GENERAL|RITE ?AID|FAMILY DOLLAR|CIRCLE K) W ?\d+$` (`_RETAIL_CASH_LOAD`), Bluevine's `<ST> <town> <street> US<RETAILER> W<n>` at the row's end. Inferred from the shape: no statement was opened to confirm it is a cash load at a retail cash network. The statements that carry it print the bank's `CASH DEPOSIT FEE` debits beside the loads (41 in the five statements with the corpus's 46 loads, 20 of them dated on a load's day), which reads as the fee for a retail cash deposit.
  - **Arm S, a branch deposit printed with its transit:** `^(?:\d{1,2} \d{1,2} )?DEPOSIT (?!.*\b(?:LLC|L L C|INC|INCORPORATED|CORP|CORPORATION|COMPANY|LTD|LTEE|LIMITED|LLP|PLLC|ULC|PLC)\b)(?:[A-Z]+ ){1,4}\d{5} \d{3}$` (`_BRANCH_DEPOSIT_TRANSIT`), Scotiabank's `DEPOSIT <place> <5-digit transit> <3-digit sequence>` as the whole row; a row that prints a legal form names a depositor and keeps its reading, and a card settlement printing digits right after `DEPOSIT` is no branch deposit. The arm reads any bank's row of that shape; the corpus has none outside Scotiabank. Audit round 3, R3-B07 (R3-45, §8.1, §20): off Scotiabank's statements its whole-row match never counts as "inside a deposit form" for the financing roots' location removal, so a funder's name before a place still holds there.
  - A row of either shape prints no payer, so a same-place debit (a purchase at the store, a withdrawal at the branch) no longer holds it as `payer_also_debited`, and a branch deposit's place is no longer read as a named payer (`named_payer_unlabelled`).
- **Bare deposit, credit or EFT,** on any channel: after the template prefixes, `GENERIC_WORDS` and the reference tokens are removed, no payer word remains, and the row prints no transfer wording. It is `counted_flagged` / `no_payer_printed` too (§8.10, last step), never Verified. BMO's `DIRECT DEPOSIT <digits>` is a numbered company (§5.2) instead.
- **A payer the parser did not read** (audit fix batch B10: I05, I60, §20): Q2 covers a row whose statement prints no payer, never a row whose parser lost the payer the statement printed. A deterministic parser marks a credit it publishes with only its own posting-type or section label because it could not read the printed payer (`Transaction.payer_text_unread`: a core-processor merchant block the attribution count cannot give to one row, the daily core-processor template's every credit block while its reading waits on G7 (a teller's reference aside, which names no payer; audit fix batch B10 review round 1), First Citizens' `Other Credit` where its description overlay fails closed); such a row, where the pass would read it as a bare deposit (§8.10's last step), is `counted_flagged` / `payer_text_not_read` instead of `no_payer_printed`, never Verified. Every hold before it still applies (a marked bare transfer label stays `transfer_no_counterparty`), and a cash, branch, teller or ATM label keeps `no_payer_printed` marked or not, since the label itself says the statement printed no payer (B10 review round 1). Whether such rows should be held instead would change this section's rule and is the owner's; the statement carries the fact `payer_text_unread` when more than 30% of its posted credit rows are marked (§9.1). Audit round 2, R2-B07 (R07, §20): the counted core-processor template keeps, on each credit it marks at a welded flush, that flush's joined text (`Transaction.unread_payer_text`, §9.1), the blocks of every row outstanding at it; a marked row that would be `payer_text_not_read` is held as `unread_run_names_financing` instead when one block of that text (split after each ACH class code; audit round 3, R3-B09: R3-87, §20: never after a class-code word followed by a legal form, which is part of a name, as CashArc's `CASH-ARC LLC`; R3-B09 review round 1, §20: a form of the LLC family only, `LLC`, `L.L.C.`, `L L C`, `LLP` or `PLLC`, since the other forms open real originator names) names a registry lender of a lender or financing state other than an alternative position or a factor (§8.1, Q6: lenders never count) or a lending bank (`LENDING_BANK_CREDIT_PAYERS`, T4). The bare financing root is not read (a customer named `CAPITAL` stays `payer_text_not_read`), the text never verifies, never names the row's payer and never puts an amount toward lender credits, and the review card prints it so a reviewer can release a customer's row the lender's block held. Which row of the run is the lender's stays unknown: pairing blocks by printed order is not done (B10 measured out-of-order flushes). Audit round 3, R3-B09 (R3-91, R3-87, §20): the daily core-processor template keeps each marked credit's block the same way (`unread_payer_text`; reading it as the payer still waits on G7, §17.1), so R07's hold reads it there too; balance_by_date keeps the continuation line printed under an incoming wire's row (the whole line, which no column boundary attributes) and B1 the lines printed under a wire's row, each on the wire it marks; and the counted template's one-block count reads a class-code word followed by a legal form as part of a name, so a lone block of such a name is one block and is attributed.
- **Transfer wording:** `\bTRANSFER\b`, `\bTRNSFR\b`, `\bXFER\b`, `\bTFR\b`, `\bBR TO BR\b`, `\bONLINE BANKING\b`, `\bINTERNET (?:BANKING|TRANSFER)\b`, `\bFUNDS TRANSFER\b`, on a row that prints no person-to-person rail. Audit fix batch B8 (I46, §20): and the plural `\bTRANSFERS\b` (`EXTERNAL DEPOSIT ACH TRANSFERS PAYMENT`, `… FUNDS TRANSFERS`), now that §7.0's revenue text cuts TD's back panel, which prints `… ELECTRONIC FUNDS TRANSFERS`; the holds' posting labels drop `FUNDS TRANSFERS` as they drop `FUNDS TRANSFER`. Audit round 2, R2-B09 (§20): American Express's label `ONLINE TRANSFER PAYMENT CREDIT` at the row's start is no transfer wording only when an originator word follows it (R31: the bare label, or the label before `FROM`, an account word, `ID`, a masked account or digits, is a bare transfer, held; audit round 3, R3-B08: R3-41, §20: the gate reads only a row the full template does not match, so on the full template any originator keeps the ACH reading, and the row before its receiver block keeps the template's `EXTERNAL` after the id for every reader of the label); the glued `ONLINETRANSFER`, `MOBILETRANSFER` and `INTERNETTRANSFER` (singular or plural) are transfer wording, the glued label at the row's start under the same originator rule (R45); and on a credit, transfer wording printed inside a company-formed ACH originator's own name (before `DES`, after `ORIG CO NAME`: `CONTOSO TRF LLC`, `TRF INDUSTRIES INC`, `CONTOSO TRANSFER INC`) is the company's name, never a transfer, so the row is an ACH payer Q6 reads (R28); the entry field's wording (`DES:TRANSFER`, `CO ENTRY DESCR:BANK XFER`) is still read, and a name with no company form once the wording is out (`<NAME> BANK XFER`, `TRANSFER AND STORAGE CO`) keeps the transfer reading. A debit's reading and Q6's entry-field refusal are unchanged. R2-B09 review round 1 (§20): `DES` opens that name only with a field of Bank of America's layout after its entry (`ID`, `INDN`, `CO ID`, `IND NAME`, `IND ID` or an ACH class code), never as a town's word (`TRANSFER FROM <NAME> LLC DES MOINES IA`; audit round 3, R3-B08: R3-88, §20: whatever field word follows the town, `DES MOINES`, `DES PLAINES`, `DES PERES`, `DES ALLEMANDS` or `DES LACS`, never opens the field), and a name printing a transfer's phrase word (`FROM`, `FRM`, `FR`, `TO`, `BETWEEN`) is no company's own name: such a named transfer keeps its transfer reading. A `VIREMENT` printed without an Interac form (`VIREMENT EN LIGNE`, `VIREMENT ENTRE COMPTES`, a bare `VIREMENT`) is transfer wording too in pass 7 (S4.2 follow-up 2; §20's `VIREMENT` line); audit round 3, R3-B12 (R3-29, §20): `PAR COURRIEL` is an Interac form (Interac's French name), so `VIREMENT PAR COURRIEL`, and its plural, is the e-Transfer rail of §8.4, read before the cash and branch `DEPOT` above, never transfer wording.
  - With no counterparty (no payer word after the template prefixes, `GENERIC_WORDS`, the account words of T13 and the reference tokens are removed), it is `excluded_pending_review` / `transfer_no_counterparty`. The tier pass tests this **before** the check, cash, branch and ATM tiers, so `TELLER TRANSFER` is held, not counted.
  - With a named counterparty, T13 and §8.4 apply.
  - **In a package** (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q4; R2-OW16): a debit printing transfer wording is the transfer out §6.2's package pass 2 matches a bare deposit of another of the business's accounts to (0 to 2 days, exact cents; package-only). Its paper-or-cash guard (`paper_or_cash_deposit`, read on the row before its receiver fields) refuses a check deposit (§8.3) and a cash, branch, teller or ATM form above that prints a cash device's word (`_CASH_DEVICE_WORD`: `ATM`, `ABM`, `CASH`, `COIN`, `SMART SAFE`, `CPS DEVICE`, `CURRENCY PROCESSING`, `NIGHT DEP…`, `NIGHT DROP`, `VAULT`, `PRE ENCODED`) or arm R's retail cash load: a paper item or cash is never a transfer's receiving leg. A teller, counter or branch deposit printing no such word stays eligible (a branch transfer between two of the business's accounts can print that way on its receiving side), and so does a bare `NIGHT DEPOSIT`, which the cash form above does not read (`NIGHT (?:DEP|DROP)` as whole words). Nothing here changes a statement's own reading.
- **A pull that names only a bank** (audit round 2, R2-B03: R05, §20; a bank's name is never the payer's name): an ACH or unlabelled credit whose payer region is only a listed sending bank's name (the registry's `P2P_SENDING_BANK_NAMES`, which now lists `MSPBNA` and `ALLY BANK`) or one to four words ending `BANK`, `BANCORP`, `FSB` or `CREDIT UNION` that read as a bank by its own form (never a food or blood bank, never a company whose name holds the bank word, never a bank's settlement form), a trailing `ACH`, `ONLINE` or `N A` aside, printed with no entry field, is the holder's pull from another of its own bank accounts (`ACH CREDIT <bank>` on Relay, `<bank> ACH` on Brex, `ELECTRONIC DEPOSIT FROM <bank>` on U.S. Bank): `excluded_pending_review` / `transfer_no_counterparty`, unless a rule verified it or the registry, a payout entity, a factoring payee or a factor claimed it. The statement's own bank's channel (`CHASE ONLINE` on a Chase statement) is never held: a customer's bill payment through the bank, counted with no payer (§8.6). Audit round 3, R3-B08 (R3-31, R3-32, §20): the own bank is read first, as a whole region, by its full name and its printed short forms (the statement's bank field, the registry's `STATEMENT_BANK_PRINTED_NAMES`, and `OWN_BANK_SENDING_SPELLINGS`: `BOFA`, `BK OF AMERICA`, `US BANK`, `U S BANK`, `JPMORGAN CHASE`, `CHASE BANK` and every other listed sending bank's full name on its own statement), so a statement whose bank is itself a listed sending bank never holds its own name alone (`WELLS FARGO ACH` on Wells Fargo, `ACH CREDIT JPMORGAN CHASE` on Chase, `BOFA <n>` on Bank of America: counted with no payer); every Chase bank field reads `CHASE` as its own name; a P2P label counts only inside the payer region (the bank's name followed by `P2P`); a sperm, eye, tissue, milk, bone or cord-blood bank is no bank. A bare `USAA` on another bank's statement stays held as a sending bank's pull (the owner's own USAA account: standard B1, B7, F1).

### 8.3 Q3: check deposits

`\bMOBILE (?:CHECK |CHEQUE )?(?:DEPOSIT|DEP)\b`, `\bMOBILE CHE(?:CK|QUE)\b`, `\bMB DEP\b`, `\bBKOFAMERICA MOBILE\b`, `\bREMOTE (?:ONLINE )?(?:DEPOSIT|CAPTURE)\b`, `\bDEPOSIT CAPTURE\b`, `\bMERCHANT CAPTURE\b`, `\bDESKTOP (?:REMOTE )?DEPOSIT\b`, `\bEDEPOSIT SCAN\b`, `\bE ?CHEQUE DEPOSIT\b`, `\b(?:ATM )?CHE(?:CK|QUE)S? (?:DEPOSIT|DEP|RECEIVED)\b`, `\bMAIL DEPOSIT\b`, `^REMOTE$`, `\bIMAGED DEPOSIT\b`, `\bDEPOSITED (?:CHECK|ITEM)\b`, `\bRDC\b`, `\bSCAN(?:NED)? DEPOSIT\b`, `\bLOCKBOX\b`, `\bLBX DEP\b`.

These are `counted_flagged` / `check_deposit`, never Verified (§6.1 step 9b). A returned deposited item is decided earlier, as a reversal.

### 8.4 Q4: person-to-person, and named transfers

- **Rails:** the consumer rails `\bZELLE\b`, `\bINTERAC\b`, `\bE ?TRANSFER\b`, `\bE ?TFR\b`, `\bVIREMENT\b`, `\bVFC\b`, `\bAUTODEPOSIT\b`, `\bVENMO\b`, `\bCASH ?APP\b`, `\bSQUARE CASH\b`, `\bAPPLE CASH\b`, `\bPOPMONEY\b`, and the real-time and push rails `\bREAL TIME (?:TRANSFER|PAYMENT)\b`, `\bRTP\b`, `\bFEDNOW\b`, `\bINSTANT (?:PMT|PAYMENT|TRANSFER)\b`, `\bVISA (?:MONEY TRANSFER|DIRECT)\b`, `\bMONEY TRANSFER\b`, `\bMC SEND\b`, `\bPMNT RCVD\b`, `\bPAYMENT RECEIVED\b`. A row the registry or a form already claimed (an RTP payout from Amazon, a Visa Direct payout from Square) is not a person-to-person row. Audit round 2, R2-B11 (R44, §20): a consumer rail whose reference is glued after its word (CIBC's `E-TRANSFER<reference> <sender>`) is read once the revenue text splits the digits off (§7.0), so Q4's holds reach it on every bank; B2's reason for keeping CIBC's glued rows off the rail (to keep them out of the round-sum hold) is withdrawn. Audit round 3, R3-B12 (R3-29, §20): pass 7 also reads Interac's French name, `\bVIREMENTS? PAR COURRIEL\b` ("virement par courriel", singular or plural: `_INTERAC_COURRIEL`), as the e-Transfer rail, before a cash or branch `DEPOT` (§8.2): Banque Royale prints its autodeposit `DEPOT AUTO VIREMENTS PAR COURRIEL <sender> <reference>`, whose plural the classifier's `\bVIREMENT\b` never reads, so such a row was a branch deposit with no payer (`no_payer_printed`) and Q4's holds never ran. Its sender is read after `COURRIEL`, and the round-sum repeat, the holder's name and the counter-debit hold (the sender matched by its whole name, R2-B02's person match) read it as they read its English twin `E TRANSFER AUTODEPOSIT <sender> <reference>`. `DEPOT AUTO` or `DEPOT AUTOMATIQUE` alone is no form (beside `VIREMENT` it can be the holder's own scheduled transfer), and Interac's own `VIREMENT INTERAC DEPOT AUTOMATIQUE` reads through `INTERAC` as before. The classifier's rail (the 5.5 channel gate, the legacy classes, the debits) is unchanged, so a French debit (`VIREMENTS PAR COURRIEL ENVOYE …`) keeps the classifier's debit reading (residual); other French issuers' spellings are unknown (only Banque Royale prints `COURRIEL` in the corpus).
- **Named transfers** (T13): transfer wording (§8.2) with a named counterparty belongs here. Audit round 2, R2-B11 (R24, §20): a short own-account source after `FROM` (`CHK`, `CHECKG`, `CK`, `SAV`, `SV`, `MMA`, `DDA`, `PCA`, `CL`, `LOC`, `LN`, `CRD`) designates the holder's own account (§7.11 T5) only before an account number, a masked account, `ACCOUNT` or `ACCT`, or at the row's end; a company whose name starts with those letters (`TRANSFER FROM CL FABRIKAM INC`) is a named counterparty here (or a wire's sender, §8.5).
- **The sender** is the payer region (§5.2).
- **`transfer_account_designation`:** a named transfer whose row prints an account designation, an account-type word (`CHECKING`, `CHK`, `CHKG`, `SAVINGS`, `SAVING`, `SAV`, `SVGS`, `MONEY MARKET`, `MMA`, `DDA`, `ACCOUNT`, `ACCT`, `EVERYDAY`; audit round 2, R2-B09: R45, §20: and `CHCKING`, `CHKING`, `CKG`, which name no counterparty either) or a masked account number (`\bX{2,}\d{2,}\b`, `\bENDING (?:IN )?\d{3,}\b`), is held: it reads as the owner's account at another bank. Measured on the memo's rows: $1.18M, 1,473 rows, 168 statements.
- **`p2p_round_repeat`:** a sender with two or more round-sum credits on these rails or through named transfers in the statement has every one of its round-sum credits held. Its other credits stay counted. The memo counted a repeat of any amount; this reading follows the ruling's words, "repeated round sums from one sender".
- A sender with the holder's name is `holder_name` (§8.1).
- Everything else is `counted_flagged` / `p2p`, never Verified, even when the sender prints a company form (Q4, §6.1 step 9b).
- **Zelle (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q3; a Settings choice since 2026-10-06):** the owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3 (R2-OW17, §19.1) makes it the Settings choice "Mark Zelle Payments as True Revenue", Yes by default. The analysis computes two readings of every statement that has a Zelle credit (`classify_statement_readings`: the shared prefix once, pass 7, pass 7b and the duplicate finalisation once per reading) and stores the first with the edits to the second (§9.1); the choice picks one when an analysis is shown, so nothing is reprocessed. **Yes, the counted reading** (`zelle_true_revenue=True`): the Zelle step below does not run, so each Zelle credit carries exactly the rules' own reading of a person-to-person credit (`p2p`, PNC's `ZEL FROM` as `named_payer_unlabelled` (since audit round 3, R3-B12: R3-12, §20: pass 7 reads PNC's `ZEL` as its `ZELLE` twin, so a PNC Zelle credit takes `p2p` or one of these holds as the same sender's `ZELLE` row does, the round-sum repeat and the counter-debit hold's person match included, except where the classifier's reading of the raw text claims it first (R3-B12 review round 1, finding 2: the residual below)), or a hold: `holder_name`, `p2p_round_repeat`, `payer_also_debited`, `non_sale_purpose`, `financing_named_payer`, `possible_return`, `payroll_or_salary`), and every later step reads it as any row (the $1 floor, the premium-trust hold, the funding aid, pass 7b's returned funder payments). Two Q3-era carve-outs are lifted there: a builder's Zelle draw is a progress draw and a Zelle truck or equipment sale is asset-sale proceeds (§8.1), so such a row also leaves Q5's and Q6's repeats, as a Venmo sale or draw does (a repeat partner on its payer key can lose a verification: declared, §14.2). The lessor fact keeps its Zelle skip in both readings (§8.1), so the setting moves Zelle rows only. The latest decision on a Zelle row sets both readings (§10.7). **No, the stored reading:** every posted Zelle credit is `non_revenue` / `zelle_excluded` (method and rule `zelle_deposit_excluded`), whoever sent it, a lender or a processor paying through Zelle included. The rail reader (`zelle_deposit`) reads the revenue text before the receiver fields: `ZELLE` with no letter on either side (a glued date or reference reads: `ZELLE1234567`, `0302ZELLE`) or PNC's `ZEL FROM|TO`, never a name holding the letters (`HAZEL`, `ROSZELL`, `MAZZELLA`, `ZELLER`, `EZELL`). Audit round 3, R3-B12 (§20): the pass, the census's facts and the served Zelle view read it on the pass's own text (`pass_text`: TD Canada Trust's e-Transfer code dropped, R2-B11, and PNC's `ZEL FROM|TO` spelled `ZELLE FROM|TO`, R3-12), and an incoming wire or a loose wire's originator row is never a Zelle deposit (R3-56): an incoming wire (`_is_wire_row`) or a loose wire's originator row (`_loose_wire_originator`, also read on the row up to its first Zelle word, since the classifier's loose-wire label refuses a row printing a consumer rail) is not read, whatever its memo prints (`PMT DET:INVOICE <n> PAID BY WIRE INSTEAD OF ZELLE`); other wire layouts are recorded residuals below. Kept: the rail printed after a bank's wording (`TRANSFER IN ZELLE FROM`, `NOW NETWORK CREDIT … ZELLE`, `VISA DIRECT ZELLE`) and the ACH entry-description forms (`DES:ZELLE`, `CO ENTRY DESCR:ZELLE`: an entry its sender wrote as ZELLE most plausibly went through Zelle). Recorded residuals (0 corpus rows each): a company whose name holds the word `ZELLE` paying by ACH (`DE ZELLE HOLDINGS LLC DES:VENDOR PAY`) is still read as a Zelle deposit (R2-OW02's report, risk 5), since telling it from a `ZELLE FROM <company> INC` rail row needs a name-position rule the corpus would not test; a wire in a layout neither wire gate reads still reads a memo's `ZELLE` as the rail (R3-B12 review round 1, finding 3: the sender-first `<sender> WIRE` with no originator label after `WIRE`, `ONLINE WIRE TRANSFER FROM <sender>`, `WIRE TRANS SVC CREDIT <sender>` and `WIRE DEPOSIT <sender>`), and the up-to-the-rail arm refuses a Zelle row that prints `WIRE` and an originator label before its rail word (`MOBILE WIRE ORG ZELLE <sender>`); the classifier's consumer rail still reads a wire memo's `ZELLE`, so such a wire is counted (`wire_named_sender`) in both readings where its twin without the word verifies; PNC's `ZEL TO` debits keep the classifier's debit reading (R3-B12 review round 1, finding 4: the legacy class `other`, where a `ZELLE TO` debit's is `transfer`, and no person key; both are circular money to the counter-debit hold, the `ZEL TO` debit through the own-account arm's `ZEL`), so a credit for the debit's own amount, or one with no person key, names it by the first word, and another person sharing the recipient's given name is held `payer_also_debited` against it where a `ZELLE TO` debit's recipient names a credit only by the whole name (a counterfactual that gives a `ZEL TO` debit its person key moves no corpus credit); and the 5.5 channel gate leaves `ZEL` open (R3-B12 review round 1, finding 2: the classifier reads the raw text before pass 7, so a `ZEL FROM` credit whose sender looks like an operating platform (`SQUARE`, `STRIPE`, `SHOPIFY`, `UBER`, `DOORDASH`, `PAYPAL`) is claimed as an operating source, counted `platform_unconfirmed` once and Verified on a repeat (`recurring_operating_source`; `PAYPAL` stays counted), where its `ZELLE FROM` twin is counted `p2p` or held `p2p_round_repeat`; it predates R3-B12, no corpus `ZEL` row reads so and none is Verified, and it waits for a later classifier batch under G7). It is pass 7's last tier step (§8.10 step 26): a count, a verification and every hold (the round-sum repeat, the holder's name, a payer also debited, financing, a payer debited as a lender, the $1 floor's) become the exclusion, and the rules' own tier and reason stay on the record (the reason sentence names them, and the context signal `zelle_prior:<tier>:<reason>` keeps them: `zelle_prior_reading`). A row a non-revenue rule decided (a refund, a reversal, an opposite-direction pair, an own-account transfer, a listed funder's financing proceeds with the lender-credit exclusion, a non-operating credit) keeps that rule and no reason, and a direction conflict keeps its hold. Everything before the step still reads Zelle rows (the holds, Q5's and Q6's counts, a sender's named round sums: a sender's Zelle round sum still completes its group on another rail). The classifier's consumer rail (`_CONSUMER_P2P_RAIL`), the legacy classes, the lender fields and the debits are unchanged; the other rails keep this section's reading.

### 8.5 Q5: incoming wires

- **The wire family:** the leading labels of §7.9 N1, a third-party book transfer (§7.11, only with T19), or, for tiering only, the loose wire words `\bWIRE\b`, `\bFEDWIRE\b`, `\bFED WIRE\b`, `\bIWT\b`, `\bCHIPS CREDIT\b`, `\bSWIFT\b`, `\bFOREIGN REMITTANCE\b`, `\bWT FED\b`, `\bFED REF\b` on a row no rail of §8.4 claimed. Audit fix batch B5 (I14, I12's reader, §20): Navy Federal's `BANK WIRE DEPOSIT`, Columbia Bank's `WIRE DEPOSIT WIRE IN` and U.S. Bank's `WIRE CREDIT REF<n>` are N1 labels, and a loose-wire row's originator label (`ORIG`, `ORG`, `B O`, `ORIGINATOR`; never `ORIG CO` or `ORIG ID`) names its sender as an incoming wire's does. Audit round 2, R2-B10 (R26, §20): only a label printed after the row's first `WIRE` word, read from its own position; a label word before it is a word of the sender's own name on the `<sender> WIRE` layout (Mercury, Brex: `CONTOSO ORG LLC WIRE`, a `.org` domain), so the whole name is the payer region.
- **Verified: the same company twice or more** (method `repeat_wire_sender`, confidence 0.85). The row begins with an N1 label (or is a third-party book transfer under T19), and:
  - no hold of §8.1 applies to it;
  - its sender prints a company form (§5.2) or is a government or healthcare payer; audit fix batch B5 (I61, §20): here only, an `LLC` the 35-character originator field cut to `LL` and glued to the address after it (`<name> MANAGEMENT LL<city>`) is a company form; never a two-letter cut of another form (`CO`, `IN`, `LI`), and never for Q6;
  - two or more wire credits in the statement have that payer key (repeats, §5.2, which never count a held row);
  - the sender is not a numbered company (§5.2), and names no bank (`BANK`, `BANKING`, `BANCO`, `BANCA`, `BANQUE`, `BANCAIRE`, `SPARKASSE`, `BANCORP`, `N A`, `TRUST COMPANY`, `CREDIT UNION`, `FCU`, `SAVINGS`; audit round 3, R3-B07: R3-14, §20, added `BANKING` and the non-English bank words beside `BANCO`), since a relaying bank hides the real payer, and no title or escrow firm (`TITLE`, `ESCROW`, `CLOSING`, `SETTLEMENT`);
  - the row passes every veto of §7.9: the financing roots read as §7.9 reads them (after the channel words and the sending and intermediary bank fields are removed, and wrap-tolerant on the originator), the non-sale purposes, the own-account test, the brand-word affiliate test, the cut-field test and `match_known_payee`;
  - it prints none of the words that refuse a Q6 verification (§8.6).
- **Verified: an invoice or PO wire:** §7.9 (step 14).
- **Held:** a wire with no sender printed is `wire_no_sender` (audit fix batch B5, I14, §20: so is a wire whose sender region holds no name word, a lone glued reference, or only bank and layout labels: `BANK`, `DEPOSIT`, `INTERNATIONAL`, `IN`, `INCOMING`, `RECEIVED`, `DEP` and the bare channel words; `IWT` waits for audit batch B10; audit round 2, R2-B10 (R32, §20): the labels are the bare channel words, every wire layout word (`FEDWIRE`, `FED`, `INBOUND`, `INBD`, `CHIPS`, `SWIFT`, `WT`, `IWT`, `DOMESTIC`, `INTL`, `INTERNATIONAL`, `INCOMING`, `BOOK`, `TRANSFER`, `CREDIT`), `BANK`, `DEPOSIT`, `DEP`, `IN`, `RECEIVED` and `CR`, one list, so `INCOMING FEDWIRE`, `FEDWIRE CR` and `INBOUND WIRE` name no sender; audit round 3, R3-B07 (R3-40, §20; the underwriter's Q1): nor does a region of only label, holder-noise, account-designation, purpose, filler or legal-form words, on every wire layout and the labelled path (`WIRE TRANSFER IN <ref> BUSINESS`, `WIRE TRANSFER FROM BUSINESS ACCOUNT`, `WIRE FROM <ref> BUSINESS`, `… BUSINESS LLC`, `WIRE TRANSFER IN THE AMOUNT OF <ref>`), a numbered company keeping its reading (OQ3); (R3-42, §20) nor a listed sending bank's or the statement's own bank's channel name printed right after the wire's label with no originator label (`INBOUND WIRE <sending bank>`), while a bank by its own form there keeps the bank-originated hold); one the holder test matches is `holder_name`; one whose sender is also debited in the statement is `payer_also_debited` (§8.1); one that a hold of §8.1 names takes that hold (`OBI SERIES A INVESTMENT`, `REF INTERCO SWEEP` and `OBI PAYROLL` are held). The underwriter's Q1 (2026-10-02; audit I12; R2-OW12): the hold stays, every no-sender shape included. Pass 7's last step (`funding_series_after`, after the $1 floor and the premium-trust hold, so it reads the final tiers) records on each held `wire_no_sender` credit every Lenders or Potential Lenders series that meets all of these: one tab name (the potential payee label, else the canonical entity, as the tabs list it) and one amount to the cent (find_recurring_debits' amount); posted, not a duplicate, counting toward the lender or potential-lender count (a settlement-reversed debit, whose counts the reversal pass cleared, is no payment of the series, but an attempt on or before the deposit's day means the series was already running: audit round 3, R3-B02 (R3-66, §20), a dated attempt of the series' tab name and amount, paid or settlement-reversed, on or before the deposit's day keeps the series off that wire, as a paid one does); every row dated after the deposit's day, the first at most 10 days after it (`FUNDING_SERIES_WINDOW_DAYS`); two or more dates that `classify_cadence` reads daily or weekly (`_promotion_cadence` with `FUNDING_SERIES_MIN_PAYMENTS = 2`). `start_observed` says whether the statement shows a full gap of the series (its mean gap rounded up, and at least 3 days, `FUNDING_SERIES_MIN_LOOKBACK_DAYS`) before the deposit, counted from its printed period start, else from its earliest dated row. "Frequent payment" is read as a lender-side series (the Lenders or Potential Lenders tabs: registry funders, keyword recurrences, D6 payees), a narrowing of the ruling's "same payee or same amount" chosen on the measured noise: an all-debits pool is card purchases, payroll, own transfers and person-to-person payments. A registry lender's series needs two payments in the statement; an unknown payee is in the pool only once three fixed daily or weekly debits promote it (D6's and the keyword groups' promotion count). A series that follows several held wires goes on each, with its own days after. The aid never changes a tier, a reason, a figure or a lender row (G7: 0). Audit round 3, R3-B09 (R3-91, §8.2, §10.7, §20): a held wire whose reader kept a payer line it could not attribute (`unread_payer_text`: the daily core-processor template's block under the row, balance_by_date's continuation line, B1's lines under the row) stays `wire_no_sender`; only its review text says the payer line was not read. Reading that line as the sender is not done: with no holder name read on those statements, it would count own-name wires, closing proceeds and an unregistered lender's wire.
- **Otherwise:** `counted_flagged` / `wire_named_sender`, including senders that are persons, banks or title companies. A wire that §8.6's verification-only words refused is `named_payer_purpose_refused`.

### 8.6 Q6: named ACH and EFT payers

**Eligible rows** are unverified posted credits that meet all of these:
- the row prints an electronic-payment form (§5.2) and has a payer region;
- the channel gate (§6.1 step 9b) does not close it: it prints no person-to-person rail, and no transfer wording in its entry fields;
- it is not a wire;
- no registry alias, payout entity or factoring payee matched it, because platforms are decided by §7;
- no hold of §8.1 applies, so no financing root in its payer region or entry fields, no insurer name, no non-sale purpose, no pay wording and not the holder;
- it is not a numbered company (§5.2);
- audit round 2, R2-B03 (R05, §20): its payer region names more than a bank. A region that is only a listed sending bank's name, only the statement's own bank's name (its channel: `CHASE ONLINE` on a Chase statement) or one to four words ending in a bank's own form (§8.2's pull), a trailing `ACH`, `ONLINE` or `N A` aside, names no customer, so its repetition proves nothing; unless its entry prints a bank's merchant deposit or card settlement (`DEPOSIT`, `DEP`, `MTOT`, `BTOT`, `SETTLE…`, `STLMT`, `MERCH…`: `<bank> DES:DEPOSIT`, Synchrony's `MTOT DEP`) or its originator is a bank's settlement form, such a row is counted as `counted_flagged` / `no_payer_printed` (a bill payment through a bank, `<bank> … SEC:CIE`), or held by §8.2 when it prints no entry field. Audit round 3, R3-B08 (R3-31, R3-32, §20): the statement's own bank is read first, as a whole region, by its full name and its printed short forms (`BOFA`, `US BANK`, `JPMORGAN CHASE`, `CHASE BANK`; §8.2), and every Chase bank field (`Chase Savings`, `Chase Transaction Export`) reads `CHASE` as its own, so `CHASE ONLINE` is the own bank's channel on each of them; a person-to-person label refuses the reading only inside the payer region, after the bank's name (`BANK OF AMERICA P2P <reference> <sender>`), never in an entry field (`ORIG CO NAME:JPMORGAN CHASE … CO ENTRY DESCR:P2P` names no customer).

**Refused** (counted as `named_payer_purpose_refused`, not verified, not held): a row whose entry fields or payer region print one of the verification-only words below. They are sales wording often enough that holding them would take real revenue out of True, but they are not proof: `\bSETTLEMENT\b` (a legal or insurance settlement prints it, and so does an unregistered processor; audit round 3, R3-B10 review round 2, §20: alone, as before the batch, for review round 1's short spellings `SETTLMT` and `STLMT` are taken out again; a settlement §8.1's exemption releases is refused as proof by the pass's own flag, in each spelling, slot and boundary, so a third party's short spelling keeps the reading it had), `\bTAX(?:ES)?\b`, `\bIRS\b`, `\bCRA\b`, `\bFEES?\b`, `\bSUBSCRIPTIONS?\b`, `\bDISCOUNT\w*`, `\bCOMM?ISS?IONS?\b`, `\bCOMPENSATION\b`, `\bEXPENSES?\b`, `\bAFFILIATE\b`, `\bPERSONAL\b`, `\bCLOSING\b`, `\bSCF\b`, `\bSUPPLY CHAIN\b`, `\bEARLY PAY(?:MENT)?\b`, `\bALLOWANCES?\b`, `\bSHORTAGES?\b`, `\bRMA\b`, and, in the entry fields only, `\bFLOOR ?PLAN\b`, `\bFLOORPLAN\b`, `\bVIN\b`, `\bEQUIP\w*`.

**Verified** (method `named_payer_repeats`, `named_payer_company_form` or `public_or_healthcare_payer`) when any of these holds:
- (a) the payer repeats (§5.2) and at least one of its credits is not a `PPD` or `WEB` entry. A consumer entry never verifies by repetition alone (structural S50);
- (b) the payer name prints a company form;
- (c) the payer is a government payer (§5.2, with §7.6's patterns and every veto) or a healthcare payer (§7.7) whose row prints none of `REIMB`, `MEMBER`, `MBR`, `SUBSCRIBER` or `PREMIUM`. Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (Q12): the seven no-purpose forms of step 3a (§6.1) are decided before arms A and B and before Q6; a purpose (`VENDOR PAY`, `PROV PAY`, `RMR IV`, a `PMT INFO` invoice, a VA entry code) keeps them here.

**Guard:** no posted debit in the same statement shares the payer's first distinctive word (§7.5). A payer that is also debited is held as `payer_also_debited`, and one debited as a lender is held as `payer_debited_as_lender` (§8.1).

**Otherwise** the row is `counted_flagged` / `named_payer_one_off`.

Lenders are decided `non_revenue` earlier (D1 and the potential registry), unregistered ones are held (T4), insurers are `non_revenue` or held (T14, `insurer_named_payer`), and the holder is held. That is Q6's "lenders, insurers and the holder never count," except an insurer paying for the business's work (§8.1, the underwriter's Q2 of 2026-10-02): counted and flagged, never verified and never a repeat.

### 8.7 Q7: an auto lender paying a dealer

At step 4 (§6.1), a credit is `verified_revenue` (method `auto_lender_dealer_funding`, source type `auto_dealer_funding`, confidence 0.90) when its payer, read on the originator segment (`_originator_segment`, never a receiver or memo field), is an auto lender, and one of these holds:
- **the listed-lender arms.** The payer is a listed auto lender: a `vehicle_financing` registry entity, or an entry of `DEALER_FUNDING_PAYERS` (registry, new: Westlake Financial (never Westlake Flooring), United Auto Credit, Strike Acceptance, PFS, Suncoast Credit Union, CU Direct / CUDL, Credit Acceptance, Exeter, Flagship Credit, GLS, Santander Consumer, Chrysler Capital, GM Financial, Toyota Financial, Honda Financial, Nissan Motor Acceptance, CarMax Auto Finance, Ally, American Credit Acceptance, Regional Acceptance, Nicholas Financial, Lendbuzz).
