And the row prints either:
  - dealer-specific funding words: `\bVHCL PURCH\w*`, `\bVEHICLE PURCHASE\b`, `\bDEAL ?FUND\w*`, `\bFUNDLOAN\b`, `\bDEALER (?:FUND\w*|FND|PMT|PAY\w*)\b`, `\bDLR PMT\b`, `\bAUTODLRPMT\b`, `\bCONTRACT FUND\w*`, `\bVADMIN FEE\b`; or
  - `\bPAYABLES\b`, `\bTRADE PAY\w*` or `\bACCT FUND\w*`.
- **the credit-union arm.** Credit unions fund dealers' indirect auto loans through CU Direct (CUDL) and print their own name with the entry `VHCL PURCH`. The payer region names a credit union (`\bCU\b`, `\bCREDIT UNION\b`, `\bFCU\b`) or CU Direct / CUDL; the entry field is `\bVHCL PURCH(?:ASE)?\b` (Chase's glued `VHCL PURCHSEC` is split by the revenue text, §7.0); and the statement holds two or more such credits. A single one can be a member's own purchase loan paid into the member's account, so it is held as `financing_named_payer`. Because it needs the statement, this arm is decided in statement pass 7 (§6.2), before the Q5 and Q6 verifications: step 4 leaves such a row `unverified_deposit` (method `credit_union_vehicle_purchase`), and the pass verifies it with method `auto_lender_dealer_funding` when the count is met. Audit fix batch B7 (I36, §20): a credit union's glued acronym (one to three letters before `CU` or `FCU`, one word: `BECU`, `SECU`, `PSECU`, `GECU`, `DCU`) names a credit union too; and once the arm verifies a statement's VHCL PURCH credits, the same credit union's other dealer-funding entries (its `VADMIN FEE`, the same deal's admin fee), or another credit union's entry that prints a verified credit's deal ID (Chase's `IND ID`), verify with them, under the same refusals; a credit union's entry beside no verified VHCL PURCH credit stays held.

Q7 never fires when any of these holds:
- the row matches a D1 entity outside the vehicle-financing group, a potential lender or an insurer (`KAPITUS DES:CONTRACT FUNDING`, `ONDECK CAPITAL DES:DEAL FUND`, `GEICO DES:VEHICLE PURCHASE`);
- the row prints `\bLOANS?\b`, `\bPROCEEDS\b`, `\bADVANCES?\b`, `\bADV\b`, `\bMCA\b`, `\bCASH ADV\w*` or a refund word (`REFUND`, `RFND`, `REFND`, `RFD`, `RETURN`, `RTN`, `REVERSAL`, `RVSL`, `CHARGEBACK`, `CHBK`) (`SUNCOAST CREDIT UNION DES:VHCL PURCH LOAN PROCEEDS`);
- the channel gate (§6.1 step 9b) closes the row.

**Payables need dealer evidence (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q9 (c'); audit round 2, R2-OW05).** A listed lender's credit read on a payables word alone (PAYABLES, TRADE PAY, ACCT FUND) verifies only on a statement with dealer evidence: a Q7 credit with a dealer-specific word, or the credit-union arm; a floor-plan financier's row, or FLOOR PLAN; a purchase at a dealer-only auction; a dealer word in the holder's name, unless the name also prints RECOVERY, REPO, REPOSSESS, TOWING or COLLATERAL. Otherwise it is `counted_flagged` / `lender_paid_for_services` (Q9 (2026-10-02)), held under the hidden-loan guard. (The arms are narrowed by audit round 3, R3-B14: R3-52, §20 below: a floor-plan financier's credit only where it prints no service wording, the floor-plan form by its own words only, and an auction purchase never by card.) In detail:
- **The payables-only credit** (`_payables_only_dealer_funding`): step 4's listed-lender arm, whose word is a payables word, not a dealer-specific one (`dealer_funding_reading` reads a dealer-specific word first, so `PAYABLES DEALER PAY` is dealer-specific).
- **The dealer evidence** (`_dealer_contract_evidence`, read once per statement in pass 7, beside the business shape): the statement's dealer activity (`_dealer_activity`, the shared core R2-OW06's Q11 reads too): a credit of the statement that is a credit union's `VHCL PURCH` (verified by the credit-union arm or a lone one, method `credit_union_vehicle_purchase`) or a Q7 credit that is not payables-only; a posted debit of a floor-plan financier, or a posted credit of one that prints no service wording (classification `floor_plan_financing`, the registry's `FLOOR_PLAN_ALIASES`, or a floor-plan form, `_FLOOR_PLAN_FORM`: `FLOORPLAN(S)`, `FLOOR PLAN(S)` or `FLOOR PLANNING`, and the glued words a narrow field prints, `FLOORPLANINT`, `FLOORPLANPAYOFF`, `FLOORPLANADV` and `FLOORPLANXPRESS` (R3-B14 review round 1, finding 6, §20), never `FLOORPLANNER` or `FLOOR PLANKS`; the service wording, `_FLOOR_PLAN_SERVICE_CREDIT`, read without the receiver field's value and without the holder's names (the latter by R3-B14 review round 1, finding 4, §20: `without_receiver_and_holder`, so a dealer advance whose unlabelled receiver is the holder's own name printing `RECOVERY`, `TRANSPORT` or `COMMISSIONS` stays evidence): a vendor payment, `REPO`, `REPOS`, `REPOSSESS…`, `RECOVER…`, a tow, `TRANSPORT…`, `INSPECT…` or a commission, so a financier's `VENDOR PAY` or `REPO FEE` credit is no evidence, while a VIN-bearing dealer advance, `FPX … FLOORPLAN XPRESS ADVANCE`, still is); a posted debit naming a dealer-only wholesale auction that is no card purchase (`WHOLESALE_AUCTION_REFUND_NAMES`: Manheim, ACV Auctions, OPENLANE or BACKLOT CARS: an ACH, wire or check purchase there; never a card purchase, `_card_purchase_debit`: class `pos` or R2-B02's card forms, `CHECKCARD …` or `POS PURCHASE … MANHEIM PA` in the auction's town; the card forms' `<ST> USA|CAN` tail, Found's and Bluevine's card charge, is no card purchase on a row that prints a wire, ACH or check form, `OUTGOING WIRE <auction> ATLANTA GA USA`, by R3-B14 review round 1, finding 5, §20) (rewritten by audit round 3, R3-B14: R3-52, §20 below); or a dealer's name on one of the holder's names (a vehicle or equipment noun before `SALES`, `DEALER`, `DEALERSHIP`, `MART`, `OUTLET`, `EXCHANGE` or `SUPERSTORE`, or `MOTORS`, `AUTOMOTIVE`, `AUTO GROUP`, `AUTO PLAZA`, `AUTO MALL`, `DEALERSHIP`, `CAR LOT`) that prints no recovery, repossession, towing or collateral word. A payables-only Q7 credit is no dealer evidence (a repossession agency's own payables would make its statement a dealer's), nor is a §7.8 auction payout credit (it is Q11's evidence only).
- **The demotion.** In pass 7's tier loop, after the factoring, the holder's own push and the lease-to-own financier's demotions, a Verified payables-only Q7 credit on a statement with no dealer evidence leaves verification (`_lender_service_never_verified`: state `unverified_deposit`, method `lender_paid_for_services`, rule `q7_payables_without_dealer_evidence`, confidence 0.50, no source type; its reason names the lender and its alias, says the statement shows no dealer evidence and that the ruling overrules `auto_lender_dealer_funding`). It is `counted_flagged` / `lender_paid_for_services`, or `excluded_pending_review` / `financing_named_payer` when the lender also collects from the account.
- **The hidden-loan guard** (`_payer_collects`): a lender or financing debit names the payer (`payer_debited_as_lender`'s reading, with the pass-7 prefix), or any other posted debit names it by the B4 forms, 5.6's first word or a cut or glued spelling; only the bank's receiving fee and a card charge are ignored. It reads more broadly than `payer_also_debited` (no bill, processor-fee, settlement or payout-pair exemption, no amount or recurrence test): a documented over-hold of the owner's "collecting loan payments".
- **What stays.** The transaction side (classification `other`, match method `auto_lender_dealer_funding`, the lender's name and every lender flag) is unchanged, so lender credits and eligible deposits do not move; Q7's dealer-specific words, credit-union arm and vetoes are unchanged; a dealer's payables on a statement with dealer evidence stay Verified; a registered lender's other credits stay financing proceeds. A real dealer whose statement shows none of the evidence (no floor plan, no dealer-worded Q7 credit, no auction purchase and no dealer word in its name), or whose name prints RECOVERY or REPO, loses Verified but stays in True, flagged. Audit round 3, R3-B14 (R3-52, §20; Q9 (c), "a lender paying a business for services counts as 'lender paid for services', never verified. The hidden-loan guard stays"): a card purchase in an auction's town, a floor-plan financier's service credit, a `FLOORPLANNER` subscription or a `FLOOR PLANKS` purchase is no dealer evidence, so a repossession agency's payables beside one is `lender_paid_for_services`, or held as `financing_named_payer` where the lender also debits the account; an ACH, wire or check purchase at the auction, a floor-plan financier's debit and a dealer advance credit still keep a dealer's payables Verified. Q11 (b)'s `_dealer_statement` reads the same arms, so a non-dealer's asset sale beside such a row is `non_revenue` / `asset_sale_proceeds`.
- **Q9's other parts (R2-OW09).** A lender that no Q7 arm reads and T4's root holds, paying the business on a line that prints invoice, payables, vendor-payment or commission wording, is released by §8.1's Q9 release as `lender_paid_for_services` under the same guard. A registered lender's credit that prints such wording (`GM FINANCIAL DES:VENDOR PMT` to a repossession agency) is D1's financing proceeds before either reading, while the same lender's `PAYABLES` there counts as `lender_paid_for_services`: releasing it would move the lender-credit exclusion (a G7 move), so it waits for the owner (§17.1).

A reversal marker still wins, because step 3 runs first. Any other credit from a listed auto lender stays financing: D1 makes it `non_revenue` / financing proceeds. S1 admits the `DEALER_FUNDING_PAYERS` lenders the ledger lacks into its vehicle-financing group, through the ledger's process. Until a lender is admitted, its credits that Q7 does not verify are held as `financing_named_payer`, whether or not its name carries a financing root; so is any row printing a dealer-funding word that Q7 did not verify (`FABRIKAM MERCHANT FUNDING DES:DEAL FUNDING`), except (audit fix batch B7, I36, §20) a wire whose purpose alone prints it from a named non-lender sender (§8.1). A dealer-funding credit is not financing proceeds, so it leaves `lender_credits` and returns to eligible deposits (an intended move).

Measured on the memo's rows: the first draft's arms (dealer wording alone) reached $4.02M, 214 rows, 11 statements. The revised rule keeps all of it: the listed-lender arms $0.37M (150 rows, 8 statements) and the credit-union arm the other $3.64M (64 rows, 4 statements of one dealer, 15 to 18 such credits in each). The corpus holds no dealer-worded credit from an unlisted, non-credit-union payer, so the tightening removes only the fabricated false positives the review built. Tryout host: $0.56M, one used-car dealer (not re-measured; the census restates it).

### 8.8 Q8: payroll and salary

`payroll_or_salary` (§8.1) is held, whoever the payer is. A payroll credit from the holder is `holder_name`. `DES:BONUS`, `DES:PAYRL`, Wells Fargo's `… DIR DEP …` to a person and an employer's `EXP REIMB` are held here, and (audit fix batch B5, I37, §20) on TD Canada Trust's statements a row whose last word is the Payments Canada payroll code `PAY` (the 200 family; `PAIE` was already read); a US row's trailing `PAY` is its own word. Audit fix batch B7 (I09, §20): a bare direct-deposit word is pay wording only with a sign of a person's pay (§8.1); a company's direct deposit to a business is its payer's credit.

### 8.9 Everything else

- A registry match that did not verify: `counted_flagged` / `platform_unconfirmed`.
- A factoring payee's credit: `counted_flagged` / `factoring_payout`. It keeps its Factoring flag. The owner deferred its Verified status (2026-09-26).
- A credit from `PAYOUT_CREDIT_ENTITIES`: `counted_flagged` / `payout_credit_entity`.
- **Lease-to-own and patient financiers (owner ruling 2026-10-02, Q8).** A credit from a lease-to-own or patient financier (`CUSTOMER_FINANCING_PAYERS`: Snap Finance, Koalafi, Acima, Progressive Leasing, Katapult, Cherry, Terrace Finance, Wisetack; each a ledger entity) is claimed as a payout entity's row is (§8.1) when all of these hold: the financier is read as the payer region; the channel is ACH, wire or other; the amount is $1 or more; the row prints no consumer-side word (OQ2's) and no legal-settlement word (`BREACH`, `LITIGAT…`, `CLASS ACTION`); the row prints no non-sale or financing word (audit round 3, R3-B14: R3-06, §8.1's claim convention, `_payout_non_sale`: an advance, capital, interest, a dividend or a rebate, read without the receiver field's value and the holder's names); and the row is not a consumer (PPD or WEB) entry to a person who is not the holder. A bare `CHERRY` is Cherry only when the whole payer region is `CHERRY` plus company or entry words; `KATAPULT ENGINEERING` and `KATAPULT PRO` are a namesake, and so is every cut form of Katapult Engineering's name (audit round 3, R3-B14: R3-54, §20: `KATAPULT ENG…`, read `(?<![A-Z])KATAPULT\b(?! (?:ENG\w*|PRO)\b)` in `CUSTOMER_FINANCING_PAYERS` and `CUSTOMER_FINANCING_NAMES`: `KATAPULT ENGINEE`, the 16-character ACH company field, `KATAPULT ENG`, `KATAPULT ENGIN`, `KATAPULT ENGINEERIN`); `SNAP LOAN FUNDING` is Snap's payout only in its merchant form (§6.3 narrowing 12). It is `counted_flagged` / `customer_financing_payout`. It is never verified: an earlier rule's verification is overruled, method `customer_financing_payer`. It never counts toward a Q5 or Q6 repeat, and neither does any row that names one of them (`CUSTOMER_FINANCING_NAMES`, read without the receiver field's value). A large one-off lump sum is held as `customer_financing_lump_sum` until sourced:
  - Large: $10,000 or more, and an incoming wire, a whole multiple of $1,000, or at least half the statement's posted credits (non-revenue included, the T7 base).
  - One-off: the financier pays fewer than three payouts in the statement of at least half its amount, itself included; read over every payout at once, so a pair of lumps holds both.
  - Basis: $10,000 sits above every lease-to-own ticket ($3,500 to $7,500) and every ordinary corpus payout; a series of similar-size payouts is ordinary business and is counted.
  - A financier's credit whose claim §8.1's non-sale or financing veto lifted and that the rules counted (an abbreviated advance, `ADVNC`, `ADVN` or `ADVC`, which no hold reads) is read here as that financier's payout (`_vetoed_financier`: the financier read without the veto), in the one-off count too, as it was read before the veto (audit round 3, R3-B14 review round 1, finding 2, §20), so a large one-off advance stays held until sourced, while a small one or a series of three is counted (never verified, its counted reason kept); a payout entity's credit (OQ2), which no lump-sum test reads, is not one.
  - Holds and debits: the claim skips the counter-debit holds as OQ2's do: for Cherry, an alternative position, that includes `payer_debited_as_lender`. Their debits keep their groups (Leases & rentals; Cherry an alternative position; a bare `CHERRY`, `WISETACK` or `TERRACE FINANCE` debit stays other). Cherry Technologies joins `PAYOUT_CREDIT_ENTITIES` and the classifier's OQ2 veto, so a `CHERRY TECHNOLOGIES` or `CHERRYPAY` merchant credit leaves D1 and its consumer-side credit keeps D1; so does (audit round 3, R3-B14: R3-06, §20) a Cherry loan or advance, a credit printing `LOAN(S)` or a non-sale or financing word (`CHERRY TECHNOLOGIES DES:LOAN`, `CHERRYPAY DES:LOAN DISB`, `CHERRY TECHNOLOGIES DES:ADVANCE`: financing proceeds, entity Cherry, its lender-credit exclusion on).
- A numbered company: `counted_flagged` / `numbered_company_payer` (T11).
- A named payer that Q5 or Q6 refused on a verification-only word: `counted_flagged` / `named_payer_purpose_refused`.
- A named payer on a row with no electronic-payment form (fintech exports, S51): `counted_flagged` / `named_payer_unlabelled`. It is never verified in this release. The census reports how much of it would pass Q6's test. Audit fix batch B5 (I37, §20): TD Canada Trust's trailing CPA code (`AP`, `MSP`, `BPY`, `APY`) is an electronic-payment form (§5.2), so its named payers reach Q6; the US layouts that print an originator and an entry but no ACH word (Wells Fargo, First Citizens, Found, Huntington, Truist, Mission Valley) stay here, an owner question (I37).
- A numbered company (§5.2) is no longer read from a payment reference printed before a named payer (audit fix batch B5, I59, §20).
- No payer word at all: `counted_flagged` / `no_payer_printed`.

### 8.10 Tiering order and thresholds

A Verified credit keeps its tier unless the pass overrules its verification, in this order: a factoring payer's (§8.9, `factoring_payout`), the holder's own push (§8.1, `holder_name`; audit round 2, R2-B04), a lease-to-own or patient financier's (Q8 of 2026-10-02, §8.9, `customer_financing_payout`; audit round 3, R3-B14: R3-06, never a credit printing a non-sale or financing word, which no financier claims, so a descriptor's verification of it stands), a listed auto lender's payables-only credit on a statement with no dealer evidence (Q9 (c') of 2026-10-02, §8.7: `lender_paid_for_services`, or `financing_named_payer` under the hidden-loan guard; R2-OW05; the evidence's arms narrowed by audit round 3, R3-B14: R3-52), and a non-dealer's sale of a vehicle or heavy equipment that an invoice or customer-payment descriptor verified, on a statement with no dealer evidence (Q11 (b) of 2026-10-02, §8.1: `non_revenue` / `asset_sale_proceeds`; R2-OW06), and a builder's progress draw that an earlier rule verified (Q11 (a) of 2026-10-02, §8.1: `counted_flagged` / `construction_progress_draw`; R2-OW06 review round 1). Before all of them, before the repeats are counted, a settlement under the merchant's own name that an earlier rule verified and that only the bare settlement word lifted from the row-alone own-push test leaves verification (§8.1 `holder_name`, R3-90 part A: counted, never verified; method `holder_named_settlement`, rule `holder_named_settlement_never_verified`; audit round 3, R3-B10 review round 2): it is read as an unverified credit, so a later hold still names it, and where none does it is `counted_flagged` / `named_payer_purpose_refused`. Last, after the $1 floor, a credit into a premium trust account leaves verification (Q10 of 2026-10-02: `excluded_pending_review` / `premium_trust_account`, below; R2-OW11). Every one of these demotions leaves a credit under $1 to the floor, which holds it with its own method, rule and sentence (audit round 3, R3-B15: R3-63, §20; the factoring and progress-draw arms now read the floor as the holder's-push arm did). A hold that re-tiers a counted re-statement (the Q2 release a later hold names, Q8's lump sum, Q9 (c')'s hidden-loan guard, the premium-trust hold, the floor on a counted or demoted unverified credit) names itself in the row's reason sentence, never "counted and flagged" (audit round 3, R3-B15: R3-53, §5.3, §20).

For each unverified posted credit the pass takes the first that applies:
1. `direction_conflict`
2. `insurer_payer`
3. `insurer_named_payer`
4. `possible_return`
5. `financing_named_payer`
6. `payer_debited_as_lender`
7. `holder_name`
8. `payroll_or_salary`
9. `personal_income`
10. `non_sale_purpose`
11. `payer_also_debited`; then (audit fix batch B4) a payroll provider's tax-service credit as `non_sale_purpose`; then, past the holds (and audit fix batch B2's named sender after an own-account designation, held as `transfer_account_designation`) and before the wires, an insurer paid for the business's work (`insurer_paid_for_services`, the underwriter's Q2 of 2026-10-02, §8.1: the release's method, which only holds 4 to 11 and that designation hold precede; on a person-to-person row §8.4's round-sum repeat still wins, as for the progress draw (audit round 3, R3-B13: R3-09, §20), the row falling to step 17 as `p2p_round_repeat`; inserted here rather than renumbered, as Q8's and Q11's tiers were, so step 26 keeps its number), a factoring payer's payout (`factoring_payout`, A3-H: `FACTORING_PAYOUT_PAYERS`) and a lease-to-own or patient financier's payout (`customer_financing_payout`, Q8 of 2026-10-02, §8.9); then a builder's progress draw (`construction_progress_draw`, Q11 (a) of 2026-10-02, §8.1: any channel but Zelle; a bare transfer's and an account designation's holds and Q4's round-sum repeat still win)
12. wires (§8.5: `wire_no_sender`, `wire_named_sender` or `named_payer_purpose_refused`)
13. `transfer_no_counterparty` (before the check and branch tiers, so `TELLER TRANSFER` is held)
14. `transfer_account_designation`
15. `check_deposit`
16. cash, branch, ATM (`no_payer_printed`)
17. person-to-person and named transfers (`p2p_round_repeat`, or `p2p`)
18. `platform_unconfirmed`
19. `factoring_payout` (a credit the classifier reads as factoring)
20. `payout_credit_entity`
21. `numbered_company_payer`
22. `named_payer_purpose_refused`
23. `named_payer_one_off`
24. `named_payer_unlabelled`
25. `no_payer_printed` (audit fix batch B10: `payer_text_not_read` on a row the parser marked as read only by its label, here only; B10 review round 1: never at 16, where the cash, branch, teller or ATM label says the statement printed no payer; audit round 2, R2-B07: `unread_run_names_financing`, held, where that row's unread payer text prints a lender's or a lending bank's block, §8.2)

The Q9 relabel (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q9; §8.1; R2-OW09), last, after step 25's unread branch: a credit the financing-root release lifted (`finance_named_customer`, `lessor_rent` or `lender_paid_for_services`) that steps 12 to 25 count takes the release's reason in place of theirs. Held reasons, `payer_text_not_read` and the kept reasons (`numbered_company_payer`, `factoring_payout`, `payout_credit_entity`, `platform_unconfirmed`, `customer_financing_payout`, `construction_progress_draw`, `insurer_paid_for_services`, `lender_paid_for_services`) win. Such a credit is never verified and never counts toward a Q5 or Q6 repeat; the asset-sale override and the Zelle step (26) still read it after.

Each row's tier taken (owner ruling 2026-10-02, Q11 (b); §8.1): a row the steps above count, or one IAA's insurer-name hold alone holds (no later hold would name it; R2-OW06 review round 1), that the asset-sale reading reads on a statement with no dealer evidence becomes `non_revenue` / `asset_sale_proceeds`; every other hold keeps it held.

After the tiers (owner ruling 2026-10-02, Q8; §8.9), a one-off lump sum among the `customer_financing_payout` rows, the verified ones the pass overruled included, is held as `customer_financing_lump_sum`; then the Zelle policy (26) and the $1 floor.

26. Then, in the stored reading, after every step above and before the $1 floor, the Zelle policy (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q3; §8.4): a Zelle deposit the steps above verified, counted or held is `non_revenue` / `zelle_excluded`, its reading kept; the floor and every later step skip it (it is `non_revenue`). The step runs in the stored (No) reading; the counted reading skips it and the two lifted carve-outs (the owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3, R2-OW17; §8.1, §8.4), and its later steps read the counted tiers.

Then, after the $1 floor, the premium-trust hold (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q10, "Hold every deposit into an account titled "premium trust""; §2.1, §9.1; R2-OW11). On a statement whose account title reads PREMIUM TRUST (`premium_trust_title` over `Statement.account_title`, `account_name`, `holder_name`: the title at the field's end, the title followed by an account word, or the title and an account or product word followed by a separator), every verified or counted posted credit is held as `premium_trust_account`. A verified one leaves verification (method `premium_trust_account`, rule `premium_trust_account_title`, its reason naming the rule it overruled). A held one keeps its first hold, and a non-revenue one stays non-revenue. In detail:
- The rule reads the statement's own fields in order: the bank's designation (`account_title`, R2-OW10) in any of the three forms (never the words anywhere: a trade name the holder reader dropped after a legal form, `PREMIUM TRUST ROOFING`, is no title); then the account name, then the holder's name, each in the end form, in the account-word form only when the field does not end in a legal form (`PREMIUM TRUST ACCOUNT LLC` is a company), in the for-benefit form even when it does (audit round 3, R3-B11: R3-65, §20: the words and an account word before `FBO`, `F/B/O`, `OF` or `FOR` and a name, `PREMIUM TRUST ACCOUNT FBO NORTHWIND AGENCY LLC`, the legal form being the beneficiary's; R3-B11 review round 1, finding 3, §20: a product adjective may print before the account word, `PREMIUM TRUST BUSINESS ACCOUNT FBO NORTHWIND LLC`), and in the separator form even when it does (`PREMIUM TRUST ACCOUNT - NORTHWIND INSURANCE AGENCY LLC`). The words are whole (`PREM`, `PREMIUM` or `PREMIUMS`, then `TRUST` or `TRST`, a dot after either allowed; never `TRUSTEE` or `SUPREMIUM`; audit round 3, R3-B11: R3-65, §20: `FUND` or `FUNDS` may print between them, `PREMIUM FUND TRUST ACCOUNT`, a bank's product name for the same account); a product adjective (`BUSINESS`, `ANALYZED`, `COMMERCIAL`) may print before a kind word or the account word (R3-65: `PREMIUM TRUST BUSINESS CHECKING`), never alone (`PREMIUM TRUST BUSINESS` is no title); the separator form needs an account or product word (never `FUND`, `FUNDS` or a bare title before a dash). It never reads a row, so a payer that prints the words makes no title. A holder line's contact whose words are the premium-trust designation itself (`ATTN: PREMIUM TRUST ACCOUNT`, glued or spaced, `C/O`, `CARE OF` after the name's legal form) is the account's title (audit round 3, R3-B11: R3-61, §20); a contact naming a person or a department never is. (Amended by R3-B11 review round 1, findings 1 and 2, §20 below: the designation a contact's words must be is this rule's own title at a field's end, read from the contact's first word, so kind words (`ATTN:PREMIUM TRUST CHECKING`, `ATTN: PREMIUM TRUST BUSINESS CHECKING`), the bare words (`ATTN: PREMIUM TRUST`) and a reference (`… ACCOUNT (1234)`, `… ACCOUNT II`) read too, and a reference's marker the address cut leaves dangling (`ACCT # 1234 PO BOX …` read as `ACCT #`) is dropped; `PREMIUM TRUST OPERATING`, an adjective alone, a department and any other word after the designation still never read. `CARE OF` is a contact only right after the name's legal form or the designation printed right after it.) Recorded false negatives (each overstates True: the trust account's deposits stay counted), absent from the corpus (audit round 3, R3-B11: R3-65 and R3-30, §20, which relabel them; R2-OW11 called them the safe direction): `PREM. TR. ACCT.`, a bare title before a separator (`PREMIUM TRUST - CONTOSO AGENCY LLC`), `PREMIUM TRUST OPERATING`; a statement whose parser reads no holder line publishes no account title (62 routes, 452 re-parsed statements at 1a761de; the True card says so on each holder-unscreened statement); a title printed on its own line under the name on a layout whose text keeps the lines apart (not seen in the corpus, whose extracted text joins these blocks); a holder line's contact that prints a name before the words (`CARE OF NORTHWIND PREMIUM TRUST ACCOUNT`) or any other word after the designation (`ATTN: PREMIUM TRUST ACCOUNT - NORTHWIND`), which the readers publish as no title (R3-B11 review round 1, finding 2, §20). Recorded over-reads (each understates True, held and reviewable): a trade name that prints the words and an account word (`PREMIUM TRUST ACCOUNT SERVICES`, `PREMIUM TRUST ACCT MGMT`, `NORTHWIND PREMIUM TRUST ACCOUNT SERVICES` as a holder with no legal form, a company named `PREMIUM TRUST ACCOUNT OF <place> LLC`, or with a product adjective before the account word, `PREMIUM TRUST BUSINESS ACCOUNT OF <place> LLC`, R3-B11 review round 1, finding 3).
- The hold follows every step: the Q5, Q6 and Q7 verifications, the demotions, the insurer-for-work release (the underwriter's Q2: a carrier's commission it counts on a trust account is held here), the customer-financing lump sum, the Zelle step and the floor. Q5's and Q6's repeat counts are unchanged. A cash, branch, ATM or bare deposit into a premium trust account is held for the title, not for being cash.
- The agency's operating, producer-payable, wire and Lloyd's-titled accounts, a credit union's checking beside an empty premium-trust share, a `PREMIUM BUSINESS` product, an IOLTA or escrow account and a family trust read as before.

Holds 2 to 11 are §8.1's; the owner's own holds (Q2, Q4, Q5, Q8 and the holder) are among them or in tiers 12 to 17.

| Threshold | Value | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Repeats | 2 or more credits, same payer, one statement | §5.2, Q5, Q6 |
| Round sum | at least $100, a whole multiple of $100 | §5.2, Q4 |
| Round-sum repeat | 2 or more round sums from one sender, rails and named transfers alike | §8.4 |
| Credit-union dealer funding | 2 or more `VHCL PURCH` credits from credit unions in the statement | §8.7 |
| Operating recurrence | 3 or more credits, or 2 on a business account (a legal-form holder counts) | §7.0 |
| Micro-deposit floor | under $1 never verifies and never counts | §7.0, §7.8, §7.10 |
| NET SETTLE from an unregistered originator | 3 or more credits | §7.1 |
| Auction refund window | 14 days, equal amount, one debit each | §7.8 |
| Package gate | held credits at least 10% of all posted credits, non-revenue included, in integer cents (`REVENUE_REVIEW_HELD_SHARE`) | T7 |
| Customer-financing lump sum | $10,000 or more and a wire, a whole $1,000 multiple or at least 50% of the statement's posted credits (`CUSTOMER_FINANCING_LUMP_FLOOR`, `CUSTOMER_FINANCING_LUMP_ROUND`, `CUSTOMER_FINANCING_LUMP_SHARE`) | §8.9 |
| Customer-financing series | 3 or more payouts from one financier in the statement, each at least 50% of the row's amount (not one-off) (`CUSTOMER_FINANCING_SERIES_MIN`, `CUSTOMER_FINANCING_SERIES_SHARE`) | §8.9 |
| Insurer for work | 3 or more eligible credits from one insurer key within an inclusive 31-day span (date[i+2] - date[i] ≤ 30 days; the span slides across a calendar month's edge; an undated credit counts as inside), one statement; a loose trade word needs 2 or more eligible insurer credits in the statement (`INSURER_FOR_WORK_MIN_CREDITS`, `INSURER_FOR_WORK_WINDOW_DAYS`, `INSURER_FOR_WORK_LOOSE_MIN_CREDITS`; the Q2 card's checker measured 3 groups, 9 rows, $19,110.19 on the first card's rows that no calendar month holds, not re-measured under the revision) | §8.1 |

Each threshold is one named integer constant ($1 as `1`, $100 as `100`, 10% as `10`). The classification thresholds live in `analysis/transaction_classifier.py`. The gate's `REVENUE_REVIEW_HELD_SHARE` lives in `analysis/revenue.py`, which the metrics and the webapp both import.

## 9. The data contract

### 9.1 Per account (`report_to_dict` / `rebuild_serialized_revenue_views`)

- **Rows:** every `statement.transactions[].classification` carries `revenue_tier`, `revenue_initial_tier`, `revenue_tier_reason` and the flags of §5.4 (5.6). Audit fix batch B9 (I13, §20): and the statement's `holder_name`, beside `account_name`. The underwriter's Q1 (2026-10-02; R2-OW12, §20): and `revenue_funding_series` (§5.4), a list of objects, empty on every row but a held `wire_no_sender` credit; it rides in every copy of the record (the classifications, the evidence lists, the package ledger, the evidence JSON cells of the exports and the JSON download), and the posted-credit export table gains no column. The underwriter's Q5 (2026-10-02; R2-OW13, §20): and, right after `settlement_reversal`, `returned_funder_payment_by` (on a confirmed funder's payment returned unpaid, the return credit's location) and `returns_funder_payment` (on that credit, the payment's location), `null` on every other row. The owner's answer of 2026-10-07 to audit round 3's R3-73 (R3-B02, §20): and, right after `returns_funder_payment`, `represented_by` (on a returned payment the same funder re-debited, out of the withholding rate, the re-debit's location), `null` on every other row. The owner's answer of 2026-10-07 to audit round 3's R3-79 (R3-B03, §11, §20): and, right after `represented_by`, `lump_sum_payoff` (on a confirmed funder's paid debit whose own text prints a payoff word, the word as the bank printed it: the debit is out of the withholding rate, in paid to lenders and the lender count), `null` on every other row, a payoff attempt the bank returned and a duplicate included.
- **Transactions:** audit fix batch B10 (I05, I60, §20): `statement.transactions[].payer_text_unread` is `true` on a credit whose parser published only its own label because it could not read the payer the statement printed (§8.2); the key is written only where it is set, so no other transaction gains a key, and it is not part of the extraction response schema (the extractor is told nothing new). Audit round 2, R2-B07 (R07, §20): `statement.transactions[].unread_payer_text` is, on a credit the counted core-processor template marked at a welded flush, that flush's joined text (several rows' payer blocks, never proven this row's, so never its description); written only where it is set and kept out of the extraction response schema, as `payer_text_unread` is.
- **Statement:** audit fix batch B9 (I13, §20): `statement.holder_name` is the holder's name the parser read from the header or the mailing block (Chase, First Citizens, TD Bank, Truist, PNC, Navy Federal, TD Canada Trust; audit round 2, R2-B05: R04 part 2, page 1's mailing address of Bank of America, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank, RBC and Banque Royale, Scotiabank, Bluevine, Huntington, Capital One, CIBC, Square, Mission Valley, BMO's US activity layout, Santander, Citibank and TD Canada Trust's French issue), never the parser's own product (audit fix batch B9 review round 1: PNC's product printed in capitals on its summary title), or `null`; `statement.account_name` keeps the printed product, nickname or name (Chase no longer publishes its summary grid header there). Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q10, its parser half), audit round 2, R2-OW10 (§20): `statement.account_title` is the title the bank prints after the holder's name (a premium trust, an operating, a wire or a producer-payable account), read from the holder reader's own anchor: the words that reader drops after the name it publishes, never other text, and none where it reads no name (audit round 3, R3-B11: R3-61, §20: a contact it drops is never a title, except a contact whose words are the premium-trust designation itself, published as `PREMIUM TRUST ACCOUNT` without its marker in any spacing; R3-B11 review round 1, finding 2, §20: the designation is the premium-trust rule's own title at a field's end, so `PREMIUM TRUST CHECKING`, the bare `PREMIUM TRUST` and a reference are published too, upper case, a dangling reference marker dropped). It is serialized only where it is set, so no other statement gains a key, and it is not part of the extraction response schema (the extractor is told nothing new). It is provenance for the revenue rule (R2-OW11); in R2-OW10 no hold, holder test, tier or figure reads it, and it never enters the holder's names. Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q10), R2-OW11 (§8.10, §20): its one reader is the premium-trust rule (`premium_trust_title`, with the account name and the holder's name), which holds a premium trust account's credits that would count; the holder's names still never read it.
- **Metrics:** unchanged keys keep their meaning. New keys:
  - `true_revenue_total`, `true_revenue_count`;
  - `counted_flagged_total`, `counted_flagged_count`;
  - `excluded_pending_review_total`, `excluded_pending_review_count`;
  - `counted_flagged_by_reason` and `excluded_pending_review_by_reason`, each `{reason: {"count": int, "total": float}}`;
  - audit round 2, R2-OW03 (owner ruling 2026-10-02, §20): `non_revenue_by_reason`, the same shape over the `non_revenue` rows that carry a code `REVENUE_TIER_REASONS` files under `non_revenue` (§5.3: `zelle_excluded`, `government_no_purpose`), a dict of its own, never a slot of the counted or held maps (a reviewer's rejection keeps its counted or held code and is not listed). `compute_metrics` and the rebuild compute it by one rule; it is one of `TIER_METRIC_KEYS`, so a payload analysed before 5.6 has it `None` (§12);
  - `revenue_review_items`, the held count;
  - audit fix batch B9 (I13, §20): `holder_unscreened`, true when no holder's name is known for the statement (no parser `holder_name`, no account name that names a holder, no holder name in the statement's own receiver fields), so the holds that read the holder's name cannot see the holder's own money; the True card and the exports show it in audit batch B11;
  - audit fix batch B10 (I05, §20): `payer_text_unread`, true when more than 30% (`PAYER_TEXT_UNREAD_SHARE`) of the statement's posted credit rows, duplicates aside, carry the parser's 'payer text not read' mark, so its True rests on credits whose payer nobody read; and `payer_text_unread_count`, how many posted credits carry it. A statement integrity fact for the True card (audit batch B11);
  - owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q10), R2-OW11 (§8.10, §20): `premium_trust_account`, true when the statement's printed title reads PREMIUM TRUST (`premium_trust_title` over its account title, account name and holder name), so pass 7 holds every credit a rule verified or counted. A statement fact for the True card and the package (§9.2, §10.1); no figure reads it.

  - owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q5), R2-OW13 (§11, §20): `returned_funder_payment_total`, `returned_funder_payment_count` and `returned_funder_payment_evidence`, the debits that carry `returned_funder_payment_by`. `lender_debits` and `lender_debit_count` stay the paid rows (`contributes_to_lender_totals`, paid to lenders); `withholding_numerator` is every row that `contributes_to_withholding_rate` (paid plus returned, equal to `lender_debits + returned_funder_payment_total` to the cent; it was `lender_debits`); `withholding_formula` reads "abs(paid lender debits + returned funder payments) / withholding basis * 100" and `potential_withholding_formula` "abs(potential_lender_debit_total) / withholding basis * 100"; a note names the returned payments in the statement's currency. `lenders_detected` counts a funder whose every payment bounced (it stays in the lender count).

  - owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q6), R2-OW15 (§6.2's package passes, §20): the served copy (`apply_revenue_view`'s `_served_account`; never stored) adds, each only where its count is above 0, `unmatched_deposit_return_count`, `unmatched_deposit_return_total` and `unmatched_deposit_return_locations` (the debits that undo a deposit, `_deposit_return_debit`, that no credit of the statement pairs) and `processor_chargeback_count`, `processor_chargeback_total` and `processor_chargeback_locations` (a processor's chargebacks and adjustments, `processor_chargeback_debit`), each total the debits' magnitude (`debit_side_flags`, `debit_flag_metrics`). They are flags, never deducted: no figure, tier, gate or lender reading reads them, and a statement without one is served as before.

  - audit round 3, R3-B03 (R3-20; §11, §17.1, §20): `withholding_basis_below_floor`, true where the withholding mode is `true_revenue` or `verified_revenue` and its basis is above $0 and under `WITHHOLDING_BASIS_FLOOR` (500 in the statement's own unit, `REVENUE_REVIEW_HELD_FLOOR`); there `withholding_rate` and `potential_withholding_exposure` are `None`, `withholding_review_required` is set, each `detection.potential_lenders` entry has an `eligible_deposit_denominator` and a `potential_withholding_exposure` of `None`, and a note names the basis and the floor ("withholding rate is unavailable because True revenue (1.00 USD) is under the withholding basis floor (500.00 USD)", and the potential exposure's twin where a potential lender is paid). False everywhere else, the legacy basis always. `compute_metrics` and the review rebuild set it by one helper (`withholding_basis_publishable`). The review rebuild (R3-13) also refreshes, on a True or Verified basis, each `detection.potential_lenders` entry's `eligible_deposit_denominator` and `potential_withholding_exposure` (the basis where a rate is published or where it is $0 or less, `None` under the floor; the entry's debits over the basis) and the two "unavailable" notes of `metrics.notes` (only where it is a list: they leave and the ones the basis reads take the first one's place, or join the end), so `REBUILT_KEYS` gains `metrics.withholding_basis_below_floor` and the two potential lender keys (`metrics.notes` stays out);
  - the owner's answer of 2026-10-07 to audit round 3's R3-79 (R3-B03; §11, §20): `lump_sum_payoff_total` and `lump_sum_payoff_count`, the paid debits that carry `lump_sum_payoff` (in `lender_debits`, out of `withholding_numerator`: the numerator is `lender_debits` + the standing returned payments - `lump_sum_payoff_total`, to the cent), and a note in the statement's unit ("1 lump-sum payment to confirmed lenders (15,000.00 USD): in paid to lenders, not in the withholding rate");
  - the final review of round 2, F1 (§10.4, §11, §20): the served copy (`_served_account`; never stored) publishes `withholding_basis_unestablished: true`, only where the basis the account's withholding mode divides by is not established (`revenue_view.withholding_basis_unestablished`: the `true_revenue` mode where `revenue_established` is false, the `verified_revenue` mode where `verified_revenue_established` is false; a stored mode is read with `normalize_withholding_denominator_mode`, so a payload with none reads the legacy basis, which is never touched). There it nulls `withholding_rate` and `potential_withholding_exposure` (`UNESTABLISHED_WITHHOLDING_KEYS`), sets `withholding_review_required`, and gives each `detection.potential_lenders` entry a `potential_withholding_exposure` and an `eligible_deposit_denominator` of `None`; it keeps `eligible_deposits`, `withholding_denominator` and `potential_withholding_denominator` (the package sums its members' and refuses its own rate on them, M10), which the downloads leave empty (§10.4). The stored analysis keeps its figures.

  `true_revenue` is repointed to `true_revenue_total` (T9). `revenue_review_required` means the gate of T7. `revenue_reconciles` checks the four-tier identity (§5.1). Audit fix batch B11 (I31, §20): the identity is published under its own name, `revenue_tiers_sum_to_posted`, and `revenue_reconciles` stays as its deprecated alias; neither is a reconciliation against the bank's figures (`reconciliation.ok`), and the dashboard no longer reads either as one.
- **Detection:** `true_revenue_evidence` is repointed to verified plus counted. `counted_flagged_evidence` and `excluded_pending_review_evidence` are new. `manual_review` holds the rows whose `revenue_review_required` is set (held rows) plus today's `review_required` rows. Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q5), R2-OW13 (§20): `returned_funder_payments` lists one item per returned funder payment (`funder`, `amount`, `debit_date`, `debit_location`, `credit_date`, `credit_location`, `credit_description`, the return as the bank printed it); each `known_funders` entry adds `returned_payment_count` and `returned_payment_total` (its `debit_count` and `total_debited` stay paid; its `transactions` and `evidence` hold the returned rows too), and a funder whose every payment bounced is listed with `debit_count` 0; `lender_evidence` stays the paid rows. Audit round 3, R3-B02 (the owner's answer of 2026-10-07 to R3-73, §20): an item whose payment the same funder re-debited adds `represented_date`, `represented_location` and `represented_kind` (`re_presented`, the same cents off its cycle, or `caught_up`, an exact 2x); every other item is unchanged. The owner's answer of 2026-10-07 to audit round 3's R3-79 (R3-B03, §20): `lump_sum_payoffs`, after `lender_payment_changes`, lists one item per paid debit carrying `lump_sum_payoff` (`funder`, `amount`, `date`, `location`, `words`, the payoff word as the bank printed it), empty where there is none; each `known_funders` entry keeps it in `debit_count` and `total_debited` (paid).
- **Withholding:** `WITHHOLDING_DENOMINATOR_MODES` gains `true_revenue` (§11).
- **The two Zelle readings (the owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3; R2-OW17, §8.4, §20):**
  - *Stored.* The payload is the stored (No) reading, built exactly as before. An account whose counted (Yes) reading differs carries, after the rebuild, the account key `zelle_counted_reading`: the lean edits that turn the stored account into the counted one (`analysis/zelle_view.py` `reading_edits`). Each edit is `[path, value]` (set) or `[path]` (delete), a path being the dict keys and list indexes into the account; dicts are compared key by key, lists of equal length element by element, anything else is replaced whole. The list is lean: it drops every edit under a path the revenue rebuild writes (`REBUILT_KEYS`: the revenue metrics and their evidence lists, the recomputed withholding figures, the detection evidence and `manual_review`, the `classifications` view and each statement row's contribution flags), because every reading is rebuilt after its edits are applied; and it is exact either way (when the rebuild of the applied lean list is not the counted payload, the full list is stored). The key is written only when the edits are non-empty, so a statement with no Zelle row publishes today's payload byte for byte; `account_content_digest` includes it. `Report.zelle_counted` holds the counted reading on the object (never serialized as itself).
  - *Served* (`apply_zelle_view`, the first step of every served copy; display keys, never stored). The setting's reading is materialised (`reading`: the edits applied and the account rebuilt; an account whose edits cannot be applied is served as stored). An account's **Zelle rows** are its stored reading's posted, non-duplicate credits of method `zelle_deposit_excluded` (the excluded ones and those a reviewer has confirmed since); an account with none is a **legacy** account when a counted, held or verified credit reads the Zelle rail (analysed before the policy, its Zelle natively counted; those credits are its Zelle rows). `metrics.zelle_deposits` = `{counted_as_true_revenue, setting_applied, count, total, by_tier: {tier: {count, total}}}` over the Zelle rows in the reading served (`zelle_deposit_figures`, money rounded as the non-revenue breakdown's); its parts are **in True** (verified plus counted), **held** and **out** (non-revenue). It is served under Yes on every account with Zelle rows, and under No only where today's output would misstate where the Zelle money sits (a Zelle row whose served tier is not `non_revenue`, or `setting_applied` false), so a fresh No analysis is today's payload exactly. `counted_as_true_revenue` is the reading served (a legacy account is served as stored, so true there); `setting_applied` is false under Yes on an account with Zelle rows and no usable edits (analysed between R2-OW02 and R2-OW17), and under No on a legacy account. Under Yes each Zelle row's served transaction carries `zelle_deposit: true` (the owner's "flagged 'Zelle'"), kept in the downloads.

- **Lender payment changes (the owner's request of 2026-10-06; R2-OW18, §20):**
  - *Detection.* `detection.lender_payment_changes`, after `returned_funder_payments`: one item per signal (`kind` `decrease`, `increase`, `cadence_change`, `pause`, `catch_up` (since audit round 3, R3-B05: the owner's answer of 2026-10-07, "Add a 'Caught up' line"), `new_stream` or `stop`; `analysis/lender_payment_changes.py`), ordered confirmed first, then by lender, series, position and date. Every item: `lender` (the canonical entity), `lender_label` (a potential payee's label, else the entity), `lender_state` (`confirmed`, `potential`), `position`, `positions`, `scope` (`statement`). A change: `lender_label_after`, `cadence_before`, `cadence_after`, `amount_before`, `amount_after`, `change_percent` (an integer, on the compared amounts), `cadence_changed`, `schedule_confirmed` (false on a possible change), `weekly_equivalent_before` and `_after` (with `cadence_changed`), `payments_before`, `payments_after`, `last_before_date`, `first_after_date`, `last_after_date`, `restart`, `pause_business_days`, `back_to_earlier`, `reverted`, `reverted_date`, `via` (the unreported levels between the reference and the new level, each with `amount`, `cadence` and `change_percent`, the step into it), `last_step_percent` (with `via`: the step from the last of them to the new level; R2-OW18 review round 1) and `after_funding` (`{date, amount}`: the latest credit of the series' entity in the window of §17.1 (11), never one that returns or reverses a payment, one within 1% of the change's own payment amounts or of a series payment or attempt 0 to 7 days before it, or one dated on or before the first payment of the regime just before the new one; audit round 3, R3-82). A pause: `cadence`, `last_payment_amount`, `last_before_date`, `first_after_date`, `first_after_kind` (what ended it: `payment`, the regime's next payment; `attempt`, a bounced or reversed debit; `other_amount`, a payment of the series at another amount; since audit round 3, R3-25, `catch_up`, a one-off within 2% of exactly 2 to 6 times the payment, which wins over `payment` on the regime's next payment day), `resumed_date` (the regime's next payment; R2-OW18 review round 1), with a catch-up `first_after_amount` and `first_after_multiple` (R3-25), `pause_business_days`, `grace_business_days`, and the notes `larger_debits_inside` (each other one-off of 2x or more dated inside the gap, before the regime's next payment, `{date, amount}`, in date order; R3-25), `catch_ups_inside` (each catch-up after the presence that ended the pause, up to and including the day payments resumed, `{date, amount, multiple}`, in date order: the pause line names it and no Caught up item repeats it; R3-B05 review round 1) and `same_amount_debits` (R3-84, below). A catch-up (`catch_up`, the owner's answer of 2026-10-07 to R3-25): `cadence` (the regime in force), `last_payment_amount` (its amount), `last_before_date` (the position's last paid presence before the catch-up: a payment, a payment-sized one-off or a catch-up), `missed_payments`, `missed_first_date`, `missed_last_date` (the scheduled payments missed in between), `multiple`, `catch_up_date`, `catch_up_amount`. A new stream: `cadence_after` and `amount_after` (its last level, B8), `first_after_date`, `payments_after`, `alongside` (each other stream, `{position, cadence, amount}`, at the level it was paying at the new stream's (P's) first payment), `weekly_total_before` (theirs at P's first payment), `weekly_total_after`, `change_percent` (the 10% gate reads the same totals; audit round 3, R3-81). A stop: `cadence`, `last_payment_date`, `last_payment_amount`, `payments`, `last_presence_date`, `quiet_business_days`, `grace_business_days`, `coverage_end`, `coverage_end_source` (`period_end`, or `last_transaction` where none is printed), `stop_confirmed` (never true inside one statement) and its notes `other_debits_after` (since audit round 3, R3-25, the payment-sized one-offs and the catch-ups after the last payment, with `catch_ups`, the number of catch-ups among them, when there is one), `payoff` (since R3-25, the last one-off of 2x or more after the last payment that is no exact multiple, with `earlier`, the number of such one-offs before it, when there is one), `same_amount_debits` (R3-84, below), `continues_as`, `other_stream_continues`, `last_attempt_returned`, `debt_relief_after`, `new_lender_after`. `same_amount_debits` (audit round 3, R3-84), on a pause or a stop: `{count, first_date, last_date}` of the debits no rule claimed (class `other`) at the series' exact cents, one per day and amount, dated inside the pause's gap or after the stop's last presence, when there are 2 or more, they keep the series' schedule and they cover 60% of the payments the schedule expects there; a stop that carries it is never confirmed; the debits are never presence, a payment or paid to lenders. And `locations` (source locations; a catch-up's `last_before` and `catch_up`). A nested note is absent when not set; no key is named `account`. `detect()` computes it in each Zelle reading (R2-OW17), so the reading served carries its own; a review decision leaves it as it is. An empty list means checked, no change.
  - *Rows.* Every record gains `potential_payee_key` after `potential_payee_label`: on every `potential_lender` row, named or not, an amount-free digest of its payee key (the entity, D6's payee words and the masked recipient; the first 16 hex characters of their SHA-256), so no payee word is published; None elsewhere. Only the module reads it.

### 9.2 Package (`_package_analysis`)

- **Each document row** gains:
  - `true_revenue_total`, `true_revenue_count`, `counted_flagged_total`, `counted_flagged_count`, `excluded_pending_review_total`, `excluded_pending_review_count` and the two by-reason dicts;
  - `revenue_established`. It is today's `verified_revenue_established` condition (`webapp/app.py:1367-1376`) and every posted credit carries a 5.6 tier. `verified_revenue_established` stays, with the old condition, for the verified figure.
- **Totals:**
  - the same keys, summed over the members;
  - `true_revenue_total`, `counted_flagged_total`, `excluded_pending_review_total` and their counts are `None` when any completed member's `revenue_established` is false, and `verified_revenue_total` is `None` when any completed member's `verified_revenue_established` is false (§10.4);
  - `revenue_unestablished_documents` lists those members' ids;
  - `revenue_review_items` is the sum of the members' held counts;
  - `revenue_review_required` is the gate of T7, applied to each member.
- **Evidence:** the package's revenue evidence stays per state, and each evidence record carries its tier fields. The package's own `true_revenue_evidence`, at the top level (`webapp/app.py:2155`) and inside `detection` (`:2167`), is repointed with the per-account one: the members' verified plus counted evidence, not `package_revenue_evidence["verified_revenue"]`. `counted_flagged_evidence` and `excluded_pending_review_evidence` join both places.
- **Fallbacks:** `_package_analysis` reads `metrics["true_revenue"]` twice as a fallback today: for a member's verified total when its rows are not authoritative (`:1441-1447`, after `verified_revenue_total` and `confirmed_true_revenue_total`), and for the withholding denominator when `withholding_denominator` is missing (`:1471-1474`). After the repoint that key is True revenue, so both fallbacks are dropped: the verified total falls back to `verified_revenue_total`, then `confirmed_true_revenue_total`, then `None` (the member's verified figure is not established); the denominator falls back to the legacy eligible deposits.
- **Currency:** the new money keys join `_CROSS_CURRENCY_TOTAL_KEYS` and the test's `EXPECTED_REFUSED_TOTALS`, the counts join `UNIT_FREE_TOTALS`, and a refused package sets every `total` inside the by-reason dicts to `None`.
- **Audit fix batch B11 (§20):**
  - *Duplicates (I06, MCA standard §4.6(3)).* Before any member is expanded, a job that repeats a kept job's id, content hash, or (account by account) statement identity is left out of every figure: an account's content digest when its ledger prints a transaction, or its statement key when every part is printed (bank, account last four, period start and end, opening and closing balance), never between two printed full numbers that conflict (audit round 2, R2-B14 below). Which copy is kept is R2-B14's rank below. It is listed in `documents` after the members (`is_duplicate`, `duplicate_of`, `duplicate_reason` `same_content` or `same_statement`, `duplicate_kept_because`, no figure), its group in `duplicates`; a job listed twice is listed once. An account of a kept document that another kept job published is excluded (`excluded_accounts`, reason `duplicate_statement`, `duplicate_accounts` in the totals); the sibling accounts of one document are never compared. Any duplicate sends the package to review. The ids of `?ids=` and `POST /package` are de-duplicated.
  - *Months and averages (I07, I33).* `months` is the number of distinct calendar months the counted statements stand for (the Monthly Statements' rule: the month holding most of a period's days, the earlier on a tie; a statement printing no period is its own month), no longer the member count; `statement_periods` is published beside it when the two differ. `avg_monthly_true_revenue`, `avg_monthly_verified_revenue` and `avg_monthly_non_revenue` are the package totals over `months` (so the per-calendar-month sum across accounts, averaged), `None` where True is N/A, and refused with the other per-period averages (one document's accounts, a mixed or undeclared currency).
  - *Reconciliation (I31).* The totals and each document row carry `revenue_tiers_sum_to_posted` beside `revenue_reconciles`; `unreconciled_documents` lists the counted members whose `reconciliation.ok` is not true. The decision no longer reads the identity.
  - *Integrity facts (B9's I13, B10's I05).* Each document row carries `holder_unscreened` and `payer_text_unread`; the totals list the members (`holder_unscreened_documents`, `payer_text_unread_documents`).
  - *Evidence (I32).* Each revenue evidence record carries `source_currency` and `source_account` (`None` for a statement of one account).
- **Audit round 2, R2-B14 (§20):**
  - *Which copy of a repeated statement is kept (R16).* The listed jobs claim their ids, hashes and identities in the order of a rank, then of their listed place: a job that is done and publishes an account first, then one whose served copy is current (no account with `revenue_established` false, no record without or before `CLASSIFICATION_VERSION`), then one whose posted credits carry an analyst's decision (`revenue_review_status` confirmed or rejected). So a failed, queued, processing or interrupted copy, a copy analysed under older rules or a copy without the decisions recorded on another never takes a better copy's place; copies alike keep the one listed first. `documents` and `duplicates` keep the listed order (a group lists the kept job first, its hash the group's); each left-out row's `duplicate_kept_because` is the first rank key the kept copy wins on (`has_analysis`, `current_rules`, `has_review_decisions`), else `listed_first`. A left-out failed copy is not counted failed.
  - *Two accounts are never one statement by the last four alone (R46).* The statement key matches only between accounts whose printed numbers do not conflict: the digits at the end of each number (blanks, `-`, `.` and `/` removed) conflict when both print more than four and the shorter's are not the end of the longer's. A masked or four-digit print still matches a full one, and a content digest (which covers the number) matches as before.
  - *A shorter printout of days another statement covers (R14).* After the exact repeats, the statements the package counts are grouped by their bank (casefolded) and their printed number's last four (never two whose full numbers conflict, never two accounts of one document); a statement's period is its printed one, or else its first and last posted row's day. A statement is left out (its `duplicate_of` the statement left in the package that shares the most of its days) when its period lies inside the union of the other statements' periods of its account, it prints a posted row, and every posted row of it, credit or debit, is one of theirs as a multiset on the day and the signed cents. The statements of more than a month (31 days) are tested first, the longest first: a quarterly printout or a multi-month export whose rows the monthly statements print is left out (`duplicate_reason` `superseded_long_printout`) and the monthly statements, each its own calendar month, stay. Then the rest, the shortest first: a month-to-date or interim printout beside the full month, the shorter of two month-to-date printouts or a short custom range the full months print is left out (`superseded_interim`), and a full month is never left out for partial printouts of it (of two periods alike, the later listed is tested first; review round 1). An account of a document whose other accounts stay is excluded alone (`excluded_accounts`, the same reason). Like a repeat, it sends the package to review. Any other overlap of two statements of one account is never netted: when the two share a credit in the days both cover (a multiset on the day, the cents and the description, casefolded, its blanks collapsed), `overlapping_statements` lists the pair (`job`, the one listed later, `other`, `shared_credit_count`, `shared_credit_total`, `currency`, the account's, null when the two declare different ones, and `account` / `other_account` for an account of a document) and the package goes to review; boundary days that share no credit say nothing. A package without such a statement is unchanged.
- **Audit round 2, R2-B15 (§20):**
  - *Months by the days the statements cover (R13).* `months` is the larger of B11's distinct calendar months (above, unchanged, as are the Month/Year labels) and a floor: the days each account's counted statements cover (`_covered_days`: a printed period's days, first and last included, none when a day does not read or the end is before the start, at most 400), as whole months of 30.4375 days, half up, the largest account's. An account is its bank, casefolded and its blanks collapsed, and the last four digits of its printed number; a member printing neither is its own. So three statements of a 16th-to-15th cycle across February, of a business-day cycle slipping around the 15th, or of a cycle whose periods share their closing day read 3 months (B11's rule read 2), and a statement of 59 days reads 2 (it read 1); calendar months never read fewer than before.
  - *Accounts left out for another reason than a repeat (R15).* Membership and every figure are unchanged (Q1, Q2, Q5 of 2026-08-30; the main-account ruling of 2026-09-23). Each `excluded_accounts` entry names its statement's `filename`. When an entry is not a repeat (`is_duplicate`): a statement whose main account is held or idle, an account that did not validate on its own, every account of a document whose transfers could not be paired or that left a section out without proof, the totals publish `completeness` `partial` (Q1: the package surfaces partial completeness) and `excluded_account_count`, and the package goes to review, as the same account uploaded alone does. `sibling_account_omission_detected` stays Q10's (a ratified omission stays partial and approved).
  - *No statement analysed, and jobs still on their way (R54).* With no completed member (every job failed, was interrupted or is still queued or processing, or every account was left out), the True, Verified, Counted and Held totals, their counts, aliases (`true_revenue`, `confirmed_true_revenue`, `confirmed_true_revenue_total`) and by-reason dicts are `None`, so the per-month True and Verified are too, `revenue_tiers_sum_to_posted` and `revenue_reconciles` are false and `true_revenue_evidence` is `None`; `total_credits`, the gross averages, non-revenue and the currency layer's `no_analyzed_documents` keep their structural zeros. A job still queued or processing is counted under `pending` (published only when there is one), never `failed`, and sends the package to review; an error, an interrupted run and a job done without an analysis stay `failed`. With a completed member §10.4 holds as before.
  - *`monthly_lender_debits` (R55)* is the confirmed lender debits per calendar month, `lender_debits / months`, refused with the other per-period figures (one document's accounts, a mixed or undeclared currency); it was the package's total under a monthly name. A statement's own `monthly_lender_debits` (`analysis/metrics.py`) is unchanged.

A member row whose basis is under the floor publishes no rate and sets `withholding_review_required`; its potential matches carry no basis and no exposure.
  - *Member rows (R3-72).* A member row divides by the basis it prints: where the package moved the member's basis from its stored one (R-d's internal-transfer deduction in the legacy mode, the 5.6 counted-pair deduction in the True mode, R2-OW15/16's moved credits), its `withholding_rate` and `potential_withholding_exposure` are its own `withholding_numerator` and `potential_withholding_numerator` over that basis; elsewhere the stored figures; neither is published under the floor or where F1 refuses the member's basis. Each `detection.potential_lenders` match's exposure reads the same helper (`withholding_basis_publishable`), so the row and the match agree.
  - *Lump-sum payoffs (the owner's answer of 2026-10-07 to R3-79).* A member's paid debits carrying `lump_sum_payoff` stay in its `lender_debits` and its funder's rollup and are out of its `withholding_numerator` (the package reads the record flags); its document row carries `lump_sum_payoff_total` and `lump_sum_payoff_count`, and the totals the members' sums, only where there is one (`lump_sum_payoff_total` joins `_CROSS_CURRENCY_TOTAL_KEYS`, 47 refused fields, and the conditional keys, so a refusal nulls it only where it is published; the count is kept); `lump_sum_payoffs` lists the items with `source_job`, `source_document`, `source_currency` (and `source_account`), only where there is one; `lender_evidence` lists the rows; the downloads carry `lump_sum_payoff_<n>` sections. A payoff attempt the package's pass 4 matches to a return in the next statement rejoins the numerator and is no lump sum, as a returned attempt inside one statement is.

- Audit round 3, R3-B17 (§20): no bump in a fix batch either; its stored-output change, for R3-B25's move: on every new analysis (in each Zelle reading), the revenue reading (state, method, matched rule, confidence, tier, reason, reason sentence, context signals, contribution flags) of a credit the counter-debit holds or pass 6 now read differently (§5.2's counter-debit readings: a bank's posting-type label, a pre-authorized-debit label and `ACHDEBIT` name no party; a numbered company is compared by its number; R3-77, R3-74, R3-15), and of a credit from a numbered company printed after RBC's `ACCOUNT PAYABLE PMT` or Scotiabank's `ACCOUNTS PAYABLE` whose payer region now keeps its number (the holder test reads the holder's own number), with their statements' revenue totals, `revenue_review_required` and True-basis withholding rates. In the census (re-parsed and cached, both Zelle readings) 0 credits change tier, reason or method and every field of all 310,172 re-parsed records is unchanged (one credit's census facts `numbered_region` and `payer_key_digest` move, a local tool's reading of its payer region); outside the shares, in unreconciled RBC statements each dumped three times, 9 counted e-Transfer credits from one numbered company ($22,060.26, 5 statements) are held `payer_also_debited` and 4 held round-sum e-Transfer credits from it take that reason. `CounterDebitReading.number` and the readings are pass 6 and 7 internals no record or download carries. No key, field, reason code, method or item kind is added or renamed, and no parser, debit, D6 name or lender output moves.

Each `ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION` bump makes a re-upload, and a re-analysis, recompute the analysis from the cached reading and keeps OCR cached. Only a `CLASSIFICATION_VERSION` move sets `analysis_rules_outdated` on older saved analyses (lender spec D12): a stage-only bump (B9 to B11, R2-B04 to R2-B07 above) sets no notice, and 5.7 sets it on every analysis saved at 5.6 or earlier (audit round 2, R2-B16: R56).

## 10. Metrics and UI

### 10.1 Cards (statement page, package page, statement modal)

The Credits section becomes:

| Card | Value | Glyph, tone | Filter |
|---|---|---|---|
| **True Revenue** (headline, first and larger) | `true_revenue_total` | REV, green | `true_revenue` |
| Verified Revenue (beside it) | `verified_revenue_total`, with its share of True | VER, green | `verified_revenue` |
| Counted, Not Verified | `counted_flagged_total` | CNT, teal | `counted_flagged` |
| Held for Review | `excluded_pending_review_total` | ?, amber | `excluded_pending_review` |
| Non-Revenue | `non_revenue_total` | X, neutral | `non_revenue` |
| Total Credits | unchanged | CR, neutral | — |
| ACH Credits | unchanged | ACH, neutral | — |

The "Unverified Deposits" and "Revenue Upper Bound" cards are removed. `maximum_revenue` stays in the payload and the exports. The statement modal shows counts beside totals, as today.

Audit fix batch B11 (§20):
- **The package page (I07, I33).** The hero reads "Total credits · N statements · M months" (M the distinct calendar months, §9.2), "Avg monthly gross credits", True revenue and "True per month"; the Package revenue section's sub-line is "N statements · M months", and it adds "True Revenue Per Month" and "Verified Revenue Per Month" cards; "Avg Monthly Credits" becomes "Avg Monthly Gross Credits" ("Gross posted credits per calendar month (not True revenue)").
- **The Revenue chip and status row (I31)** read "Balanced" only where the statement's own rows reconcile (`reconciliation.ok`) and its revenue is established (a package: every counted member reconciles, revenue is established and its currencies are not refused); otherwise "Review required".
- **The True card's note** names the statement integrity facts True rests on: no holder name read (`holder_unscreened`) and the credits whose payer text was not read (`payer_text_unread`); a package names how many statements carry each. Audit round 3, R3-B11 (R3-30, §8.10, §20): a statement with no holder line read publishes no account title either, so the fact reads "No holder name read: the holder's own deposits are not screened, nor is a premium-trust account title read", and a package's "N statement(s) with no holder name read (nor a premium-trust title)"; a title its account name prints is still read, which the copy does not deny.
- **Non-Revenue (I51)** stays a figure where revenue is not established, and its note says "Captured rows only".
- **The Revenue evidence table (I53)** breaks Counted down by reason, as it does Held (filter `counted_flagged:<reason>`); the credit mix says its shares are of posted credits.
- **A repeated statement (I06)** is named in a notice on the package page, which says it is left out of every figure; the Monthly Statements, the chart, the title and the counts never show it; the upload queue names a file repeated within its batch. Audit round 2, R2-B14 (§20): the queue matches the files of its batch on the content hash the upload reply carries (a file also uploaded in an earlier batch still reads as repeated in this one), and once the batch's package arrives only the row the package left out reads "left out of the package figures", naming the copy kept in its place (R49, R16); the notice says why a later copy was kept ("`<file>` left out: `<kept>` is the same file and has a completed analysis / current rules / the review decisions"), names a shorter printout another statement covers ("a shorter printout of days another statement covers") or a printout of more than a month the monthly statements print ("a printout of more than a month whose every row other statements of the account print", review round 1) and each pair of overlapping statements that share credits, with the count and the money they share in the pair's own currency, counted in both (R16, R14).

Audit round 2, R2-B15 (§20):
- **Months (R13).** The package page's statements and months follow §9.2's months. A statement's copied summary reads its monthly figures over the calendar months its period covers (`statementMonthsCovered`: its days, first and last included, over 30.4375, half up, at least one; one when a day does not read), so a statement of 59 days prints half its True "a month", never its whole total; a statement of a month prints its totals as before.
- **Accounts left out (R15).** A notice beside the repeats' one names every account left out of every figure for another reason than a repeat: "N account(s) left out of every figure. The package needs review." then each by its file (and "account i of n" for an account of a document) and why: "main account not verified", "main account printed no activity", "transfers between its accounts could not be paired", "a section left out without proof", otherwise "account not validated". The hero's True line then adds " · covers K of M statement(s)": the statements with an analysed account the package counts, of the statements it lists.
- **Nothing analysed, and jobs still on their way (R54, R15).** A package that counted no statement or analysed none is never "Balanced" (the chip and the status row read "Review required"); its credits label and memo read "No statements analysed" instead of an invented "1 statement · 1 month", and True, Verified, Counted, Held and the per-month figures read N/A. A job still queued or processing reads "N still processing" in the processing note (beside "N statement(s) failed") and "Processing" on its Monthly Statements row, never "Failed" or "Unavailable".
- **Counts (R50).** A repeat is no statement on any surface: the summary card reads "C completed of S" over the statements the package counts (it read the listed jobs, repeats included). A package holding an account of a document counts its statements and its accounts apart, A being its completed, failed and pending accounts: the hero kicker and the Monthly Statements count read "S statement(s) · A account(s)", the status row "Accounts completed C / A", the summary card "S statement(s) · C of A account(s) completed", the copied summary "C of A account(s) completed", and the unestablished note counts statements over the statements done ("1 of 1 statement has no established revenue", never "1 of 2"). The credits label keeps "N statements · M months"; a package of single-account statements reads as before.
