- **Returned funder payments: the defaults (the underwriter's Q5 of 2026-10-02, §6.2, §10.1, §11; R2-OW13).** Each default is in the code; the owner may change it. (1) A potential (unconfirmed) lender's returned payment keeps today's zeroing: the owner's words name funders (G7: 0 potential moves); the zeroed payment is the one on or before the return (audit round 3, R3-B02: R3-71, §6.2 pass 4, §20). Alternative: take it out of the potential totals and keep it in the potential exposure. (2) The warning sends nothing to review. Alternative: gate the statement on it. (3) A pair classification 5.4's lender side makes on any settlement word (`RETURN`, `REJECTED`, `REVERSAL`, `VOID`, `CANCEL`, `NSF`, `CHARGEBACK`) restores the funder's payment, so a business-initiated reversal of a funder's debit (PNC's `REVERSE CORPORATE ACH DEBIT`, the reversal-only sub-count of §20) is treated as a bounce: out of paid, in the withholding rate, with the same warning, which quotes the bank's words so the underwriter can tell it from a bank's return. Alternative: restore only on the bounce forms rule D reads. (4) The return credits keep their revenue reading, so those held as `possible_return` stay on the review list (their row names the matched payment, §10.6; counts in §20). Alternative: read a matched return as `non_revenue` / `matched_reversal_pair` (no True move). Audit round 3, R3-B02 (R3-21; the brief's default (a), an owner decision): a Confirm on such a credit is refused ("a credit that returns a confirmed funder's payment can only be marked non-revenue"; Mark Non-Revenue and Reset stay; §10.6, §10.7), since nothing re-reads the pair after a review and a Confirm counted the business's own payment coming back as Verified revenue while its payment stayed out of paid (13 held matched credits, about $10.9 thousand, in 7 statements on the cached basis). Alternatives: (b) on Confirm, restore the paired debit to paid to lenders, drop its warning and rebuild the lender figures at review time (a review would then move lender figures, which no review does today); (c) this default's alternative above (every matched return `non_revenue`, no Confirm path). (5) The attribution reads the amount and the window: across two funders at one amount the warning can name the other funder (the dollars are right either way); Bank of America's printed `RECEIVED ON` day settles it there. The final review of round 2, F2 (§6.2, §20): a return is matched only to a payment dated on or before it (a confirmed funder's paid payment or, since audit round 3, R3-B02 (R3-71), a potential lender's payment; 5.4's named pair picked the nearest day either way, so a return printed at a month's start took a later payment), and a return whose payment sits in the previous statement of the account is matched by the package (pass 4), never by either statement alone; a statement viewed alone keeps such a payment paid and shows no warning for it. Review round 1 of that fix run (§6.2, §20), for ratification: (6) pass 4 reads a bounce-worded return that D1 reads as a lender credit where it names the matched payment's funder (rule D never reads a lender credit; no corpus row moves through it). Alternative: rule D's credit filter exactly, so such a return across two statements warns nowhere. (7) Pass 4 holds back a credit the revenue side paired only where the partner is dated on or before it (rule D holds back every such credit that is not its payment's partner); F2(a) makes this necessary, since a return paired with a later payment cannot reverse it. (8) R2-OW18's package payment changes read pass 4's matched payment as a returned attempt, as R2-OW13's restore does inside one statement. (9) Re-presentment (audit round 3, R3-B02: R3-73; ANSWERED by the owner on 2026-10-07, "Count it once (Recommended)", option (b)): a returned payment LEAVES the withholding numerator once the same funder re-debits it, the same cents off its cycle within one cadence gap after the return, or an exact 2x catch-up within that gap (the catch-up covers the bounced payment once); until then it stays, the obligation standing (§6.2 pass 7c and the package's pass 5, §11). The returned-funder-payment warning adds "re-presented on <date>" (or "caught up on <date>, 2x"); paid to lenders, the lender count and revenue do not move. The audit's corpus shapes (cached basis, no PDF opened): three clean weekly re-takes (at Scotiabank, RBC and Citibank: 5, 5 and 6 numerator rows for 4 weekly slots, one re-debit itself returned), about 10 statements with re-take shapes in all, and exact 2x catch-ups in 2 to 4 statements; daily series cannot be told from two concurrent positions, so a daily series reads only a 2x catch-up. Its defaults, the orchestrator's (the owner may change them): "off its cycle" is more than a day from the weekday most of a weekly or biweekly series keeps (three days from the day of the month for a monthly one; a daily or semi-monthly series, and a re-debit on the payment's own day, read no same-cents re-debit, since such a debit cannot be told from a second position); a schedule needs three dates of the series; one cycle is 7, 14, 16 or 31 days, one business day for a daily catch-up; a 2x debit with three or more 2x debits of the funder within one cycle (at least a week) is a second position; the earliest qualifying re-debit is taken. Review round 1 of R3-B02 added two more, both keeping the returned payment standing where the shape cannot be told from a regular payment: a weekday (a day of the month for a monthly series) that two or more other attempts of the series keep is a second recurring phase, a twice-weekly schedule or a second position at the same cents, whose next payment reads no re-presentment (before it, a twice-weekly series' regular payment on its other weekday took a bounced payment out of the numerator; a same-cents stream that starts after the bounce, seen on only one more date, still reads as a re-presentment); and a 2x debit followed by two or more 2x debits within two cycles after it (any schedule but daily) is a step-up to a new level, a renewal or a modified payment, never a catch-up (a step-up seen for only one more cycle in the statement still reads as a catch-up, the limit of one statement). Review round 2 of R3-B02 changed one and added two: every 2x debit within two cycles after the candidate counts toward that level, on the series' cycle or not (round 1 counted only those on the cycle, which read a second position's 2x payment on another weekday as a catch-up although the bounced payment's own weekday was paid at 1x the week after and never caught up: one returned payment in the corpus, one statement in two analyses, now standing); two or more 2x debits within two cycles BEFORE the candidate are a level already running (its next payment past the statement's end, or the position paid off), no catch-up either, so the returned payment stands (a 2x debit already taken as another bounce's catch-up is no level payment, so alternating bounces each caught up 2x still count once); and a weekday kept only by attempts each dated within one cycle after another return of the series is no recurring phase: those are a funder re-presenting every bounce on one weekday, and each returned payment counts once (round 1's guard kept them all standing). Alternatives: count only the 2x debits on the series' cycle (round 1's default; the corpus payment above reads as caught up again); read no level before the candidate; keep every weekday two or more other attempts keep as a recurring phase (round 1's default). The limits, in shapes that cannot be told apart: a twice-weekly schedule whose every payment on one weekday in the statement bounced (or a same-cents second position that starts after a run of bounces, each of its payments within a cycle after one) reads as a weekly series re-presented on that weekday (counted once); a run of 2x catch-ups that themselves bounced and were caught up again, two or more within two cycles of another, reads as a level, so its returned payment stands; and where the re-presentments sit one to four days after the payments, the median gap reads no weekly schedule, so every returned payment stands, as before the review rounds. The alternatives the owner did not take: (a) keep every returned attempt in the numerator; (c) a "re-presented on <date>" note with no figure moving.
- **The withholding basis and cash deposits: the follow-ups (the underwriter's Q7 of 2026-10-02, T8, §8.2, §11; R2-OW14).** Each default is in the code; the owner may change it. (1) A statement whose True revenue is $0 has no rate on the default basis and asks for review (`withholding_review_required`, never a gate; a basis that is not established does gate, the final review of round 2, F1, review round 1 of its fix run, §20) until a review confirms held credits: 171 census statements on the re-parsed basis at R2-OW13's tip; 19 of the 858 lender-paying accounts lose a rate they had on the legacy basis (15 at c486fd5 and at R2-B15's tip; R2-OW01's Q12 and R2-OW02's Q3 added two each), most with every credit held. The legacy basis's figure stays published (`legacy_eligible_deposits`); a fallback to the legacy rate where True is $0 was not asked and is not built. Audit round 3, R3-B03 (R3-20; §11, §20): the same treatment now covers a True or Verified basis above $0 and under a floor, `WITHHOLDING_BASIS_FLOOR` = 500 in the statement's own unit (`REVENUE_REVIEW_HELD_FLOOR`, the floor T7 already uses so a $0-True statement never gates on held cents), the brief's default (a) of an owner decision: no rate, no potential exposure, `withholding_review_required`, `withholding_basis_below_floor` and a note naming the basis and the floor, never a gate; the legacy basis bypasses it. The cached walk of the round-3 audit found 17 established lender-paying statements publishing an unflagged True-basis rate above 100%, only 3 of them on a near-zero True (the other 14 carry True from about $1.5K to $117K and several are above 100% on the legacy basis too: real leverage, so no cap on the rate is built). Alternatives for the owner: (b) a share of posted credits instead (True under 1% of posted: 25 re-parsed accounts; it catches two of the three near-zero statements, not the third, whose True is a few hundred dollars); (c) publish the rate but set the review flag and a note under the floor; (d) no floor (before R3-B03). (2) Arm R reads `US<RETAILER> W<n>` as a retail cash load from the row's shape; no statement was opened. The five statements that carry its 46 loads print 41 `CASH DEPOSIT FEE` debits, 20 of them dated on a load's day, which supports the reading; the planning check noted loads above the per-load limit it expected of a retail cash network (10 of the 46 are between $500 and $1,000). Confirm it on a Bluevine statement, or drop the arm (its 38 rows, $9,965.00, go back to `payer_also_debited`, and 8 counted rows to `named_payer_unlabelled`). (3) Arm S reads any bank's `DEPOSIT <place> <transit> <sequence>`; the corpus has none outside Scotiabank (on another bank, arm S no longer lifts R35's funder-name guard: R3-45, audit round 3, R3-B07, §20; its channel reading there is still this question). (4) Noted, out of scope: the cash form's `DEPOT` arm reads `THE HOME DEPOT` as a branch, so 12 Home Depot card credits ($1,030.71) count as cash deposits and the store's refunds on the cash channel are excluded only by the refund rules (both measured at R2-OW13's tip and at c486fd5).
- **Lump-sum payoffs in the withholding numerator (audit round 3, R3-79; §11).** Answered 2026-10-07 by the owner (§19.1): "Exclude worded payoffs (Recommended)" (option (b) of four: (a) every paid funder debit stays in the numerator, the brief's default before the answer; (b) take word-marked lump sums out of the numerator, keep them in paid to lenders, show a line; (c) (b) plus one-offs of 10x the funder's median or more after which the series stops; (d) an information line only). In the code since R3-B03 (`lump_sum_payoff`, `_build_record`). The implementer's defaults inside the answer, which the owner may overrule: (1) the words are exactly the owner's list, read as whole words on the debit's normalized text (a hyphen reads as a space), so a word glued to letters or digits (`XPAYOFF12`, `PAYOFF7788`), a plural (`PAYOFFS`), `PREPAID`, `PRE PAYMENT` and `PAY OUT` read nothing, and a word followed by its reference field (`PrePay:[...]`) reads; (2) the matcher reads the whole row, so a funder's debit whose holder or memo field prints one of the words reads as a lump sum (a residual, as for Liberis's receiver field); (3) a payoff attempt the bank returned is out of paid, so Q5 keeps it in the numerator as every returned payment and it is no lump sum (alternative: out of the numerator too); the package's pass 4 does the same across a statement boundary; (4) a lump sum stays a payment of its series for R2-OW18's payment changes (they read paid to lenders), and R2-OW18's stop payoff note still reads only a one-off dated strictly after the last payment (the side defect the audit recorded; R3-B25 records it); (5) an outsized one-off with no word (the audit's 10x-and-$5,000 debits) stays in the numerator (option (c), not built). Corpus: 7 distinct debits in 5 statements (14 analyses), $211,826.19, on the re-parsed and the cached basis alike: five PREPAY fields of one funder, one PAY OFF wire, one LOAN PAYOUT debit; one payoff-worded debit the bank returned (one statement) stays in the rate under default (3). The published rate falls where a lump sum was large beside the scheduled payments (§20).
- **Returns across statements and chargebacks: the defaults (the underwriter's Q6 of 2026-10-02, §6.2's package passes; R2-OW15).** Each default is in the code; the owner may change it. (1) "Consecutive months" is read literally: the original is sought only in the same account's immediately preceding statement (it starts 0 to 7 days after the earlier one ends; one account's statements on the corpus follow each other within 0 to 3 days, or more than 20 when a month is missing), with no day cap inside it. Alternative: keep pass 4's 14 days across statements too (on the corpus 2 of the 4 matches, 32 and 49 days after their deposits, $1,400.00, would stay counted and flagged). (2) The nearest equal deposit before the return is taken, not the earliest (pass 4's choice inside one statement): with no day cap, the earliest could reach weeks back past a nearer deposit. On the corpus each match has one candidate, so the two agree. Alternative: the earliest. (3) The chargeback flag includes a processor's adjustments (`MERCH ADJ`, `FINCL ADJ`, `BANKCD ADJ`: 9 of the corpus's 32 rows, $11,938.22 of $20,846.28), each flag naming its wording. Alternative: chargebacks alone (23 rows, $8,908.06). (4) A statement printing fewer than four account digits is matched through its balance chain (it opens on the preceding statement's closing balance to the cent), never by its bank alone; two accounts of one bank that chain to the cent by chance would read as one (none on the corpus). (5) A return that only a confirmed deposit could match stays flagged and names that deposit (`candidate_decided`, "you confirmed … ; review"); a deposit the analyst marked non-revenue names nothing. Alternative: a further decision kind for "this deposit bounced", which the routes, the store and the replay would need.
- **Transfers between the business's accounts: the defaults (the underwriter's Q4 of 2026-10-02, §6.2's package passes; R2-OW16).** Each default is in the code; the owner may change it. (1) The release is Confirm Revenue, one control and one audit trail: it releases the deposit into True and marks it Verified, on its own statement too (§10.7), although a rule never verifies a bare deposit (Q2 of 2026-09-28); the row note says so. Alternative: a release that restores the deposit's earlier counted tier (`tier_before`, which `package_match` already carries), which needs a new decision kind in the route, the store and the replay. (2) A teller, counter or branch deposit stays matchable (a branch transfer between two of the business's accounts can print that way on its receiving side, and the transfer out must still print transfer wording); a check deposit and a deposit printing a cash device's word (ATM, ABM, cash, coin, smart safe, night drop, vault, pre-encoded) or a retail cash load never are. Alternative: refuse every cash, branch and teller form (0 corpus rows either way at c486fd5). A bare `NIGHT DEPOSIT` stays matchable: §8.2's cash form does not read it. (3) A credit whose payer the parser did not read (`payer_text_not_read`) is never matched: such rows are often a welded customer line (R2-B07). Alternative: admit it (0 corpus rows either way). (4) No extra gate: the held deposit gates its statement in the package as any held credit does, and the notice and Held for Review list it. (5) Two accounts of one document are matched too (the owner's example, sent in one PDF, counted twice under R-d, which nets only same-day legs printing a designation). This hold sets no internal-transfer mark and changes no R-d pair, deduction or refusal, so the ruling of 2026-08-30 on R-d's exclusion (L1 design §8.14) is untouched; the corpus holds no multi-account document, so only the tests measure this arm. Alternative: match across uploaded statements only. (6) Two accounts are told apart by their printed numbers alone (four digits or more, the last fours differing or the full numbers conflicting); one account read under two bank spellings is never two, and two banks' accounts sharing a last four are never matched (the conservative direction).
- **Read the printed account number on Chase, Capital One and Banque Royale statements** (the underwriter's Q4 of 2026-10-02; R2-OW16), so the package can check their transfers: a statement whose account number was not read (fewer than four digits) is never paired by Q4 and is marked `no_account_number` ("Transfers between accounts not checked for P statement(s): no account number read"). On the corpus's package proxies (§20) most such statements are Chase's. Parser work, outside this run; Q6 already reaches these accounts through the balance chain, and Q4 follows as soon as the number is read.
- **The Zelle setting: the defaults (the owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3; §8.4, §9.1, §10.7; R2-OW17).** Each default is in the code; the owner may change it. (1) The Q3-era carve-outs in the counted reading (the orchestrator's choice, 2026-10-06): a Zelle truck or equipment sale is asset-sale proceeds and a builder's Zelle draw counts (Q11 (2026-10-02)), as for Venmo; a Zelle tenant never makes the business a lessor, in both readings, so the setting moves Zelle rows only. Alternatives: keep all three carve-outs (a Zelle `TRUCK SALE` would then count as person-to-person under the default Yes), or lift the lessor's too (a non-Zelle rent `LEASE` would then be released under Yes only, needing its own fact line and export figure). (2) The lender side follows the reading: a bounce-worded Zelle credit the rules count leaves its funder debit paid under Yes (pass 7b; corpus: none). Alternative: pass 7b reads the No reading's tier in both. (3) Analyses stored before the setting are served as analysed, with the True card's notice, until R2-B16's stage bump lets a re-analysis compute both readings. Alternative: a lossy restore from `zelle_prior` (tier and reason right; method, rule, confidence, sentence, the $1 floor, the premium-trust hold and pass 7b wrong). (4) The latest decision on a posting sets every reading, and the replay does the same. Alternative: a decision binds only the reading it was made in (a Yes-mode reject would then vanish on re-analysis unless the review log recorded the mode, a storage schema change). (5) "Flagged 'Zelle'" is the rules' reason plus a row tag (a ledger chip, a `zelle` column) and a True-card line. Alternative: a new counted reason code. (6) The Non-Revenue note keeps ", Zelle deposits included" under No and on a Zelle-free account. Alternative: a top-level mode key on every payload. (7) The benchmark (`benchmark/run.py`, `compare.py`) keeps the stored reading. (8) `zelle_excluded`'s label and sentence are unchanged ("excluded by policy"). (9) One settings file per data directory: everyone using the installation shares the choice, and the gate, the decision pill, the package decision and the withholding rate flip for all of them; a per-underwriter choice waits for sign-in (D-2b).
- **Lender payment changes: the defaults (the owner's request of 2026-10-06, §9.1, §10.1; R2-OW18).** Each default is in the code; the owner may change it. The orchestrator's defaults of 2026-10-06: an increase mirrors the decrease (10% or more, held 2 or more payments; alternative: its own threshold); a schedule change is compared on the weekly equivalent and is never by itself a decrease (alternative: raw amounts); two concurrent positions with one funder are separate series (alternative: one series); the grace windows come from the corpus probe (daily 5, daily irregular 6, weekly 10, biweekly and semi-monthly 15, monthly 25 business days; alternative: other windows); information only (alternative: none). The open points: (1) the increase threshold mirrors the decrease (alternative: 5%, about 10 more increases, mostly variable-pay drift); (2) the statement's items are computed at analysis time (alternative: a serve-time view, which reaches saved jobs but cannot key potential lenders on old payloads); (3) payments are the classification plus the paid flag (alternative: the classification only; measured identical); (4) payloads stored before the check read "not checked" (alternative: compute confirmed series at serve time); (5) the Federal Reserve calendar, and Payments Canada's published closure days on a CAD statement (the Civic Holiday is no closure day; alternative: the US calendar everywhere, which changes the business-day counts of 19 package and 3 statement items and no item's presence); (6) a stop inside one statement is a possible stop (alternative: packages only); (7) temporary cuts and restorations are shown and marked (alternative: suppress a change reverted within N payments); (8) a level under 5% of the weekly weight of a schedule-confirmed level of the series (3 payments, 5 if daily) whose dates keep that level's beat is a fee level, dropped before positions are formed; a whole position under 5% of the series' weekly weight is still dropped (audit round 3, R3-24: the brief's A7 tested positions only, so a fee level that joined a payment position survived) (alternatives: raw amounts, or a "fee stream" line). Known shapes it does not cover: a large level with one isolated early payment far before its regular run joins the first position and can split a step-up into a "New payment stream" (corpus: 1 confirmed ONDECK package line); a level read as irregular can do the same (fabricated only); (9) no Settings checkbox (alternative: a display setting); (10) potential lenders are shown in the neutral tone and not under $100 a week (alternatives: amber and blue chips, no or another floor, or no signal on an unnamed key pooling 3 or more streams); (11) the funding note reads a credit from 20 days before to 5 days after the new amount's first payment; it never cites a credit that returns or reverses a payment, one within 1% of the change's own payment amounts or of a series payment or attempt 0 to 7 days before it, or one dated on or before the old regime's first payment (audit round 3, R3-82: on the corpus 12 of 83 notes leave, 4 statement and 8 package, 7 by the old regime's first payment and 5 by a payment's size; none moves to another credit; no size floor, since a revolving product's genuine draws can be payment-sized) (alternative: the reverse window, or no note); (12) the statement modal shows its lines but not R2-OW13's returned lines (alternative: both); (13) lines only, no lender-row or ledger chip (alternative: a "Changed" chip); (14) this §2.2 and inline amendments in the lender-detection spec (alternatives: a §2.1 row, no amendment); (15) no cross-reference to R2-OW12's funding aid (alternative: name it); (16) one line per qualifying step of a variable-pay product (alternative: one "variable payment" note per series); (17) a pause that resumes at the same payment is shown (alternative: no line); (18) THE ORCHESTRATOR'S CHOICE OF 2026-10-06, the alternative: a decrease or an increase at a new schedule held 2 payments but not yet the 3 (5 if daily) that confirm it is shown as a possible change, "new schedule not yet confirmed", when it is the position's last regime, or mid-position when its payments span 80% of a cycle (the default showed nothing until confirmed); a possible change never becomes the reference of point 23: the next regime is compared with the last confirmed level, and its line names the possible level and each step in its "via …, then …" suffix (daily 500 → weekly 1,600 held 2 → weekly 2,300 reads a possible -36% decrease, then a schedule change of -8% "via weekly $1,600.00 (-36%), then weekly $2,300.00 (+44%)"; daily 500 → weekly 1,500 held 2 reads a possible -40% as well (before audit round 3, R3-70, the catch-up rule of (22) silenced it); alternative: a possible level becomes the reference; R2-OW18 review round 1); (19) a potential payee's new amount joins its series only once D6 promotes it, 3 equal debits in a statement (alternative: the probe's 'ext' variant, never judged); (20) a bounced payment is presence for pauses, restarts and stops, for every position of its series (alternatives: paid payments only, or the matching position only); a line whose presence is a bounced attempt says so: a pause it ended reads "no payment or payment attempt", names the attempt and the date payments resumed, and a stop whose last presence it is reads "no payment or payment attempt" with the last payment's date (R2-OW18 review round 1; on the corpus 1 package and 1 statement pause and 4 package stops); a bounced attempt at a level's amount also keeps its schedule: a level's and a regime's cadence read the attempt dates beside the paid dates when that gives a faster regular schedule that the dates together keep (a daily one needs 60% of its dates or more in stretches of 5 consecutive business days holding 4 or more of them, more than NACHA's 3 presentments of one debit fill (R3-B04 review round 1, which replaced the batch's first guard, 60% of the gaps at one daily cycle, that covered one re-presentment on long levels only), and, between its paid dates, more returned presentments than one debit's chain holds before its paid one: of the intervals between consecutive paid dates with 3 business days or more inside, one at least and 60% hold 3 attempts or more, a shorter interval telling neither apart (R3-B04 review round 2: the stretches alone let the chains of two adjacent weeks, or of a week a holiday shortens, add up, so on fabricated rows a weekly cut whose chains alternate "the Monday returned, the Friday paid" and "the Monday and the Tuesday returned, the Thursday paid" read a confirmed "+250% weekly → daily", a 2-week level re-presented twice across Thanksgiving gave a false possible stop and a twice-weekly debit re-presented the next day read daily); so a weekly debit whose every chain (the original entry and at most two re-presentments) ends paid before the next week's entry stays weekly whatever its days and the level's length (every such layout checked on fabricated levels of 2 to 5 weeks, from each weekday of entry and across the weeks of Veterans Day, Thanksgiving, Memorial Day, Juneteenth and Christmas); the beat tests of concurrency and of the fee level read such a level's attempt dates beside its payments, as its cadence does, and the slower-run test of (22) reads its payments' own schedule while it is still presented (R3-B04 review rounds 1 and 2); attempts still never set an amount or a payment count (audit round 3, R3-23; on the corpus 8 package items leave and 12 appear, 1 statement item is relabelled and 5 more appear). Known shapes the dates cannot tell apart: a biweekly or monthly debit re-presented at weekly steps presents the dates of a weekly debit whose other presentments bounce, so it reads weekly as that one does (a biweekly cut of -30% re-presented a week later each time reads "+40% biweekly → weekly"; fabricated only); refusing a weekly reading there would undo a verified corpus series' -49% cut and +96% restoration, which are exactly that shape (alternative: refuse it, measured on the corpus: that series' two lines become one +96% without its "back to the earlier" mark); and a weekly debit can still read daily where a chain returned all three times (a missed week) or re-presented past the next week's entry puts 3 attempts between two paid dates, in most of its intervals or in the only one of a short level (fabricated only: of Monday debits each presentment of which is returned at a probability of 0.6 and re-presented 1 to 4 business days later, 0, 4, 0 and 2 of 150 levels of 2, 3, 4 and 6 weeks read daily where the base did not, against 1, 6, 3 and 3 before review round 2; of every layout of 2, 3 or 4 weeks that also lets a chain be returned three times, none, 2.0% and 2.4% read daily, against 18%, 8.0% and 7.6%); a stricter test would refuse verified corpus readings: a daily level another amount interrupts holds 4 attempts in an interval of 14 business days, which a share of the interval's days refuses, and another verified daily level's only interval with room holds exactly 3 (alternative: 4 attempts or more, measured on the corpus: that series' statement loses its -39% line and its package's +133% restoration returns to the base's "-53% daily → weekly"); (21) an amount change whose old and new amounts overlap for a few payments reads as a stop with "another … payment stream continues" (alternative: an "overlapping" change); (22) a level at 2x or 3x the main amount never run longer than 2 payments is a catch-up (a 2-payment run at a slower schedule than the main level is no catch-up but § Still open 18's possible change: daily 500 → weekly 1,500 held 2 reads a possible -40%; audit round 3, R3-70; corpus: 1 package item replaced by 2; the main level's schedule there is its payments' own while that level is still presented, paid or returned, through the run, so a 2x run on the paying weekday of a daily level whose other days bounce stays a catch-up, R3-B04 review round 1, and its cadence read through its attempts once it no longer is, so weekly 1,000 whose every other debit bounced, then biweekly 3,000 held 2, reads a possible +50% as its clean twin does, R3-B04 review round 2) (alternative: only when the main level returns); (23) THE ORCHESTRATOR'S CHOICE OF 2026-10-06, the alternative: each regime is compared with the last REPORTED level of its position (the first level until something is reported), so steps under 10% that add up are reported once the cumulative change reaches 10% (the default compared each regime with the one before it); such a line names the unreported levels with the step into each and the last step ("via weekly $950.00 (-5%), then weekly $650.00 (-32%)"), never "steps of under 10% each": an abrupt last step after a small drift reads as such (R2-OW18 review round 1; on the corpus 9 of the 12 package and 1 of the 2 statement lines with such levels have a step of 10% or more); (24) one presence definition, payments, attempts and payment-sized one-offs of 5% to under 2x (alternative: the probe's); a restart's pause, like a pause, leaves out the business days no statement of the chain covers (a hole between two members), so a level change across a hole is no restart unless the covered days alone pass the grace (R2-OW18 review round 1; no corpus item moves); and (audit round 3, R3-25; R2-OW18 review round 2 finding 2) a one-off within 2% of exactly 2 to 6 times the reference amount, a catch-up, is presence too, for pauses, restarts and stops alike, and never a payoff: a pause it ends reads "a debit of $X (k times the payment) on D (possible catch-up)" (a catch-up on the regime's next payment day still ends it as a catch-up), a stop names how many later debits are such multiples, the payoff note reads only a debit of 2x or more that is no exact multiple and counts the earlier ones, and every other debit of 2x or more inside a pause's gap is named (corpus, against the batch's base: 2 of 44 confirmed and 1 of 50 possible package stops and 1 of 42 statement possible stops leave, the frozen tree's 1 of 41; 1 package pause ends at its catch-up; 1 names a 4.33x debit; 1 package stop names its 3.95x as a catch-up and keeps its 2.85x as the payoff; 1 payoff counts an earlier debit). The owner's answer of 2026-10-07 ("Add a 'Caught up' line", §19.1) adds the line (kind `catch_up`), information only; the implementer's defaults inside it, each the owner may change: the reference is the regime in force (the position's last kept regime paid before the one-off); the missed payments run from the position's last paid presence before it (a payment, a payment-sized one-off or an earlier catch-up; a bounced attempt is a missed payment), so a run of growing multiples that each come before the next due date reads no line (corpus: the confirmed package stop with 2x, 3x and 4x debits leaves and shows nothing, so about nine payments' worth of exact multiples after the last regular payment is named on no line (R3-B05 review round 1, finding 4); alternatives: count from the last regular payment, which reads one missed monthly payment there although 5 payments' worth were paid before its due date, or a neutral note, "N debits of exact multiples after the last payment"); a daily regime's business days are each due, an irregular daily one's and another schedule's due dates (weekly, biweekly and semi-monthly the last paid date plus 7, 14 and 16 days, monthly the same day of the next month, each moved to the next business day) are missed only when the catch-up comes more than one business day after them (`CATCH_UP_LATE_BUSINESS_DAYS`; alternative: no allowance, so a weekly 2x the day after its due date reads as caught up); no line across a coverage hole; one line per one-off and per event (a pause or a stop line that shows for the same gap names it instead); a multiple seen twice at one amount is (22)'s catch-up level and reads no line (corpus: one statement's line has no package twin for this reason; alternative: a line per level payment). two known shapes of the defaults, each the owner may change: a multiple no larger than the missed payments before it (a partial catch-up) still reads "Caught up" and, being presence, takes the place of the stop or pause line although the regular payment may not resume (corpus: 1 statement line, 8 missed daily payments then 6x, and 1 package line, 2 missed biweekly payments then 2x; ### 18.2 Where this revision departs from the review's wording, and why

1. **Q7's credit-union arm (C1).** The review asked that every Q7 payer be a listed lender, with CU Direct / CUDL for the credit-union form. On the memo's rows, $3.64M of the draft's $4.02M Q7 reach is a credit union's own name with the entry `VHCL PURCH` (the CUDL indirect-lending form), paid to one dealer in 15 to 18 rows a statement. Requiring the credit union itself to be listed would drop all of it, and listing credit unions one by one does not scale. The revision admits the credit-union form instead, with three guards: the payer is a credit union, the entry is exactly `VHCL PURCH`, and the statement holds two or more such credits (a member's own purchase loan is a single credit). The loan-word veto and the lender and insurer vetoes apply as the review asked. G12 checks it.
2. **Refused, not always held (C4).** The review asked that every row Q5 or Q6 refuses on a purpose word be held. The revision holds the review's own list (investment, distributions, dividends, equity, contributions, owner money, intercompany, sweeps, rebates, interest, grants, claims, insurer words, reimbursements, bonus, pay, repayment) and the rest of §7.9's clearly non-sale purposes. It refuses verification but still counts a short list of words that ordinary sales also print: `SETTLEMENT` (an unregistered processor prints it), `TAX`, `FEES`, `SUBSCRIPTION`, `DISCOUNT`, `COMMISSION`, `COMPENSATION`, `EXPENSES`, and, in the entry fields only, floor-plan and equipment words. Holding them would take real sales out of True, and `TAX` would also hold the tax-preparer disbursements the owner has not ruled on (§15). These rows get their own reason, `named_payer_purpose_refused`, so the census shows them. `DISTRIB` excludes `DISTRIBUTORS` and `DISTRIBUTING`, and `OWNER` excludes owner-operators; the probe found a distributor's payments caught by the bare root.
3. **The holder test's reach (C5).** The review asked for the veto in every verifying rule of steps 10 to 14. The revision applies it to step 11's customer and invoice descriptors, steps 12 to 14, Q5 and Q6, but not to the registry (step 10 and recurrence) or to the card-settlement and claim-payment forms. Their payer is the platform, processor or insurer, and their rows print the merchant's own name as the payout's recipient. BMO prints `DIRECT DEPOSIT DOORDASH <store> MSP/DIV`, and the store is the holder, so the veto would hold every such payout. G3 lists any holder-matching row those paths verify, and the precision sample reads them.
4. **The first-distinctive-word test (C5).** The review's wording matched the holder's first distinctive word anywhere in the payer region. That would hold a supplier that shares a trade word with the holder (`FABRIKAM PLUMBING SUPPLY` paying `SAMPLE PLUMBING LLC`). The revision compares the payer's first distinctive word with the holder's, as §7.9's brand-word veto does. It skips common name-starters (`FIRST`, `UNITED`, `PREMIER` and the like), and never runs on a channel that prints no payer. Run unrestricted on the memo's rows, the test matched only bank and product words on check deposits (`COMPTE`, `BANK`) and no real affiliate, so those words are now holder noise.
5. **Push rails (I2).** The review asked that a row with a person-to-person rail verify only by a registry payout form. The revision closes the consumer rails completely, and lets the real-time and push rails (RTP, FedNow, Visa Direct, MC Send) verify through the registry only, by its form, its alias with context or its recurrence. §7.2 already decided that `RTP CREDIT AMAZON COM` verifies by recurrence, and Q4 names people paying people, not a platform's payout on a real-time rail.
6. **`DIRECT DEPOSIT` as pay wording (I4).** The review asked for `DIR ?DEP` anywhere except BMO's leading template. The revision takes `DIR DEP`, `DIRDEP` and `DIRECT DEP` anywhere, but the whole phrase `DIRECT DEPOSIT` only as an entry description. BMO and ATB print it as their channel template, and §5.2 lists it among the template prefixes. Amended by audit fix batch B7 (I09, §20): a direct deposit is a payment channel a company also settles a business's invoices through, so the words are pay wording only beside a sign of a person's pay (a payroll provider, a person receiver, a consumer entry, a consumer-shaped account), the reading Q8's own words ("Payroll" or "Salary" credits) support; the owner may restore the wider reading.
7. **Bank interest (M12).** Held as `non_sale_purpose`, not named `non_revenue` under T5. Holding it is reviewable, adds no new non-revenue move to account for under §6.3, and takes it out of True all the same.
8. **`CREDIT` in T4 (C2, I3).** The review asked that a standalone posting `CREDIT` never be read on payer-less rows. The revision extends that to the entry fields (`DES:CREDIT` is a posting word too). It keeps a whole-word `CREDIT` as a root inside a payer name, next to another name word, so `UNITED AUTO CREDIT` and a credit union still read as financing.
9. **T18 and T19 (I10).** The review asked for explicit T numbers with measured sizes. The revision keeps the draft's direction as its recommendation, and adds the verifiers' fallback in full. It builds each behind a switch that ships off unless the owner says yes (§16), so neither non-revenue move happens on this spec's word alone.

### 19.1 Owner decisions since the review

Recorded by audit fix batch B12 (§20); each line names where the code and §20 carry it.

- **2026-09-29, the plan.** The owner approved the implementation plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-28-true-revenue.md`) and delegated the calls it leaves open to the orchestrator's own recommendations, keeping for himself pushes, deploys and the genuinely split, high-impact calls.
- **2026-09-30, Q5 and Q6 kept.** After the precision sample (plan Task A3, §14.5), the owner kept Q5 and Q6 (a) and (b) as ruled and waived the A3 bar for their three strata, whose shortfall was rows the sorters could not tell (§20, "The precision bar for Q5 and Q6 (a) and (b)").
- **2026-09-30, the MCA principle.** This is an MCA underwriting tool: True revenue is the money the business earns from its operations, as the MCA industry counts deposits. Government money unrelated to the business is never revenue; a government or an insurer paying the business for its goods or services still is. The audit of 2026-09-30 and its fix batches read every rule against it.
- **2026-09-30, government money (GOV).** Under that principle a personal benefit is held as `personal_income` (class B), a tax refund is `non_revenue` (class C), a grant or subsidy is held as `non_sale_purpose` (class D), and a government paying for goods or services keeps its reading (class A); the forms that print no purpose (class E) wait for the owner (ruled on 2026-10-02, below). §20's four GOV lines carry it.
- **2026-09-30 to 2026-10-02, decisions the owner delegated during the audit fix run** (the owner may overrule each): a personal or family trust's payment whose purpose cites the holder's service (`TUITION`, `STUDENT ID`; an invoice or PO already escaped) is counted, and a trust payment with no purpose stays held (audit I57; §20, audit fix batch B7); the IRS's tax-refund interest (`IRS TREAS 310` with an `INT` or `INTEREST` entry) is `non_revenue` with the refund, and RBC's provincial label `Prov./Loc.G.Paym Canada` is a provincial benefit, held as `personal_income` (§20, "The GOV follow-ups", audit fix batch B8).
- **2026-10-02, government payments that print no purpose (Q12).** The owner's underwriter ruled that the seven government payments that print no purpose are excluded from revenue (`non_revenue`): `MN STATE MMB`, the VA's `36 TREAS 310 MISC PAY`, Wisconsin DCF's `WIDCF DD`, `PROVINCIAL PAYMENT PROVINCE OF BC`, WSIB, `GOUV QUEBEC MSP` and North Dakota's `WORKFORCE SAFETY` (the owner: "Let's just change to Exclude"; audit I40, GOV class E). A government paying for services with its purpose printed (Medicaid or another health program paying a clinic, a vendor or provider payment, an invoice in the addenda) keeps counting, and so does every form the ruling did not name. §6.1 step 3a and §20 carry it; §17.1 asks whether the program's card settlements (`FIS EBT … WIDCF EBT`, counted) and a Treasury `MISC PAY` with no agency code (Verified) should follow. Audit round 3, R3-B13 (R3-55, §20): a form printed after a digit run glued to its first letter (a glued date, `0102GOUV QUEBEC MSP`) is read too, the VA's Treasury form excepted.
- **2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q13: a processor payout printed as a bare card credit stays excluded.** Asked whether Stripe and Intuit payouts pushed to a debit card should count, and shown only the bare card-credit form (`DEBIT CARD CREDIT: STRIPE`, which reads as a card refund; Relay's layout, the 119 rows and $199K the switch would count), the owner's underwriter answered "keep them excluded" (option 1; audit I11). Such a credit stays `non_revenue`, and `PROCESSOR_CARD_PAYOUT_RELEASE` (§6.3 narrowing 9) stays off; its code stays as the declined option's record, and the Relay fixture's pins stand. The orchestrator reads the same answer onto `CASH_APP_CARD_PUSH_RELEASE` (§6.3 narrowing 6: a Cash App or Apple Cash push printed as a `DEBIT CARD CREDIT` or `POS CREDIT`, the same kind of credit; switched on it would hold 8 rows, $585.17, and move no True), which also stays off; the owner may overrule it. The question did not show a Stripe or Intuit payout that prints its push rail (`VISA DIRECT`: verified at RBC, counted as `p2p` at Bank of America and Woodforest), Wells Fargo's card push (`MONEY TRANSFER AUTHORIZED … FROM INTUIT … CARD`, held) or an instant payment (`INSTANT PMT FROM STRIPE`, verified): each keeps today's reading as the orchestrator's default, and §17.1 asks the owner whether the counted Visa Direct pushes should also be excluded. This closes §17.1's two switches; §20 carries it.
- **2026-10-02, Zelle and no-sender e-Transfers (Q3, Q3b).** The underwriter's answer to Q3 (audit I35), "Let's change to Exclude (not many merchants receive Zelle as payments, if I see that rev came extremely low in comparison to the monthly statement table I can review ...)", clarified as "All Zelle deposits": every Zelle deposit is `non_revenue` (`zelle_excluded`), whoever sent it, a lender or processor paying through Zelle included; a row a non-revenue rule already decided keeps its rule and a direction conflict keeps its hold, and the rules' own reading stays on the record (§8.4, §8.10 step 26). The dashboard's statement of the excluded Zelle total per statement, package and month, and the underwriter's confirm of a single Zelle deposit, landed with R2-OW03 (§9.1, §9.2, §10.1, §10.2, §10.7). Other person-to-person rails stay counted and flagged, and repeated round sums from one sender stay held. Q3b (round-2 R09), "Same rule as Q3": an e-Transfer that prints no sender is held when its round sum repeats in the statement (`p2p_round_repeat_no_sender`), keyed on the amount; its code waits for the owner's word on the one real-statement pin it moves (§17.1). §20 carries both.
- **2026-10-02, lease-to-own and patient-financing payouts (Q8).** The underwriter's answer to Q8 (audit I17), "2 Count it as true revenue, flag it just so i am notified" (option 2: count them as revenue, flagged and never verified, like Affirm and Klarna; keep large one-off lump sums held until sourced): lease-to-own and patient-financing companies paying the merchant (Snap Finance, Koalafi, Acima, Progressive, Katapult, Cherry, Terrace, Wisetack) are counted in True, flagged `customer_financing_payout`, never verified, like OQ2's BNPL settlements; a large one-off lump sum is held as `customer_financing_lump_sum` until sourced; their consumer-side credits and their debits keep their readings (§2.1, §8.9, §20; the defaults the owner may change are at §17.1). Audit round 3, R3-B14 (R3-06, R3-54; §8.1, §8.9, §20): a financier's credit printing a non-sale or financing word (an advance, capital, interest, a dividend or a rebate) is no merchant payout and takes the reading the same row from any other payer takes; a Cherry loan or advance keeps D1 (financing proceeds, its lender-credit exclusion on), as the answer's "Their consumer-side credits (refunds, loans to the holder) stay as today" says; and a cut form of Katapult Engineering's name (`KATAPULT ENG…`) is the namesake, never the lessor.

Its part (c') lands first (audit round 2, R2-OW05): a listed auto lender's credit read on a payables word alone (`PAYABLES`, `TRADE PAY`, `ACCT FUND`) verifies as Q7's dealer funding only on a statement with dealer evidence (§8.7); otherwise it is `lender_paid_for_services`, counted and flagged, never verified, Westlake's PAYABLES to a repossession agency among them (141 credits, $246,412.39, in 4 statements of one agency, leave Verified; True unchanged), and it is held as `financing_named_payer` when the lender also debits the account (the hidden-loan guard, read broadly: a documented over-hold of "collecting loan payments"). Audit round 3, R3-B14 (R3-52; §8.7, §20): the dealer evidence reads an auction purchase only where it is no card purchase, a floor-plan form by its own words (never `FLOORPLANNER` or `FLOOR PLANKS`) and a floor-plan financier's credit only where it prints no service wording, so a row that is no dealer evidence never keeps a repossession agency's payables Verified, and under the hidden-loan guard they are held.
- **2026-10-02, builder progress draws and asset sales (Q11).** The underwriter's answer to Q11 (audits I18, I45), "A) Count as true revenue and flag it  B) Don't count as true revenue and go straight to non-revenue". (a) A builder's progress draw (`ACME BUILDERS DRAW 3`) is counted in True, flagged `construction_progress_draw`, never verified, when the payer is a builder (a builder, homebuilder, construction or contractor name; never a builders' supplier, exchange or insurer), not a lender and not the business's own loan: the lender, own-loan and holder guards run first and any other hold wins; a `DRAW` printed only inside the payer's own name and a Zelle row keep today's reading. A project owner or developer that is no builder stays held (§17.1). (b) A non-dealer's sale of equipment or vehicles (`RITCHIE BROS SELLER PAYOUT`, `CARVANA PAYMENT`, `TRUCK SALE`, a `SALE OF` or `SOLD` purpose, a vehicle's sale even when it cites an invoice) is `non_revenue` (`asset_sale_proceeds`), not held, tagged on its row and named in the Non-Revenue breakdown; a dealer's sales stay revenue when the statement shows dealer evidence (Q7 dealer funding that is not payables-only, a §7.8 auction's payout credit or a dealer-only auction purchase, a floor-plan row, or a vehicle or equipment trade name without a recovery or towing word). The trade-name arm, the absent confirm-dealer path and the invoiced generic equipment are defaults the owner may change (§17.1). §8.1, §8.10 and §20 carry it. Audit round 3, R3-B15 (§20): on a label-less layout the entry's `CONST DRAW` or `CONSTRUCTION DRAW` names no builder, the holder's own builder word is never the payer's and a `DRAW` printed before the builder word is inside the payer's name (R3-08), and a sale printed net of a fee or a commission (`TRUCK SALE FEES WITHHELD`, `LESS COMMISSION TRUCK SALE`) is still a sale (R3-59). Its review round 1 (§20): the entry's own purpose phrase before the builder word (`CONST DRAW <NAME> BUILDERS INC`) is no `DRAW` inside the payer's name, so the builder's draw counts, and a broker's or an agent's `NET COMMISSION` next to the sale is its earned revenue, never what the sale is net of. Its review round 2 (§20): only a phrase that starts the payer region is that entry (a root-less payer's `<NAME> CONST DRAW` before a later builder word stays held), and a commission the netting phrase follows or the fees come out of (`COMMISSION LESS FEES ON TRUCK SALE`, `TRUCK SALE FEES WITHHELD FROM COMMISSION`) is a broker's revenue too.
- **2026-10-02, every insurer spelling (I26, by Q6 of 2026-09-28; not asked in Q2 (2026-10-02)).** Recorded apart from the underwriter's answer to Q2 ("True revenue", which moves money into True; its batch is separate): the Q2 question was not about spelling and the owner was not asked this. Its authority is Q6 of 2026-09-28 ("insurers never count"), which the question's Today line told the owner the tool already applies, and the last sentence of the option the owner picked ("A one-off claim paid to a business on its own policy stays out"), applied however the bank spells the insurer (audit I26). The insurer reading covers every spelling: the `INS` abbreviation, the cut forms `ASSUR`, `MUTUA`, `CASUALT` and `INDEMN`, `ASSURANCES`, `ASSURANT`, `ASSUREUR`, `P AND C` at a name's end, `LOSS PMT`, `SUBRO` and nine carrier brands that print no insurer word, read without the holder's own names. An insurer credit so spelled that nothing else counts is held as `insurer_named_payer`, as the spelled-out form already was; HCCLAIMPMT, healthcare payers and the §15 deferred carriers read as before. Measured on the re-parsed basis (R2-OW07): $146,351.51 out of True (39 rows, 19 statements) and $21,846.85 out of Verified (5 rows, 2 statements), all to Held; of it, the agency commissions and a body shop's repeats (24 rows, $90,498.80) are rows the Q2 card measured its release (a later batch, not yet in the code) counting on a ground, which would leave 15 rows, $55,852.71, on 12 statements out of True by this reading alone, each listed in the batch's owner report. Audit round 3, R3-B13 (R3-11, R3-57, §20): a Texas county mutual (`PROG COUNTY MUT`) is an insurer, never a county government, and a push or instant rail, a named transfer and an ACH entry worded `TRANSFER` read every spelling and brand (only a consumer rail keeps the spelled-out words alone).
- **2026-10-02, insurers paying for the business's work (I27; Q2).** The underwriter's answer to Q2 (audit I27, with I26), "True revenue" (option 2). An insurer's credit is counted and flagged as `insurer_paid_for_services`, never Verified and never toward a Q5 or Q6 repeat, when a holder name shows a repair shop, an insurance agency, a clinic or a pharmacy; or the row prints the form those trades are paid with (`DRP`, an agent's EFT, a commission); or the same insurer pays three or more times within a 31-day span. A one-off claim on the business's own policy stays out as before (a listed insurer's credit `non_revenue`, any other held). `HCCLAIMPMT`, healthcare payers and the §15 deferred carriers read as before. Other insurers' credits in a statement where one insurer qualifies are not counted (owner switch, OFF: `INSURER_FOR_WORK_STATEMENT_ARM`). The insurer reading's every spelling is the separate line above (I26, by Q6 of 2026-09-28), not this answer's (§8.1, §17.1, §20; R2-OW08). Audit round 3, R3-B13 (R3-10, R3-09, §20): a personal benefit's wording (a disability benefit by any name, death, survivor, surrender, cash-value or maturity money; workers' compensation or a plain benefit except at a clinic or a pharmacy) is never paid for work, and on a person-to-person rail one insurer's repeated round sums are held as any sender's (Q3).
- **2026-10-02, Q9: finance-named customers, rent received and lenders paying for services (I16, I36(d)).** The underwriter's answer to Q9, "Keep them as true revenue" (option 2). Counted and flagged, never verified and never toward a Q5 or Q6 repeat: (a) a payer whose name carries a finance word, on a line that prints invoice or vendor-payment wording (`COMMISSION` added by the orchestrator, under Q10 (2026-10-02)) and no debit naming the payer (`finance_named_customer`); (b) a rent `LEASE` when the business is in leasing or property (`lessor_rent`); (c) a lender paying the business for services, as "lender paid for services" (`lender_paid_for_services`), including Westlake's `PAYABLES` to a repossession agency, which leave Q7's verification (part (c'), R2-OW05, the line above). The hidden-loan guard stays, read as any posted debit naming the payer (the bank's receiving fee and a card purchase aside). Recorded limits: payer-less rows stay held; on layouts with no entry label, two roots, or a root after the payer's company form, stay held; a registered lender's vendor-worded credit stays financing proceeds (a §17.1 question). §20's Q9 line carries it (§8.1, §8.7, §8.10; R2-OW09). Audit round 3, R3-B14 (R3-60; §8.1, §20): the lessor's third arm reads rent words outside the payer's own name and never counts an account designation as a rent payer, so one vendor named `… RENTALS` or an own-account transfer printing `RENT` never makes a business a lessor.
- **2026-10-02, premium trust accounts (Q10; audit I39 with I24, I38).** The underwriter: "Lets go with 2. Hold every deposit into an account titled "premium trust". Count only commissions that reach the agency's operating account." Every posted credit of an account whose printed title reads PREMIUM TRUST that a rule verified or counted is held as `premium_trust_account`. Held rows keep their first hold, and non-revenue rows stay non-revenue (the default; §17.1 asks the owner). The agency's operating, producer-payable, wire and other accounts read as before. On the operating account, insurer-worded carrier commissions count through the same day's ruling on the underwriter's Q2 (2026-10-02) (§20, the Q10 and Q2 lines). The title is the statement's own (its printed title, account name or holder name), never a row's payer (§2.1, §8.10, §9.1; R2-OW11).
- **2026-10-02, Q1: wires with no sender (I12).** The underwriter keeps every wire with no sender printed held (`wire_no_sender`, option 1: "Held for review (look at the day $ amount got deposited and see if there is a frequent payment following the deposit)") and asks the review to look at the deposit's day and amount for a frequent payment that follows it. The review item names each lender's daily or weekly payment series that starts after the wire ('possible funding'), read on the Lenders and Potential Lenders tabs only (registry funders, keyword recurrences, D6 payees: a narrowing of "same payee or same amount" chosen on the measured noise of an all-debits pool); it never changes the tier, a figure or a lender row (§2.1, §5.4, §8.5, §10.7, §20; R2-OW12). The defaults the owner may change are at §17.1.
- **2026-10-02, bounced funder payments (Q5; I29).** The underwriter: "Match the return to the funder payment it reverses, take the bounced amount out of "paid to lenders" but keep it in the withholding rate. Keep the funder in the lender count, and show a "returned funder payment" warning" (the amended option 2). A return that reverses a confirmed funder's payment is matched to it (the same amount, 0 to 7 days after, a bounce form; a return naming the funder as classification 5.4's lender side pairs it, on its settlement words). The payment leaves paid to lenders, stays in the withholding numerator and in the lender count, and is shown as a returned funder payment, the warning quoting the bank's words; revenue does not move (§2.1, §6.2, §9, §10.1, §11, §14.3, §20; R2-OW13). The defaults the owner may change are at §17.1.
- **2026-10-02, the withholding basis and cash deposits (Q7; I34).** The underwriter: "2 Make True revenue the default, make cash injections like ATM count as true revenue" (option 2). `true_revenue` is the default withholding basis for the confirmed rate and the potential exposure; legacy eligible deposits and Verified revenue stay selectable through `WITHHOLDING_DENOMINATOR_MODE`, `legacy_eligible_deposits` stays published, and a payload stored with no mode keeps the legacy basis. Cash, ATM, branch and teller deposits count in True, flagged `no_payer_printed`, never Verified (Q2 of 2026-09-28): the corpus check found none held or excluded for being cash, and two cash shapes the reader missed (a retail cash load, inferred from its shape, and a branch deposit printed with its transit) now count (§2.1, §8.2, §10.1, §10.5, §11, §14.3, T8, §20; R2-OW14). The follow-ups are at §17.1.
- **2026-10-02, returns across consecutive statements and chargebacks (Q6; I42).** The underwriter's answer to Q6, "2" (option 2: match a bounced deposit to its original deposit across consecutive months of the same account, within a package and within one statement as today, and count a redeposited check once; flag, but do not deduct, returns that cannot be matched and processor chargebacks). "Consecutive months" is read literally: within a package, a return its own statement cannot pair is matched to the nearest equal deposit in the same account's immediately preceding statement, with no day cap inside that statement, and that deposit leaves the package's True as non-revenue; inside one statement pass 4 keeps its 14 days, and a redeposit after the return counts once. The chargeback line includes a processor's adjustments (`MERCH ADJ`, `FINCL ADJ`, `BANKCD ADJ`) beside its chargebacks: the about $21K the question showed the owner was the two together, so the line says "Processor chargebacks and adjustments" and each flag names its wording. Unmatched returns and chargebacks are flagged on the statement and the package and never deducted. The match is package-only: an analyst's Confirm or Mark beats it, nothing is written back, and a statement viewed alone keeps its own figures (§2.1, §6.2's package passes, §9.1, §9.2, §10.1, §11, §20; R2-OW15). The defaults are at §17.1.
- **2026-10-02, transfers between the business's accounts in a package (Q4; I30).** The underwriter's answer to Q4, "Let's go with option 2 and I'll review it anyways" (option 2: within one deal, match a deposit to an exact-cents transfer out of another of the business's accounts 0 to 2 days earlier, hold it under a named reason and list it so it can be released; never match round sums or person-to-person payments). Within a package, a counted deposit that prints no payer, matched that way, is held as `own_account_transfer_matched` and listed in the package's notice and in Held for Review; a statement viewed alone keeps its own figures. In plain words for the owner: (a) the release is Confirm Revenue, which puts the deposit back into True and marks it Verified, and it counts as your verification: the row turns Verified on its own statement too (a rule never verifies a bare deposit; your Confirm does, as for every held row). (b) Your example also counted twice when both accounts came in ONE PDF, because the tool nets two accounts of one document only when the transfer prints an account designation on the same day ("TRANSFER TO CHK 4821" prints none); that case is now matched too. (c) Only bare deposits are held (a bare, teller, counter or branch deposit): a named payer, a check, a cash or ATM deposit, a round sum or a person-to-person payment is never matched, and on the test set Q4 holds 1 row, $25.00. The First Citizens money of the question (its `TRANSFER INTERNET` credits, about $2.7M) was already held before this ruling, as bare transfers; 8 of those rows ($386,618.63) now show the transfer out they match, and in all 191 already-held rows ($445,033.58) gain that note, nothing about them moving. (d) Q4 cannot check an account whose number was not read, most Chase statements among them (429 of the 528 statements on the test set's package proxies that print no account number): such a statement carries a "not checked" note ("no account number read"), and reading those numbers is a parser follow-up (§17.1). The defaults the owner may change are at §17.1 (§2.1, §6.2's package passes, §8.2, §9.2, §10.1, §10.6, §10.7, §11, §20; R2-OW16).
- **2026-10-06, Zelle as True revenue is a Settings choice (Q3 amended).** The owner, after a second underwriter's view: "One change to zelle payments. I initially asked to exclude all zelle payments but ive sat down with another underwriter and he gave me a really good reason why a zelle payment would be considered true revenue. So this is what i want you to do instead: Create a setting in the settings page that says "Mark Zelle Payments as True Revenue" with yes / no as a check box. If selected yes, as imagined, it should make all zelle payments in the statement count as true revenue. This should also be the default option selected. If the user selected no, as also imagined, count zelle payments into the non-revenue category. The user should only be able to select either or. Not both at the same time." Clarified (AskUserQuestion, "When Yes, should the usual safety checks still apply to Zelle?"): "Keep safety checks (Recommended)", that is: Zelle counts in True revenue, flagged 'Zelle'; like other P2P, Zelle from the business owner's own name and the same round amount repeated by one sender are held for review (releasable); refunds, returns and loan money stay out. Yes (the default): Zelle counts in True revenue, flagged, with the person-to-person holds; No: `zelle_excluded` as ruled on 2026-10-02. Both readings are computed when a statement is analysed and the choice picks one when it is shown, so nothing is reprocessed. §20 carries it.
- **2026-10-06, lender payment changes (the owner's request).** The owner: "can we also detect when a payment to lender has decreased? That would be a really important metric to track." Clarified: "Decreases, increases, stops", "Sustained, 10%+ drop" (the regular payment drops by at least 10% and stays at the new amount for 2 or more payments; one-off short payments do not count; bounced payments are left out of the series), "Confirmed + potential" (potential lenders labelled). The orchestrator's defaults, which the owner may overrule (§17.1): an increase mirrors the decrease; a schedule change is compared on the weekly equivalent and is never by itself a decrease, and a decrease or an increase at a new schedule held 2 payments is shown as a possible change ("new schedule not yet confirmed") until it has run 3 payments (5 if daily); each regime is compared with the last level reported, so steps under 10% that add up are reported; two concurrent positions with one funder are separate series, and a second stream that starts while the first pays is shown as a new stream; a pause that resumes at the same payment is shown; a stop needs 3 or more payments and then no payment, a payment-sized debit or a bounced attempt for longer than the schedule's grace window (5 business days for daily, 6 for an irregular daily rhythm, 10 for weekly, 15 for biweekly or semi-monthly, 25 for monthly), and is only a possible stop inside one statement; information only. §20 carries it.
- **2026-10-07, a returned funder payment its funder re-presents (audit round 3, R3-73; extends Q5 of 2026-10-02).** Asked whether a bounced confirmed-funder payment that the same funder re-presents or catches up should still count in the withholding numerator (Q5 keeps every returned payment there, "the obligation standing", so a re-presented one counted twice), the owner answered "Count it once (Recommended)" (option (b)): a returned payment leaves the withholding numerator once the same funder re-debits it, the same cents off its cycle within one cadence gap after the return, or an exact 2x catch-up within that gap (the catch-up covers the bounced payment once); until such a re-debit exists it stays, as Q5 rules; the returned-funder-payment warning adds "re-presented on <date>" (or "caught up on <date>, 2x"); paid to lenders, the lender count and revenue do not move. Applied inside one statement (§6.2 pass 7c) and across a package's member boundary (the package's pass 5), declared in G7 row by row (`returned_funder_represented`, §14.3). §11, §17.1 default (9) and §20 carry it (audit round 3, R3-B02).
- **2026-10-07, lump-sum payoffs in the withholding rate (audit round 3, R3-79).** Asked whether a confirmed funder's lump-sum payoff, prepayment or buyout should count in the withholding numerator like a recurring payment (every paid funder debit counted, so a payoff raised the published rate as much as a payment of the same size, with no note), the owner answered "Exclude worded payoffs (Recommended)" (option (b)): a CONFIRMED funder's paid debit whose own text prints PAYOFF, PAY OFF, PAY-OFF, PREPAY, PRE-PAY, PREPAYMENT, BUYOUT, BUY OUT or PAYOUT (whole words, read on the debit's own text, never on a credit, a processor's payout credit included) leaves the withholding numerator and stays in paid to lenders and the lender count; the lender table shows an information line per such debit ("Lump-sum payment to <funder>: $X on <date> (<the bank's words>): in paid to lenders, not in the withholding rate."), the copied summaries and the downloads carry it, and the withholding note names the excluded amount. Potential lenders and debits to no funder are unchanged; the shape-only alternative (a one-off of 10x the funder's payment or more after which the series stops) is not built. Declared in G7 row by row (`lump_sum_payoff_excluded`, §14.3). §11, §17.1 and §20 carry it (audit round 3, R3-B03).
- **2026-10-07, a merchant who misses payments then catches up with an exact multiple (audit round 3, R3-25; the lender payment changes of 2026-10-06).** Asked whether a catch-up should get its own line, once an exact 2x to 6x one-off counts as the funder still being paid (a merchant who missed payments and caught up inside the grace window otherwise shows no line at all), the owner answered "Add a 'Caught up' line" (the alternative to the brief's default, no new line): wherever such an exact multiple follows one or more missed scheduled payments of the series' regular amount (business days for a daily schedule, due dates for the others), one amber line, chip "Caught up" (↺; a potential lender's in the neutral tone), "Caught up: no payment to KAPITUS on 2 scheduled daily payments (2054-03-16 to 2054-03-17), then $1,700.00 on 2054-03-18 (2x the daily $850.00)."; one line per event, so a pause or a stop line that still shows for the same gap names the catch-up instead; a multiple with no missed payment before it gets no line. The kind (`catch_up`) is carried wherever the other kinds go: the detection, the package, the statement modal, the copied summaries ("1 catch-up"), the downloads, the CLI and the batch CSV (`lender_payment_catch_ups`), and the lender census's counts. Information only: nothing in paid to lenders, the withholding rate, the counts, revenue or the gate moves. §9.1, §10.1, §10.8, §17.1 (24) (the implementer's defaults inside the answer) and §20 carry it (audit round 3, R3-B05).

The questions still open are at §17.1.

## 20. Implementation amendments (2026-09-29 to 2026-10-06)

The implementation reviews decided these behaviors, which differ from or add to the text above. Each line names the section it amends and the commit(s) that carry it; `docs/transaction-classification.md` ("Review decisions (2026-09-29)") states the same decisions for the code's readers. "A3 review" is the commit that adds this section (418c5f9), "A3 review round 2" is 3dca290, "A3 review round 3" is 851093f, "A3-G" (the redrawn largest-counted stratum's misses) is 1ce3624, "A3-G refinement" is f59db7f, "A3-G review" is a998228, "A3-G re-review" is 75906d2, "A3-G re-review 2" is 35457ff, "A3-G re-review 3" is 66645fe (after b6b5f48, the fixtures' neutral amounts), "A3-H" (the Verified strata's misses at s56c) is bf54caf, "A3-H review" is 6491643 (with 4d1da1b, the registry comment), and "A3-H review 2" the commit that follows it. The final whole-branch review's fix wave (2026-09-30) is 8021847 (the reader fixes), 59c5335 (the lender side and the census) and 69486cb (the webapp); the commit that carries these lines is "FW-4" (1377e3f), and "FW re-review" is the commit that follows it (the re-review of the fix wave). "GOV" is the commit that carries the owner's government-money ruling of 2026-09-30 (the four lines at the end of this section, b1c5918), and "GOV review" is the commit that follows it (the review's fixes, ruled by the coordinator, which amend those lines in place). The lines after GOV's carry an independent audit of the branch (2026-09-30: 62 verified issues, `I01` to `I62`) and its twelve fix batches, "audit fix batch B1" to "B12" (2026-10-01 and 2026-10-02), each line naming its commit(s) and each batch measured from the tree before it; "B12" is the commit that adds its own lines at the end of this section (the contract documents and the final census), which changes no behavior, and "B12 review round 1" the commit that follows it (the review's documentation fixes, no behavior change either). The lines labelled "audit round 2, R2-Bnn" carry the branch's re-audit (2026-10-02: 56 confirmed issues, `R01` to `R56`, 54 of them planned as sixteen fix batches, R2-B01 to R2-B16), each naming its commit(s); each batch is measured against the snapshot of the batch before it on the re-parsed basis that R2-B01 builds. The lines labelled "owner ruling 2026-10-02, R2-OWnn" carry the owner's underwriter's answers of 2026-10-02 to the questions §17.1 left open (§2.1, §19.1), sixteen ruling batches, R2-OW01 to R2-OW16, each naming its commit(s) and measured as the round-2 batches are; none bumps a version (R2-B16's single bump covers the run). The lines labelled "owner ruling 2026-10-06, R2-OW17" carry the owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3 (§2.1, §19.1), measured the same way; it bumps no version either.

- **Glued dates** (§7.0, §6.1 step 9b): a date glued to a row's first word never changes its reading: the revenue text strips it, the channel gate fails closed on a glued or dated prefix, and every card form's boundaries, refusals and required words read through it. 3504281, a5e6f90, 94334b5, 65440df, 8d70ba5.
- **The holder's name is never a payer** (§5.2): the receiver field's value (the holder's name) never names a payer, an operating source or a wire; an incoming wire's beneficiary never names a source. 3bde85e, 58720e6, 213586f.
- **Own-account transfers** (§6.1 step 9, §7.11): a transfer leaves `non_revenue` only on a distinctive payer word; account adjectives stay own-account. a9b4754, 58720e6.
- **Wire vetoes** (§7.9): the vetoes also read a wire glued to its reference and a wire that cites an invoice. a9b4754.
- **The recurrence veto's holder-word exemption** (§7.0) reads only on store-name platforms. 93185ad.
- **Pass 6's counter-debit guard** (§7.5) reads a card purchase's merchant, never its city. 071215a, 151f898. Superseded for card purchases by the final review's line below: pass 6 now leaves a card purchase out.
- **The card-purchase hold rule** (§8.1 `payer_also_debited`): a card purchase at a merchant that shares the payer's word never holds the payer; a card-form debit the classifier names as a lender still counts for `payer_debited_as_lender`. 8cb733b.
- **BNPL consumer credits** (§19 OQ2, §7.11): a buy-now-pay-later return, withdrawal, refund or card credit keeps its 5.4 reading; the OQ2 ruling covers merchant settlements only. 2652ba1, 9f3d954.
- **Direction conflicts** (§6.1 step 2, §7.0, §10.7, T7): a direction conflict is never lifted, grouped, counted or made a repeat by any pass; one an analyst has confirmed or rejected no longer gates the statement's review. 167c83d, 75eae34.
- **Bare transfers** (§8.2): field labels, SEC codes, reference labels and their values, account words and an account description never name a transfer's counterparty; such a transfer is `transfer_no_counterparty`. 167c83d, 213586f.
- **The $1 floor** (§7.0, §7.8, §8.10, §5.3): absolute; a posted credit under $1 is never verified, never counted and never a repeat, whichever rule read it. It is held as `non_sale_purpose` (§5.3's table has no micro-deposit code); one a rule verified is held by pass 7's last step (method `micro_deposit_floor`; marked in place by audit round 3, R3-B15: R3-63, §20 below: every pass-7 demotion leaves a credit under $1 to the floor, the factoring and progress-draw demotions included); a held credit keeps its first hold; a non-revenue credit stays non-revenue. 167c83d, 75eae34.
- **Owner money** (§7.5, §8.1 `non_sale_purpose`): a credit from a brokerage, investing or crypto-exchange platform (the registry's `OWNER_MONEY_PLATFORMS`) or a consumer savings or investing originator is held; `BROKERAGE`, `SECURITIES` and `WEALT…` join the investment words, except on a row that prints §7.5's accounts-payable wording (counted, never verified). 167c83d, 3d6fd9a, 213586f. Amended by audit round 2, R2-B12 (R37, below): the registry's platforms hold no row that prints §7.5's accounts-payable wording (its review round 1: a bare vendor, invoice or payables word spares only `KRAKEN`, `UPHOLD` or `PAXOS` as the row's only platform), and `KRAKEN`, `UPHOLD` or `PAXOS` as the row's only platform holds only outside a customer's trade name; the consumer savings and investing originators are read as before.
- **§15 deferred sources** (§15, §19 OQ4): their payers (the registry's `SECTION_15_DEFERRED_PAYERS`) stay counted and flagged, never verified by Q5 or Q6, never a Q5 or Q6 repeat; on a wire or ACH row their reason is `named_payer_purpose_refused`. 167c83d, 213586f.
- **Rows left to their family** (§7.1, §8.5, §8.6): Q5 and Q6 never verify a row the operating registry names or a NET SETTLE row; a waiting processor's bare word takes no row from them. 167c83d, 213586f.
- **Round-sum repeats** (§8.4): a sender printed without FROM after a person-to-person rail, and a named transfer's counterparty printed without FROM, take the holder test and the round-sum repeat (`p2p_round_repeat`); rail, layout, city and bank words are never a sender. 167c83d, 213586f, ad2c69d, 5997234.
- **VIREMENT** (§8.4, §8.2): a person-to-person rail only in its Interac forms; any other `VIREMENT` is transfer wording. 2309bc1. - **Currency conversion** (§8.1 `non_sale_purpose`): a credit that prints foreign-exchange or currency-conversion wording and names no payer beside it is the holder's own money converted, held; the wording never names a counterparty. The statement's own bank printing its name right before the wording names no payer: its whole normalized name, and the registry's `STATEMENT_BANK_PRINTED_NAMES` forms when the bank field contains one of that entry's bank words (RBC: a bank field containing `ROYAL BANK OF CANADA`, `RBC ROYAL BANK`, the whole word `RBC` or `BANQUE ROYALE` reads `ROYAL`, `RBC`, `ROYAL BANK`, `RBC ROYAL BANK` and the `BANQUE ROYALE` forms; a bare `ROYAL BANK`, as in the Royal Bank of Scotland's name, is no marker). Its credit whose purpose cites the holder's fee (a commission, an origination or broker fee, an invoice, consulting, services rendered) takes its normal reading; the purpose is a wire's OBI, RMR, PMT DET, RFB or URI field (`ORIG FEE` inside one is purpose wording, never an originator label), Santander's REF field (its layout prints `ACCT <n> <originator> REF <purpose>`), an ACH entry or a memo; any other REF field is never read (on the Fedwire layout it is the sender's bank reference; Bank of America's `SERVICE REF` is its own reference). fdbdb2a, A3 review, A3 review round 2.

A join counts only when its two words together spell a financing word (`FINANCIAL`, `FINANCE`, `FINANCING`, `FUND`, `FUNDS`, `FUNDED`, `FUNDING`, `CAPITAL`, `LOAN`, `LOANS`, `LEND`, `LENDER`, `LENDERS`, `LENDING`, `MORTGAGE`, `ADVANCE`, `ADVANCES`, `ACCEPTANCE`, `SERVICING`, `SERVICER`, `LEASING`, `PORTFOLIO`) or a prefix of one of five letters or more, so the join falls inside that word: a line wrap's split (`F INANCIAL`, `SERVICIN G`, `FUN DING`, `LO AN`, `MORT G`: held as `financing_named_payer`). Two words that spell none never make a root (`SERVICE REPAIR`, `SOLO ANALYTICS`, `ROYAL ENDEAVORS`, `ALLEN D`, `HELEN DE`, `GLEN DI`, `CAPT L`, `SERVICE RX` keep their reading). - **A glued CRED** (§8.1 T4): §7.9's word-end `CRED` arm, with a glued letter on its left, read on the payer's name only, as the whole-word `CREDIT` is: a word of the payer name that ends in `CRED` (a credit provider's glued name) holds the credit as `financing_named_payer` when the payer region is a payer's name field (a wire's sender, an ACH originator, a transfer's sender after `FROM`) or prints a company form (`FABRICRED INC EDI PYMNTS`, `ACH CREDIT FABRICRED LLC`).
